day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅 「越後市振の関 （国道8号）」
day_to_day.description: Roadside station on the Niigata–Toyama border, with jade picking on Ichiburi Coast behind it.

activities.name: Renge Onsen Area
activities.name_ja: 蓮華温泉周辺
activities.description: Mountain area around Renge Onsen (1,475 m) in Itoigawa, where Shiroike and the 5 km Renge Forest Nature Trail show autumn colors.

activities.name: Suzawa Seaside Park Auto Campground
activities.name_ja: 須沢臨海公園オートキャンプ場
activities.description: Auto campsite opened in 2016 where Sea of Japan waves can be heard, with golf practice, putter golf, and a 40-metre roller slide.

activities.name: Arasaki Campground
activities.name_ja: 荒崎キャンプ場
activities.description: A lawn tent campground near Marine Dream Nou in Itoigawa, with 32 sites and views of the Sea of Japan.

activities.name: Mount Korenge (Renge Onsen Trailhead)
activities.name_ja: 小蓮華山・蓮華温泉登山口
activities.description: Renge Onsen is the trailhead for Mount Korenge (2,766 m), Niigata’s highest peak, which shares a ridge with Mount Shirouma in Chubu Sangaku National Park.

activities.name: Shirouma-dake Renge Onsen Lodge
activities.name_ja: 白馬岳蓮華温泉ロッジ
activities.description: Natural hot-spring lodge at 1,475 m in Chubu Sangaku National Park, with indoor baths and four open-air baths facing the Northern Alps.

activities.name: Kaganoi Sake Brewery
activities.name_ja: 加賀の井酒造
activities.description: Sake brewery in Itoigawa founded in 1650, Niigata’s oldest, still brewing with its historic well water; tours available.

activities.name: Charmant Hiuchi Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: シャルマン火打スキー場
activities.description: Ski resort.

activities.name: Fudotaki Campground
activities.name_ja: 不動滝キャンプ場
activities.description: Forest campground beside Fudotaki, a 70-metre three-stage waterfall in Itoigawa, with 20 grass tent sites, hiking, and stargazing.

activities.name: Renge Onsen Campground
activities.name_ja: 蓮華温泉キャンプ場
activities.description: Campground in Chubu Sangaku National Park where visitors can hike a two-hour nature trail and relax in Renge Onsen baths.

activities.name: Mount Amakazari (Amakazari Onsen Trailhead)
activities.name_ja: 雨飾山・雨飾温泉登山口
activities.description: Trailhead at Amakazari Onsen for the 1,963 m twin-peaked Mount Amakazari in Joshin'etsu Kogen National Park, one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains.

activities.name: Itoigawa Seaside Valley Ski Area
activities.name_ja: 糸魚川シーサイドバレースキー場
activities.description: Ski area in Itoigawa with courses mainly for beginners and intermediates, sea-facing runs, and a 360-degree summit view of mountains and the winter Sea of Japan.

activities.name: Maple Syrup Tapping and Making Experience
activities.name_en: Maple Syrup Tapping and Making Experience
activities.name_ja: メイプルシロップ採取&シロップ作り体験
activities.description: Snowshoe walk in Itoigawa to tap Itaya maple trees, then boil the sap into maple syrup.

food.name: Echigo Ichiburi no Kan Restaurant
food.name_ja: 越後市振の関 お食事処

food.name: Issaku Itoigawa nunagawa ten
food.name_ja: 一作 糸魚川奴奈川店

food.name: Ramen Shop Itoigawa
food.name_ja: ラーメンショップ 糸魚川店

food.name: Teuchi Soba Kikuemon
food.name_ja: 手打ちそば 菊右ヱ門

food.name: Ramen House Higashiteramachi ten
food.name_ja: ラーメンハウス 東寺町店

food.name: Sun Repass Route 8
food.name_ja: サンレパス ルート8

food.name: Hamayaki no Mise Kobanzame
food.name_ja: 浜焼きの店 小判鮫

food.name: Nakashima Itoigawa
food.name_ja: なかしま 糸魚川店

food.name: Sato Kashiho
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Itoigawa.

sights.name: Jade Coast
sights.description: A coast in Itoigawa covered with colorful stones rather than sand, where visitors can search for natural jade carried down the Hime River.

sights.name: Takanami Pond
sights.description: A 13-metre-deep highland pond at 540 metres in the Hakuba foothills recreation area, with giant-fish sightings, camping, and water activities.

sights.name: Fossa Magna Museum
sights.name_ja: フォッサマグナミュージアム
sights.description: Museum in Itoigawa with six exhibition areas on jade, the Fossa Magna, geological history, natural resources, and disasters such as earthquakes and landslides.

sights.name: Oyashirazu-Koshirazu Coast
sights.description: A coastline famed as a perilous stretch, spanning about 15 km between Omi Station and Ichiburi Station.

sights.name: Gyokusui-en and Tanimura Art Museum
sights.description: Museum of Masahiro Sawada’s wood carvings in a Togo Murano building, beside Gyokusui-en, a 1981 viewing garden with an 8-meter stone Kannon.

sights.name: Benten Rock
sights.description: Benten Rock, an Itoigawa Geopark geosite, is a coastal reef formed by a Fossa Magna submarine eruption and marked by a lighthouse.

sights.name: Kotakigawa Jade Gorge
sights.description: Kotakigawa Jade Gorge is a national natural monument on the Kotaki River, where jadeite is naturally polished by the stream below Mount Myojo.

sights.name: Itoigawa Aranami Anglerfish vs Snow Crab Winter Gourmet Fair
sights.name_en: Itoigawa Aranami Anglerfish vs Snow Crab Winter Gourmet Fair
sights.name_ja: 糸魚川荒波あんこうVS本ズワイガニ冬の二大激ウマグルメフェア
sights.description: Winter food fair at participating Itoigawa restaurants featuring local rough-sea anglerfish and snow crab.

sights.name: Oito Line Extra Bus
sights.description: Extra buses between Itoigawa Station and Hakuba Station accept railway tickets, fill Oito Line gaps, and connect with Hokuriku Shinkansen trains at Itoigawa.

sights.name: Itoigawa Geo Station Geopal
sights.name_ja: 糸魚川ジオステーション ジオパル
sights.description: A promotion base for the Itoigawa Global Geopark under Itoigawa Station, with real trains and large HO and N gauge dioramas you can operate.

sights.name: Amatsu Shrine and Nunagawa Shrine
sights.name_ja: 天津神社・奴奈川神社
sights.description: Amatsu Shrine shares its grounds with Nunagawa Shrine and dedicates bugaku, a national Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, on April 10–11.

sights.name: Hisui-en Garden
sights.description: A stroll garden in Itoigawa centered on a 70-ton cobalt-colored jade boulder, with three waterfalls and ponds, created by Nakane Kinsaku in 1978.

sights.name: Jade Hunting
sights.description: Beach activity in Itoigawa where visitors search pebble shores for jade and other rare stones; exploration kits cost 800 yen.

sights.name: Nou Swimming Beach
sights.description: A sandy swimming beach symbolized by Benten Rock and its red bridge, with clear shallow water inside a breakwater, popular with families.

sights.name: Cheap! Fast! Delicious! Red Snow Crab
sights.name_en: Cheap! Fast! Delicious! Red Snow Crab
sights.name_ja: 安い！早い！うまい！紅ズワイガニ
sights.description: Fresh red snow crab can be bought and eaten on the spot beside Nou fishing port at Marine Dream Nou.

sights.name: Itoigawa Station North Plaza Kitare
sights.name_ja: 糸魚川市駅北広場キターレ
sights.description: A plaza linking Itoigawa Station with the Sea of Japan, with a hall, entrance, three kitchens and dining, plus a workspace and children's play space.

sights.name: Itoigawa Beach
sights.description: Summer swimming beach in Itoigawa, also called Jade Coast because jade is found there, one stop from Itoigawa Station.

sights.name: Live Cafe Hisui no Umi
sights.description: A cafe-attached guesthouse with a shared lounge, free Wi-Fi, rooms with desks and hot-tub bathrooms, and buffet breakfast.

sights.name: Oyashirazu Beach
sights.description: A pebble swimming beach two minutes from Oyashirazu IC, with clear water where fish can be seen, beside a roadside station popular with families.

sights.name: Town Rental Cycles
sights.name_ja: 街なかレンタサイクル
sights.description: Rental bicycles on a roughly 10 km bicycle-only road along the former Hokuriku Main Line, with remaining tunnels, bridges, and Sea of Japan views.

sights.name: Itoigawa Black Yakisoba
sights.name_ja: 糸魚川ブラック焼きそば
sights.description: Squid-ink yakisoba using Niigata squid, with each shop’s own toppings and seasonings, created by Itoigawa restaurants in 2009.

sights.name: no Hakusan Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Itoigawa, Niigata.

sights.name: Momokawa Beach
sights.name_ja: 百川海水浴場（2026年度開設無し）
sights.description: Sandy swimming beach in Itoigawa that will not open in 2026, with rocky reefs including chicken-shaped Tottoko Rock.

sights.name: Yamatogawa Beach
sights.description: Pebble swimming beach in Itoigawa with calm, clear water, a beach hut, and barbecue.

sights.name: Fossil Excavation Experience (Fossa Magna Museum)
sights.name_ja: 3億年前の神秘！化石発掘体験！
sights.description: On the Fossa Magna Museum grounds in Itoigawa, visitors can dig for roughly 300-million-year-old coral and bryozoan fossils and take home up to three.

sights.name: Itoigawa Geo Station Geopal
sights.name_ja: 鉄道好き必見！ジオラマ鉄道模型で運転手になろう！
sights.description: A facility under Itoigawa Station with real trains, models and Plarail, where you can drive a large diorama of Itoigawa’s terrain.

sights.name: Shiroike Forest at the Foot of Mt. Amakazari
sights.name_en: Shiroike Forest at the Foot of Mt. Amakazari
sights.description: Forest at Mt. Amakazari's foot; Shiroike views that peak, one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains, and nearby Mt. Tokura (975 m) is hikable.

sights.name: Nou Fishing Port Daytime Auction Market Tour
sights.name_en: Nou Fishing Port Daytime Auction Market Tour
sights.name_ja: 能生漁港昼セリ市場見学
sights.description: At Nou Fishing Port, visitors can watch a rare daytime fish auction that starts at 3 p.m.

sights.name: Mt. Komagatake Ogamido Trailhead
sights.name_ja: 駒ヶ岳・大神堂登山口
sights.description: Trailhead for the Nechi route up 1,487 m Mt. Komagatake, set among steep cliffs above Umidani Gorge, about three hours to the summit.

sights.name: Shiraike Pond
sights.description: A pond on the way to Renge Onsen with a mirror-like surface, a surrounding path, spring skunk cabbage, and autumn foliage.

sights.name: Jade Bracelet Making at Gyokusuien
sights.name_ja: 日本最古の宝石 “翡翠” のブレスレットを作ろう！！
sights.description: After viewing Gyokusuien and Tanimura Art Museum, make a bracelet at Gyokusuien's jade table using one jade bead with natural stones or crystal.

sights.name: Bibira Beach (Fujisaki)
sights.name_ja: びびら浜（藤崎）海水浴場
sights.description: A long sandy swimming beach with shallow water in the Hokuriku region, opening on 1 July 2026.

sights.name: Oyashirazu Brick Tunnel
sights.name_ja: 100年前のトンネルを歩こう！親不知レンガトンネル
sights.description: Visitors can walk this abandoned, well-preserved Meiji brick tunnel, a civil-engineering heritage site in Oyashirazu, Itoigawa, and view four generations of roads.

sights.name: Daio Hydrangea Garden
sights.description: A private hydrangea garden with about 1,500 plants of 35 varieties and hilltop views of Benten Rock and the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: mûrir
sights.description: Farm restaurant in Itoigawa serving French courses that use rice, with views of the Sea of Japan and Mount Yakeyama.

sights.name: Mount Myojo (Hisui-kyo Trailhead)
sights.name_ja: 明星山・ヒスイ峡登山口
sights.description: The Hisui-kyo route ascends Mount Myojo (1,188 m), an independent peak that shapes the gorge; the summit takes about three and a half hours, with no mountain hut.

sights.name: Miyama Park
sights.description: A park overlooking the Sea of Japan and the Northern Alps, with the Fossa Magna Museum, Chojagahara Archaeological Museum, sports facilities, and 2,000 cherry trees.

sights.name: Umidani Gorge
sights.description: A gorge where the Umikawa River flows past cliffs of Mount Senjo and Mount Koma, known for autumn foliage and called Echigo's Kamikochi.

sights.name: Umidani Sankyo Park
sights.description: A campground at the entrance to Umidani Gorge, near the Mt. Komagatake trailhead, with views of Senjogatake's cliffs and the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Gekkazan Kaneko Azalea Garden
sights.name_ja: 月華山かねこつつじ園
sights.description: Private azalea garden in Itoigawa, where about 3,500 plants cover a hillside and the Sea of Japan is visible from the top.

sights.name: Hiraushi Weeping Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: Weeping cherries in Hiraushi bloom against still-snowy Mount Hiuchi, Mount Yakeyama and Mount Komagatake, and the tree-lined path can be walked.

sights.name: Healing Garden Takanami Campground
sights.name_ja: ヒーリングガーデンたかなみキャンプ場
sights.description: Campground next to Takanami Pond in Itoigawa, with 53 grass tent sites, warm showers, lawns, boating, and stargazing.

sights.name: Omi General Ground
sights.description: About 260 Somei-Yoshino cherries are viewed against remaining snow on Mount Kurohime, with partial night lighting and the Omi viewing event.

sights.name: Mount Kurohime
sights.description: A 1,221 m limestone mountain in Itoigawa, one of Japan's 300 famous mountains, at the northern end of the Hida Mountains.

sights.name: Clubhouse Miyama
sights.description: Multipurpose facility in Itoigawa serving as a telework and remote-work base with power and Wi-Fi.

sights.name: Hisui-kyo Fishing Park
sights.name_ja: ヒスイ峡フィッシングパーク
sights.description: An artificial stream drawn from the river, stocked with char, rainbow trout, and yamame, where beginners can fish and grill their catch on site.

sights.name: Kotakigawa Jade Gorge
sights.name_ja: 大型バスでは行けない“秘境小滝川ヒスイ峡”
sights.description: A national natural monument since 1956 in Kotaki, Itoigawa, this jade-producing riverbed lies where Myojo-yama's limestone cliff meets the Kotaki River.

sights.name: Perennial Snow of Saiguchi
sights.description: Mid-slope snow on Mount Gongen at Saiguchi that stays unmelted in summer and was once used to cool children's fevers and fish.

sights.name: Himekawa Cherry Embankment
sights.description: About 500 Somei-Yoshino cherry trees bloom along 2 km from the Himekawa river mouth, where families picnic.

sights.name: Tokuai Weeping Cherry Trees
sights.description: More than 100 weeping cherries line the road in Tokuai, Itoigawa, on a Japan Scenic Byway in the Itoigawa Global Geopark.

sights.name: Guided Town Walk in Itoigawa
sights.name_ja: ガイドと楽しむまちあるき
sights.description: A Geopark-guided walk in Itoigawa passes Soma Gyofu’s birthplace, the Edo-period Kaga Kaido, and Makino’s handmade candy shop.

sights.name: Jade Cocktail
sights.description: A local Itoigawa cocktail in six varieties, using a jade color and local sake, with a different taste at each participating shop.

stays.name: Hotel Itoigawa Inta
stays.name_ja: ホテル糸魚川インター
stays.description: Hotel in Itoigawa, Niigata.

stays.name: Hotel Route Inn Itoigawa
stays.name_ja: ホテルルートイン糸魚川
stays.description: Hotel in Yoko, Itoigawa with Wi-Fi.

stays.name: Hotel Kunitomi Annex
stays.name_ja: ホテル国富アネックス
stays.description: Hotel in Itoigawa, Niigata.

stays.name: Minshuku Nagomi
stays.name_ja: 民宿 和
stays.description: Family-run minshuku in Uta, Itoigawa with local seafood dinners.

stays.name: Hotel Kunitomi Suisen Kaku
stays.name_ja: ホテル国富翠泉閣
stays.description: Hotel in Taisho, Itoigawa with riverside setting.

stays.name: Sasakura Onsen Ryuun-so
stays.name_ja: 笹倉温泉 龍雲荘
stays.description: Inn at Sasakura Onsen in Ohira, Itoigawa.

stays.name: Oyashirazu Kanko Hotel
stays.name_ja: 親不知観光ホテル
stays.description: Hotel in Ichiburi, Itoigawa with local seafood dinners.

stays.name: Saku Kuchi Onsen Yamashiro-ya
stays.name_ja: 柵口温泉 山城屋
stays.description: Inn at Sakukuchi Onsen in Sakukuchi, Itoigawa.

stays.name: Saku Kuchi Onsen Tsui Gaku-so
stays.name_ja: 柵口温泉 対岳荘
stays.description: Inn at Sakukuchi Onsen in Sakukuchi, Itoigawa.

stays.name: Saku Kuchi Onsen Gongen-so
stays.name_ja: 柵口温泉権現荘
stays.description: Inn at Sakukuchi Onsen in Tamugitaira, Itoigawa.

day_to_day.name: Roadside Station (Echigo Izumozaki Tenryo Village)
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Izumozaki, Niigata.

activities.name: Original Paper Balloon Decorating Experience
activities.name_ja: 世界にひとつ！オリジナル紙風船・飾付け体験
activities.description: Decorate an original paper balloon in Izumozaki, which accounts for over 90 percent of paper balloons made in Japan.

food.name: Drive-in Dosanko Izumozaki Bypass
food.name_ja: ドライブインどさん子 出雲崎バイパス店

food.name: Dai Nigata Country Club Izumozaki Kosu
food.name_en: Dai Nigata Country Club Izumozaki Kosu
food.name_ja: 大新潟カントリークラブ 出雲崎コース

food.name: Gelato Tre Izumozaki
food.name_ja: ジェラート トレ イズモザキ
food.description: Gelato and ice-cream shop in Izumozaki, Niigata.

sights.name: Hamayaki (Charcoal-Grilled Fish)
sights.description: Fish grilled over Uonuma white charcoal, a preserved food from Izumozaki that is also valued as a gift.

sights.name: Ryokan and Sunset Hill Park
sights.description: Hill park beside the Ryokan Memorial Hall in Izumozaki, with a Ryokan statue, poem monuments, and a stone marking a selected Sea of Japan and Sado view.

sights.name: Ryokan Memorial Hall
sights.description: Memorial hall displaying Ryokan's calligraphy, belongings, and documents, with a replica of the Gogo-an hermitage on the grounds.

sights.name: Izumozaki Paper Balloons
sights.description: Paper balloons have been made in Izumozaki since 1919, including decorative crested ibis and penguin designs and custom orders.

sights.name: Ryokan Hall
sights.description: Hall completed in 1922 on Ryokan's birthplace site in Izumozaki, with a stone Jizo he carried, his inscribed poem, and a statue facing Sado.

sights.name: Inohana Beach
sights.description: Wide sandy swimming beach at the north end of Izumozaki, with views of Sado Island and Mount Yahiko.

sights.name: Basho Garden
sights.description: A garden with a carved haiku monument and a Basho statue commemorating the poet’s 1689 stay in Izumozaki on the Narrow Road to the Deep North.

sights.name: Izumozaki Strawberry Farm
sights.description: A farm where visitors can pick and buy Niigata’s Echigo-hime strawberries, then eat them in the rest area or take them home.

sights.name: Tsumairi Streetscape
sights.description: A long streetscape along the Sea of Japan that once thrived as a Hokkoku Kaido post town and port for ships bound for Sado.

sights.name: Fureai no Sato Health and Welfare Center
sights.name_en: Fureai no Sato Health and Welfare Center
sights.name_ja: 保健福祉総合センター ふれあいの里
sights.description: A day-trip hot spring in Izumozaki with baths, assembly halls, Japanese-style rooms, a library, and a cooking classroom.

sights.name: Ryokan Zazo
sights.description: Ryokan in Izumozaki, Niigata.

sights.name: Ryokan and Basho Tour
sights.description: A short guided historical tour of Izumozaki, Ryokan's birthplace and a place Basho wrote about, visiting sites linked to both.

sights.name: Izumozaki Gourmet Town Walk
sights.description: A food event in historic Izumozaki where local restaurants serve seasonal dishes and sake, combinable with town sightseeing.

sights.name: Izumozaki Hometown Storyteller Tour
sights.name_ja: 出雲崎ふるさと語りべ
sights.description: Local guides lead tours of Izumozaki, Ryokan’s birthplace, sharing stories of its Edo-period port town and 4 km coastal tsumairi streetscape.

day_to_day.name: Kitadai Grape Orchard (Direct Sales Only)
day_to_day.name_ja: 北代ぶどう園（直売のみ）
day_to_day.description: Hillside grape orchard in Kitadai, Sanwa, Joetsu, covering 2 hectares and growing more than 15 varieties.

day_to_day.name: Roadside Station Yuki no Furusato Yasuzuka
day_to_day.name_en: Roadside Station Yuki no Furusato Yasuzuka
day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅 「雪のふるさとやすづか」（国道403号）
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Yasuzuka, Joetsu, selling local farm produce, rice, and regional foods, plus gelato, coffee, and stone-milled soba.

day_to_day.name: Yoshikawa Toji no Sato Roadside Station
day_to_day.name_en: Yoshikawa Toji no Sato Roadside Station
day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅よしかわ杜氏の郷
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Yoshikawa with views of Mt. Ogamidake, Mt. Yoneyama and the Myoko mountains, selling local sake and offering brewery tours.

day_to_day.name: Yukidaruma Local Products Shop
day_to_day.name_ja: 雪だるま物産館
day_to_day.description: Direct-sales shop in Yasuzuka selling local vegetables, rice, sake, and snow-room-aged coffee and gelato.

day_to_day.name: Oshima Open-Air Market
day_to_day.name_ja: 大島青空市場
day_to_day.description: A direct-sales market along National Route 253 in Joetsu, selling seasonal wild vegetables, local produce, mushrooms, yams, and Koshihikari rice.

day_to_day.name: JA Echigo Joetsu Uragawara Local Products Hall
day_to_day.name_en: JA Echigo Joetsu Uragawara Local Products Hall
day_to_day.name_ja: JAえちご上越 浦川原物産館
day_to_day.description: Local products hall in Uragawara, Joetsu, selling spring mountain greens, bamboo shoots, local vegetables and handmade foods, with oyaki on Wednesdays from November.

activities.name: Echigo TOKImeki Resort Setsugekka
activities.name_ja: えちごトキめきリゾート雪月花
activities.description: A sightseeing train linking Joetsu-Myoko, Myoko-Kogen, Naoetsu and Itoigawa, where you can enjoy local cuisine amid countryside, mountains and the Sea of Japan.

activities.name: 21st Echigo-Kenshin Sake Festival 2026
activities.name_ja: 第21回越後・謙信SAKEまつり2026
activities.description: A Joetsu event gathering sake, wine, doburoku and local beer to introduce local sake-making culture, with brewery sales and food booths on Takada Honmachi shopping street.

activities.name: Unohama Onsen
activities.name_ja: 鵜の浜温泉
activities.description: Hot spring area along the pine-lined Unohama coast, with Sea of Japan sunsets and Sado Island views on clear days.

activities.name: Ogata Campground
activities.name_ja: 大潟キャンプ場
activities.description: Seaside campsite among pines in Ogata, Joetsu, in a forest-bathing park where waves can be heard, beside a field-athletics course.

activities.name: Yuttari no Sato (Nagamine Onsen)
activities.name_ja: ゆったりの郷（長峰温泉）
activities.description: A natural day-trip hot spring overlooking Mount Ogami and Mount Yoneyama, with Japanese and Western baths, an outdoor bath, and a sauna.

activities.name: Shichifuku no Yu Open-Air Bath (Joetsu)
activities.name_ja: 野天風呂 七福の湯 上越店
activities.description: Sauna in Joetsu with daily löyly sessions in a high-temperature room and monthly sauna events on the 3rd and 17th.

activities.name: Namba Highland Campground
activities.name_ja: 南葉高原キャンプ場
activities.description: Campground on the mid-slope of 949-meter Mt. Namba in Kubiki Prefectural Natural Park, with tent sites, bungalows, and views of the city and Sea of Japan.

activities.name: Unohama Ningyokan (Hot Spring and Pool)
activities.name_ja: 鵜の浜人魚館（温泉とプール）
activities.description: Natural hot-spring baths and heated pools, including a 25-metre pool, where you can watch the sun set over the Sea of Japan.

activities.name: Kanayayama Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 金谷山スキー場
activities.description: Historic ski area known as the birthplace of Japanese skiing, with three courses, a sledding area, and a museum of early ski gear.

activities.name: Itakura-tei Soba Restaurant
activities.name_ja: 体験交流施設 そば処いたくら亭
activities.description: An experience facility and soba restaurant in a private house built in 1923 in Itakura, Joetsu.

activities.name: Kubiki Brewery (Kubiki)
activities.name_ja: 頚城酒造（株）
activities.description: Sake brewery in Kakizaki, Joetsu, brewing Kubiki in small traditional tanks with Niigata rice polished to about 58 percent.

activities.name: Fukuhei Campground
activities.name_ja: 伏兵キャンプ場
activities.description: A mountaintop campground in Joetsu with 30 auto-camp sites, an observation deck, nature trails, and a campfire plaza.

activities.name: Yukidaruma Hot Spring Kubikino
activities.name_ja: ゆきだるま温泉 久比岐野
activities.description: A day-use hot spring expanded from the baths of the inn Onsen no Yado Kubikino, with free-flowing source water near Cupid Valley.

activities.name: Cupid Valley Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: キューピットバレイスキー場
activities.description: Ski resort in Yasuzuka, Joetsu, opened in 1990, with a 4,000-metre course, a kids' park, and ungroomed runs.

activities.name: Takeda Sake Brewery (Katafune)
activities.name_ja: （資）竹田酒造店
activities.description: Sake brewery in Ogata, Joetsu, producing Katafune, a sake with rounded sweetness balanced by dryness, and offering reserved tours from mid-November to February.

activities.name: Musashino Sake Brewery (Ski Masamune)
activities.name_ja: （株）武蔵野酒造
activities.description: Sake brewery in historic Takada, Joetsu, making slightly sweet Ski Masamune, named for Japan’s skiing birthplace, with year-round brewery tours by reservation.

activities.name: Myoko Sake Brewery (Myokosan)
activities.name_ja: 妙高酒造（株）
activities.description: Sake brewery using ultra-soft underground water from Mount Myoko to make smooth, umami-rich sake; tours require prior consultation.

activities.name: Gochi Campground
activities.name_ja: ごちキャンプ場
activities.description: Year-round hilltop campsite in Joetsu that opened in July 2025, on a wide grassland with ocean views and close to city shops and baths.

activities.name: Joetsu Sake Brewery (Echigo Bijin)
activities.name_ja: 上越酒造（株）
activities.description: Sake brewery making clean, soft-drinking sake such as Echigo Bijin and Koshi no Wakatake; tours are available by reservation.

activities.name: Skytopia Yurand Experience Exchange Center
activities.name_ja: スカイトピア遊ランド 体験交流センター
activities.description: Large public bath in a Joetsu lodging and experience facility, with an observation bath containing natural black silica.

activities.name: Joetsu Resort Center Kurumi Kazokuen
activities.name_ja: 上越リゾートセンターくるみ家族園
activities.description: A bathing facility using waste heat from a clean center, with a large bath, sauna, osteopathic clinic, gateball field, and Japanese garden.

food.name: Yukinoka Terrace
food.description: Pudding shop serving snow-room-aged matcha pudding and soft serve made with Niigata Prefecture milk; terrace seats only, open 10:00-18:00, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: CAFE Sweets Nekoji
food.name_ja: かふぇ すいーつねこじ
food.description: Cafe serving crepes, parfaits, SNOW ICE, hot-sandwich lunches from 750 yen, one-plate rice, and hot dogs with Nagomi pork sausage; open 9:30-18:00 (until 19:00 Fri-Sun), closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Yukinoka Terrace Naoetsu
food.name_ja: 雪の香テラス 直江津店
food.description: Cafe serving original sweets made from snow-room-aged tea; open 10:00-18:00, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: Chinese Restaurant Rouran
food.description: Chinese restaurant serving crab omelette, sweet-and-sour pork, chili shrimp and homemade noodles; open 11:00-14:30 and 17:00-21:00, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: Chinese Restaurant Oka Hanten
food.name_ja: 中国料理 王華飯店
food.description: Chinese restaurant using local ingredients, with spring rolls and shumai at 850 yen each and mapo tofu noodle soup at 900 yen; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-22:00, closed Thursdays.

food.name: Tantanmen no Mise Saishin
food.name_ja: たんたん麺の店 菜心
food.description: Tantanmen shop serving Sichuan tantanmen (780 yen), soupless tantanmen (700 yen), creamy tantanmen (850 yen) and fried gyoza (330 yen); open 11:00-14:30 and 17:00-20:30, closed Mondays and other days.

food.name: Italian Restaurant Frutto
food.description: Italian restaurant with pasta and pizza; a lunch set (pasta, pizza or dessert plus appetizer, salad, focaccia and a drink) is 1,620 yen before tax. Lunch 11:00-14:30, dinner 17:30-21:00 or 22:00; closed Tuesday.

food.name: Yuttari no Sato Restaurant Ajisai
food.name_ja: ゆったりの郷 レストラン味彩
food.description: Restaurant serving about 120 Japanese, Western, and Chinese dishes; open 11:00-21:00 (last order 20:15), closed Mondays (next day if a holiday).

food.name: Restaurant Fines Herbes
food.name_ja: レストラン フィーヌ・ゼルブ
food.description: French restaurant in the Chez Toya wedding venue serving lunch sets and dinner courses, with terrace seats and a drink bar; lunch 11:30-15:00, dinner Fri-Sun 17:30-21:00, closed Mondays (Tuesday if Monday is a holiday).

food.name: Restaurant Sepiora
food.name_ja: レストラン セピオーラ
food.description: A hotel chef prepares Western dishes, with lunch at 1,300 yen and dinner courses from 4,400 yen; open 7:00-21:00 (last order 20:30), no closing day.

food.name: Bistro Dezamiantimu
food.name_ja: ビストロ デザミアンティム
food.description: French bistro offering dinner courses and lunch; open 11:30-14:00 and 18:00-22:00, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Restaurant Yodel Kanaya
food.name_ja: レストラン・ヨーデル金谷
food.description: French and casual Western restaurant at the foot of Mt. Kanaya using Joetsu ingredients; open 11:00-21:00, closed Monday evenings and all day Tuesday.

food.name: Art Hotel Joetsu Cafe & Restaurant Allegro
food.name_en: Art Hotel Joetsu Cafe & Restaurant Allegro
food.name_ja: アートホテル上越 カフェ＆レストラン アレーグロ
food.description: Western restaurant and cafe on the first floor of Art Hotel Joetsu; lunch 11:30-14:30 (last order 14:00), dinner 17:00-21:00 by reservation only, no closing days.

food.name: Winery Restaurant Kinseki no Oto
food.name_ja: ワイナリーレストラン 金石の音
food.description: Winery restaurant inside Iwanohara Vineyard; lunch course from 2,500 yen, one-plate lunch from 1,300 yen, dinner course 5,000 yen; open 11:00-16:00, closed Wednesdays.

food.name: Tonari no Kare-ya-san
food.name_ja: となりのカレー屋さん
food.description: Serves curry rice (410 yen), ramen (410 yen), a curry-and-ramen set (570 yen), and tonkatsu katsudon (770 yen); open 11:00-18:00, noodles until 14:00 on weekdays and 15:00 on weekends, closed January 1.

food.name: Restaurant Erisu
food.name_ja: レストラン エリス
food.description: Serves omakase lunch (4,000 or 7,000 yen, 11:30-14:30) and dinner (7,000 or 10,000 yen plus 10% service, 18:00-22:00) in a 110-year-old Joetsu cultural-property building; closed Mondays.

food.name: Satoyama Restaurant Sanwa Well
food.name_ja: 里山レストランさんわwell
food.description: Restaurant in a renovated house in Joetsu's Sanwa district serving set meals of Sanwa rice and local vegetables; lunch 11:30-14:00, dinner 18:00-20:30 by reservation, closed Tue and Wed.

food.name: Gun Chan Naoetsu
food.name_ja: 軍ちゃん 直江津店

food.name: Cafe Dining CoCo
food.description: Serves local sake from the Joetsu and Myoko area, drinking snacks, and meals using Myoko Yashiro Koshihikari and local vegetables; open Mon-Sat 17:30-22:30 and Sun 17:30-21:00, irregular holidays.

food.name: Kutsurogi Izakaya Kanbee
food.name_ja: くつろぎ居酒家 かんべえ
food.description: Izakaya serving creative dishes with seasonal ingredients and drinks; two-hour all-you-can-drink courses with 5 dishes (4,000 yen) or 7 dishes (5,000 yen); open 18:00-2:00, irregular holidays.

food.name: Miraizaka Joetsu Takada Store
food.name_ja: ミライザカ上越高田店
food.description: Izakaya serving Iwate Seiryu Wakadori chicken dishes, including bone-in thigh fried and grilled at 999 yen each (excl. tax); open weekdays 17:00-3:00 and Fri-Sat 17:00-5:00, irregular closures.

food.name: Izakaya Hikozaemon
food.description: Izakaya serving sashimi, ginger pork, tempura, a salmon and ikura donburi and ramen from 880 yen, plus an 8-dish course (5,000 yen with 2-hour all-you-can-drink); open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-24:00, closed Mondays.

food.name: Sake to Meshi Agosuke
food.name_ja: 酒とめし あごすけ
food.description: Serves charcoal-grilled yakitori, salt ago champon (990 yen) and soy-sauce chicken ramen (935 yen); lunch 11:30-14:00, evening 18:00-23:00 (last order 22:00), closed Mondays.

food.name: Seiniku Yakiniku Toyoka
food.name_ja: 精肉・焼肉 とよおか
food.description: Yakiniku (grilled meat) restaurant in Joetsu, Niigata.

food.name: Yakitonya Maruan
food.name_ja: やきとん屋 まるあん
food.description: Yakiton shop with a seven-dish all-you-can-drink course and drink plans; open 17:00-23:00 (last order 22:30), closed Sundays.

food.name: Sumibi Yakitori Toto
food.description: Yakitori restaurant grilling chicken over binchotan; 2-hour all-you-can-drink courses are 4,000 yen (5 dishes) or 5,000 yen (8 dishes); open 17:30-23:00, closed irregularly.

food.name: Nikuzo Yakiniku & Wine
food.description: Yakiniku restaurant with 2-hour all-you-can-drink courses from 5,500 yen (from 3 people) and a 120-minute drinks-only plan from 2,178 yen; open 17:00-23:00, closed on irregular days.

food.name: Sumibi Yakiniku Jaian
food.name_ja: 炭火焼肉 じゃい庵
food.description: Charcoal-grilled yakiniku restaurant serving mainly Japanese Black wagyu in private rooms, with takeout; open 17:00-23:00 (last order 22:00), closed Tuesdays, one Monday a month, and irregular days.

food.name: Hogure Niku Keishu Reservation
food.name_ja: ほぐれ肉 けいしゅう

food.name: Soba Dokoro Itakuratei
food.description: Serves handmade, hand-cut soba made with local flour in a Taisho-era building; salt soba is 900 yen. Weekdays 11:00-14:30, weekends/holidays 11:00-15:00; closed Tuesday.

food.name: Ramen Daiji
food.description: Ramen shop serving Joetsu tonkotsu: a mild pork-bone soup with a soy-sauce tare blending seven soy sauces, including the fish sauce Saigo no Itteki; open 11:00-14:00, closed Mondays.

food.name: Kaiseki Soba Dokoro Amori
food.name_ja: 会席そば処 安茂里
food.description: Serves handmade soba, seasonal Japanese dishes, local fish and local sake; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-21:30 (last order 21:00), closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Tanpopo Ramen
food.description: Ramen shop serving lobster black soy sauce ramen (limited to 20 a day), snow-room sake-lees miso ramen, and tomato cheese noodles; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-20:00, closed Tuesday evenings and Wednesdays.

food.name: Teuchi Ramen Marutoku
food.name_ja: 手打ちらーめん まるとく
food.description: Ramen shop serving handmade high-hydration noodles and chicken white-broth soup, including spicy miso daiginjo ramen (890 yen); open 11:00-14:00 and 17:30-20:30, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Teuchi Ramen Sapporo
food.name_ja: 手打ちらーめん さっぽろ
food.description: Ramen shop serving handmade high-hydration noodles, including miso chashu ramen (950 yen) and vegetable ankake ramen (800 yen); open 11:00-14:00 and 17:30-20:30, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Ramen Haruki
food.description: Ramen restaurant serving high-grade tamari soy sauce ramen (930 yen) and Sea of Japan megi yakiboshi ramen (930 yen, Wednesdays and Saturdays); open 11:00-14:00 until the soup runs out, closed Sundays and Mondays.

food.name: Hana Zen
food.description: Ramen shop serving standard ramen and limited ramen made mainly with local seasonal ingredients; open 11:00-13:30, closed Monday and Tuesday.

food.name: Ramen Shop Fukuhashi ten
food.name_ja: ラーメンショップ 福橋店

food.name: Echigo Tokamachi Kojimaya Jouetsu ten
food.name_ja: 越後十日町 小嶋屋 上越店

food.name: Yukimuro Sobaya Chiisana Sora
food.name_ja: 雪むろそば家 小さな空

food.name: Ramen Shop Oogata ten
food.name_ja: ラーメンショップ 大潟店

food.name: Wagokoro Yukai
food.description: Japanese restaurant serving domestic-beef steak and wappa-meshi, using morning-picked vegetables from its own garden; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-21:00, closed Mondays and other days.

food.name: Eshin Kizawa
food.description: Japanese restaurant in a quiet residential area near the university, serving lunch mini-kaiseki and kaiseki with seasonal local ingredients; open 1:30-13:30 and 18:00-21:00, closed Mondays.

food.name: Shofuen Tosaku
food.description: Seasonal Japanese restaurant with private rooms; lunch from 1,650 yen, evening kaiseki from 3,300 yen, banquet courses with 2-hour drinks from 5,500 yen; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-21:30, closed Mondays.

food.name: Tosaku Bekkan
food.description: Seasonal Japanese restaurant with private rooms; lunch from 1,100 yen, evening kaiseki from 3,300 yen; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-21:30, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Tosaku Koto
food.description: Seasonal Japanese restaurant with private rooms; lunch from 1,100 yen, evening kaiseki from 3,300 yen; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-21:30, closed Mondays.

food.name: Choyokan
food.description: Serves Japan Sea kaiseki in private tatami rooms overlooking a Japanese garden; open 11:30-22:00 (entry until 20:00), closed irregularly plus year-end, New Year, and Obon.

food.name: Shunkashuto Taizo
food.description: Japanese restaurant with all private rooms, serving omakase courses (4,000, 6,000, and 8,000 yen, tax excluded, among others) and sake from around Japan; open 17:00-22:00, closed Sundays.

food.name: Waitaya Shikisai
food.description: Serves original dishes combining Japanese and Italian cuisine; open Mon-Thu 17:00-23:00 and Fri-Sat 17:00-24:00, closed Sunday.

food.name: Art Hotel Joetsu Shunetsu Ryori Myoko
food.name_en: Art Hotel Joetsu Shunetsu Ryori Myoko
food.name_ja: アートホテル上越 旬越料理 妙高
food.description: Japanese restaurant on the 11th floor of Art Hotel Joetsu serving Hanakago Gozen (4,620 yen, tax included) and seasonal kaiseki; open 17:00-21:30, lunch by reservation, closed Sundays.

food.name: Hyakunen Ryotei Ukiyo
food.description: Japanese ryotei in a late-Edo shoin-style building registered as a national tangible cultural property; open 11:30-22:00 (last order 21:00), closed irregularly.

food.name: Tempura Wakasugi
food.description: Tempura restaurant serving freshly fried tempura of local seasonal ingredients, lunch set meals, and takeout tendon and kakiage bowls; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-22:00, closed Sundays.

food.name: Kaiseki Ryori Wasabi
food.description: Private-room kaiseki; seasonal courses from 4,400 yen, two-hour all-you-can-drink plans from 6,600 yen. Lunch 11:30-14:00 by prior reservation; dinner 17:00-22:00 (LO 21:30); closed Sundays unless a banquet is booked.

food.name: Ootoya Joetsu Dainichi-ten
food.name_ja: 大戸屋 上越大日店
food.description: Japanese set-meal restaurant serving a chicken and vegetable black-vinegar set (890 yen) and lunch sets (790 yen); weekdays 11:00-15:00 and 17:00-21:30, weekends and holidays 11:00-21:30, closed January 1.

food.name: Sosaku Washoku Shin
food.description: Creative Japanese restaurant serving seasonal kaiseki and a la carte dishes that change by season; open 17:00-22:00, closed Sunday unless it is a holiday.

food.name: Arurunbatake Noka Restaurant Okagesama
food.name_ja: あるるん畑 農家レストラン おかげさま
food.description: Farm restaurant serving local Koshihikari rice and vegetables, with side dishes at lunch and freshly made soba on Fridays and Saturdays; open 11:00-14:00, closed 31 Dec-3 Jan.

food.name: Okinawa Ryori Haisai Ojisan
food.name_ja: 沖縄料理 ハイサイおじさん
food.description: Okinawan cuisine restaurant serving dishes sourced from the owner's hometown in Okinawa and cooked with Okinawan techniques, open from 17:30 and closed on Sundays.

food.name: Taishu Sakaba Maruchan
food.name_ja: 大衆酒場 まるちゃん

food.name: Issaku Joetsu Inter
food.name_ja: いっさく上越インター店
food.description: Restaurant with 49 private rooms serving about 800 dishes, including fresh seafood such as sashimi and seafood donburi; open 11:00-21:30 Sun-Thu and 11:00-22:30 Fri-Sat, no closing day.

food.name: Sakanaya
food.description: Serves fresh fish and snacks, with lunch and banquet courses; open 11:30-14:00 and 18:00-23:00, closed Tuesdays.

food.name: Shungyo Ryori to Jizake no Mise Daikokuya
food.name_en: Shungyo Ryori to Jizake no Mise Daikokuya
food.name_ja: 旬魚料理と地酒の店 大黒屋
food.description: Serves Japan Sea seafood and seasonal ingredients with 10 or more local sakes; open 11:30-22:00 with no closing days.

food.name: Kappo Kiganso
food.description: Kappo restaurant overlooking Sakata Pond and Mt. Yoneyama, serving carp set meals, eel rice boxes, and takeout handmade soba; open 11:00-22:00 (entry until 19:30), closed Mondays and irregular days, reservations required.

food.name: Marine Hotel Hamanasu Restaurant Kurage
food.name_ja: マリンホテルハマナス レストラン海月
food.description: Restaurant facing the Sea of Japan, serving a seafood bowl (2,200 yen), Hamanasu set meal (1,980 yen), and two-tier seafood box (3,080 yen, tax included); open 11:30-14:00 and 17:30-20:00, closed irregularly.

food.name: Kani Isoryori Echigoya
food.name_ja: かに磯料理 越後家
food.description: Restaurant serving crab course meals with sashimi and tempura, plus local-fish sashimi and lunch sets; open 11:30-14:30 and from 16:30 (last order 20:00), closed irregularly.

food.name: Oshokuji Dokoro Tashichi
food.description: Restaurant serving fish-centered meals; open 11:30-14:00 and 17:00-20:30 (last order 20:00), closed Mondays.

food.name: Oshokuji Dokoro Kisuya
food.description: Serves seafood donburi of Joetsu Koshihikari with sashimi (2,760 yen incl. tax) and Kenshin Shobu-meshi (1,960 yen incl. tax), eaten first as a seafood bowl then with dashi poured on; open 11:00-14:30, closed Mondays.

food.name: Sushi Kappo Ikedaya
food.description: Sushi kappo restaurant; open 11:00-14:00 and 17:00-22:00 (last order 21:30), closed Tuesday.

food.name: Seafood Dining TOMMY SAY
food.name_ja: シーフードダイニング TOMMY SAY
food.description: Seafood dining next to Tomizushi Takada Station store serving seafood dishes, wine and cocktails; open 17:00-24:00, closed Sundays, December 31 and January 1.

food.name: Shiki no Chizakana Ryori Mino
food.name_ja: 四季の地魚料理 美乃
food.description: Local-fish restaurant serving tiger pufferfish, snow crab and eel courses and a budget-matched local-fish omakase; open 16:00-21:00 (last order 20:30), lunch by reservation, irregular holidays.

food.name: Umiterasu Nadachi Seafood Restaurant Umi no Daidokoya
food.name_en: Umiterasu Nadachi Seafood Restaurant Umi no Daidokoya
food.name_ja: うみてらす名立 海鮮レストラン「海のだいどこや」
food.description: Seafood restaurant in a roadside station serving rice bowls and set meals with seafood landed at nearby ports; lunch 11:00-15:00, dinner 17:00-21:00, closed the second Wednesday of each month.

food.name: Kamata Maru Gourmet Ship Joetsu-Myoko Station East Exit
food.name_en: Kamata Maru Gourmet Ship Joetsu-Myoko Station East Exit
food.name_ja: 美食船 かまた丸 上越妙高駅東口

food.name: Nihonichi Umai Tokoroten
food.name_ja: 日本一うまいところてん
food.description: Japanese sweets shop in Joetsu, Niigata.

food.name: Brooklyn Joetsu Store
food.name_ja: ブルックリン 上越店

food.name: Pan Kobo Kurowassan
food.name_ja: パン工房 くろわっさん
food.description: Bakery selling salt-butter pull-apart bread (194 yen), anko croissants (248 yen), and gelato in 16 or more varieties (380 yen); open 10:00-16:00, closed January 1.

food.name: nina
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Joetsu.

food.name: Kanazawa Sohonpo Choeian
food.name_ja: かなざわ総本舗 長栄庵
food.description: Sweets and bakery shop in Joetsu.

sights.name: Kasugayama Castle Ruins
sights.description: Ruins of Uesugi Kenshin's castle, a national historic site listed among Japan's Top 100 Castles, retaining dry moats and earthworks, with sea views from the main bailey.

sights.name: Takada Castle Ruins Park
sights.description: Park on the site of Takada Castle, a Niigata Prefecture historic site, with a restored triple turret, museums, and spring cherry blossoms.

sights.name: Umiterasu Nadachi Roadside Station
sights.description: A roadside station in Nadachi with baths, a hotel, seafood dining, a fresh-fish shop, and summer pools facing the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Myoko Sunshine Land
sights.name_ja: 妙高サンシャインランド
sights.description: An amusement park with a Ferris wheel, camping, barbecue, bicycle rental, and short golf, plus stays at an adjacent hotel.

sights.name: Kubiki Cycling Road
sights.description: A roughly 32 km bicycle and pedestrian path on the former Hokuriku Main Line, with Sea of Japan views and original brick tunnels.

sights.name: Kasugayama Shrine
sights.description: Shrine enshrining Uesugi Kenshin, founded in 1901, with a shinmei-zukuri hall and a memorial museum of his relics.

sights.name: Joetsu City Aquarium Umigatari
sights.name_ja: 上越市立水族博物館 うみがたり
sights.description: Municipal aquarium in Joetsu centered on the local sea and town.

sights.name: Kazamaki Shrine
sights.description: A shrine in Joetsu reached by 114 stone steps between towering cedars, with 200- to 300-year-old Edo-higan cherries at the inner sanctuary.

sights.name: Hikarigahara Highland
sights.description: Highland at 800–1,100 meters at the foot of Mt. Kurokura on the Nagano border, overlooking the Kubiki Plain, with views of Sado and the Noto Peninsula on clear days.

sights.name: Cherry Blossoms around Matsugamine and Mount Myoko
sights.name_en: Cherry Blossoms around Matsugamine and Mount Myoko
sights.name_ja: 松ヶ峯周辺の桜と妙高山
sights.description: About 1,500 cherry trees around Matsugamine contrast with remaining snow, and blossoms and Mount Myoko reflect in Matsugamine Pond.

sights.name: Mount Yoneyama
sights.description: A 992 m peak on the Joetsu–Kashiwazaki border, nicknamed Echigo Fuji and counted among Japan's Three Yakushi, long used as a Sea of Japan navigation landmark.

sights.name: Iwanohara Vineyard
sights.description: Vineyard and winery in Joetsu founded in 1890 by Kawakami Zenbei, known as the father of Japanese wine grapes.

sights.name: Ogami-dake Super Slider
sights.name_ja: 尾神岳スーパースライダー（ボブスレー）
sights.description: Sled course on the mid-slope of Mount Ogami, with a 200-metre tow and a 470-metre run through tunnels and beech forest.

sights.name: Gangi-dori (Covered Walkways)
sights.description: Covered walkways in Takada, Joetsu, formed by extending house eaves over streets to keep winter paths clear in heavy snow.

sights.name: Kota Shrine
sights.description: Engishiki-listed shrine also called Echigo Ichinomiya, known for one-sided reeds linked to Shinran and Kamakura-period wooden guardian dogs.

sights.name: Unohama Beach
sights.description: A wide sandy beach in Joetsu with clear water and hot springs, where sunsets over the Sea of Japan can be seen.

sights.name: Nadachi Seaside Park
sights.name_ja: シーサイドパーク名立
sights.description: A seaside park in Nadachi with a big bobsled, lawns, and views across the Sea of Japan to Sado and the Noto Peninsula.

sights.name: Naoetsu Beach
sights.description: A shallow Sea of Japan beach in Joetsu with a wide sandy shore and parking for about 400 cars.

sights.name: Naoetsu D51 Rail Park
sights.description: Railway theme park at Naoetsu's depot, with a surviving roundhouse, turntable, steam-locomotive rides, and historic railcars open for viewing.

sights.name: Rinsen-ji Temple
sights.description: Temple founded in 1497 where Uesugi Kenshin studied from ages 7 to 14; his grave is in the cemetery.

sights.name: Lord Kenshin's Kachidoki Meal
sights.description: Historical meal based on Uesugi Kenshin's wartime feasts, cooked with period ingredients and methods at designated shops in Joetsu.

sights.name: Tanihama Beach
sights.description: A long Sea of Japan swimming beach in Joetsu, known for good water quality, with clear-day views from Sado Island to Mount Yoneyama.

sights.name: Naoetsu Yatai Hall
sights.description: Hall that stores 18 of 19 Naoetsu Gion Festival neighborhood floats and offers rental rooms plus a free rest area.

sights.name: Kasugayama Castle Historic Site Plaza and Story Hall
sights.name_en: Kasugayama Castle Historic Site Plaza and Story Hall
sights.name_ja: 春日山城史跡広場・春日山城跡ものがたり館
sights.description: Reconstructed earthworks, moats, and buildings let visitors experience medieval Kasugayama Castle; the museum shows Kenshin videos and a battle screen.

sights.name: Jofuku-ji Temple
sights.description: Temple in Kakizaki associated with Shinran, housing a principal Amida Nyorai image in traditional Japanese temple-style grounds.

sights.name: Kakizaki Central Beach
sights.description: A 1,000-metre beach in Joetsu with a 200-metre swimming area, slightly larger sand grains that do not cling, clear water, and sunset views.

sights.name: Joetsu Science Museum
sights.description: Science museum opened in 1984 on human science and snow science, with nine permanent exhibition zones and science events.

sights.name: Takada Sekaikan
sights.description: Historic cinema in Joetsu, opened in 1911, still screening films in a registered cultural-property hall with a wooden-frame ceiling.

sights.name: Takada Castle Three-Story Turret
sights.description: Three-story turret of Takada Castle, rebuilt in 1993 from historical records, with exhibits below and an observation room above.

sights.name: Joetsu City Marine Fishing Center
sights.name_ja: 上越市海洋フィッシングセンター
sights.description: A marine fishing center in Joetsu that will suspend fiscal 2024 operations to review safety and management due to aging facilities.

sights.name: Kanayayama Park
sights.description: Mountain park in Joetsu where Theodor von Lerch first introduced skiing to Japan in 1911, with a memorial hall and bronze statue.

sights.name: Eshin-no-Sato Yasuragiso
sights.name_ja: ゑしんの里やすらぎ荘
sights.description: Day-use hot spring at Omine Onsen, a sodium chloride spring known for heat retention, with local meals and seasonal flowers around the facility.

sights.name: Mount Yoneyama (Mizuno Forest Road Trailhead)
sights.name_ja: 米山・水野林道登山口
sights.description: Intermediate trailhead for 993 m Mount Yoneyama, linked to one of Japan's three great Yakushi, with a hut and about a 90-minute climb.

sights.name: Mermaid Legend Park
sights.description: Seaside park on Ganiko Beach overlooking Sado, with a monument to a local mermaid legend linked to Ogawa Mimei's fairy tale.

sights.name: Nishichi Market
sights.description: A Takada morning market held on days containing 2 or 7, started in 1910 to supply soldiers with fresh vegetables.

sights.name: Funami Park
sights.description: Coastal park in Joetsu developed to restore sandy beaches, where visitors can stroll by the sea in the breeze.

sights.name: Kotagahama (Landing Place of Shinran)
sights.name_ja: 居多ヶ浜（親鸞聖人上陸の地）
sights.description: Landing place of exiled Shinran Shonin, maintained as a park with an observation deck for sunsets over the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Takada Komachi Machiya Exchange Hall
sights.name_ja: 町家交流館 高田小町
sights.description: Restored Meiji-era townhouse, the former Kozumaya, where you can view the atrium and earthen storehouse free of charge.

sights.name: Former Division Commander's Residence
sights.description: Meiji-era Japanese-Western wooden residence built in 1910 for a division commander, restored in 1993 and now also used as a restaurant.

sights.name: Kakizaki Castle Ruins
sights.description: Castle ruins on 25-meter Kizaki Hill, said to have belonged to the Kakizaki clan, senior retainers of the Uesugi in the Sengoku period.

sights.name: Shiku Market
sights.description: Morning market in Omachi, Joetsu, held on days with a 4 or 9, with vegetable and fruit stalls along gangi covered walkways.

sights.name: Oike Ikoi-no-Mori Visitor Center
sights.name_ja: 大池いこいの森ビジターセンター
sights.description: Visitor center in a nature area around Oike and Koike, with trails, camping and an agricultural museum, chosen among Niigata's 100 scenic spots.

sights.name: Gochi History Village Hall
sights.description: Sightseeing base in Joetsu near historic sites, with a souvenir corner, tourist information, a free rest room, and large-bus parking.

sights.name: Gochi Kokubunji Temple
sights.description: Gochi Kokubunji in Naoetsu is said to have been revived by Uesugi Kenshin in 1562 and has a 1997 main hall, three-story pagoda, and Takenouchi Hermitage.

sights.name: Hokkoku Kaido and Kaga Kaido
sights.description: Historic post roads from Oiwake on the Nakasendo to Takada and Izumozaki, used for Sado gold transport and daimyo travel; pine rows remain in Gochi.

sights.name: Joetsu City History Museum
sights.description: History museum in Takada Castle Ruins Park covering Echigo history from the Azuchi-Momoyama period and the Kasugayama, Fukushima and Takada castles.

sights.name: Asahi Pond
sights.description: A 79-hectare lake in Ogata, the largest of five, reflecting Mount Yoneyama and hosting over 3,000 greater white-fronted geese plus about 100 whooper swans in winter.

sights.name: Suruten (Dried Squid Tempura)
sights.name_ja: するてん（するめの天ぷら）
sights.description: Tempura of overnight-dried salted squid, long eaten in Joetsu and available at Takada restaurants and local supermarkets.

sights.name: Sanpachi Market
sights.description: A Naoetsu morning market held on days containing 3 or 8, with vegetable, dried-seafood, and fresh local fish shops.

sights.name: Kasuga Shrine
sights.description: A shrine in Joetsu founded in 958 that enshrines a divided spirit of Nara's Kasuga Taisha and gave Kasugayama Castle its name.

sights.name: Joetsu Kiyosato Star Hometown Hall
sights.name_ja: 上越清里星のふるさと館
sights.description: Astronomy museum beside Lake Bogaike, with a 65 cm reflecting telescope, a 4K planetarium, and the Kushike Meteorite on display.

sights.name: Seaside Park
sights.description: Seaside park next to Joetsu City Aquarium Umigatari, with an octopus-shaped slide, play equipment, and a summer dry-mist fountain.

sights.name: Mount Ogami
sights.description: A 757 m mountain once tied to mountain worship, now known for sky sports, summit views, beech-forest bathing, and a 120-minute climb.

sights.name: Yasuzuka Flower Road
sights.description: Flower plantings along the riverside road, villages, and facilities in Yasuzuka, with seasonal blooms from pansies and daffodils to marigolds, willow-leaf sunflowers, and cosmos.

sights.name: Oike Recreation Forest
sights.description: Nature area around Oike and Koike ponds, listed among Niigata’s 100 scenic spots, with trails, cycling, and equipped campgrounds.

sights.name: Tanihama Park
sights.description: Park in Joetsu with a hill overlooking the Sea of Japan, playground equipment, a barbecue area, and a dog run.

sights.name: Gochi Park
sights.description: Gochi Park in Joetsu has a summit observatory overlooking the Sea of Japan and Kubiki Plain, plus about 700 double-flowered cherry trees.

sights.name: Mount Hishigatake (Hishigatake Green Park Trailhead)
sights.name_ja: 菱ケ岳・菱ケ岳グリーンパーク登山口
sights.description: A 1,129 m mountain called the Eastern Mount Sumeru, with a summit Yakushi Nyorai shrine that doubles as a hut and north-side views of terraced rice fields.

sights.name: Maki Yunosato Miyamaso
sights.description: Hot-spring inn at secluded Utsumata Mineral Spring, with baths overlooking tranquil, expansive scenery and meals of local ingredients and fresh sashimi.

sights.name: Sakaki Shrine
sights.description: Shrine founded in 1876 by Takada domain retainers to enshrine founder Sakakibara Yasumasa; Sorinkan displays the family's heirlooms.

sights.name: Shobu Highland
sights.description: Highland with 10 cottages for seasonal nature, including wild-vegetable picking, fireflies, irises, Japan Sea views, and self-catering with barbecue gear.

sights.name: Torigakubi Cape Lighthouse
sights.description: Lighthouse on an 80-meter hill in Nadachi, Joetsu, lit since 1952, with views of Sado Island, the Noto Peninsula, and Sea of Japan sunsets.

sights.name: Kuwadori Yuttari Village
sights.description: Hot spring lodging facility offering beech-forest walks and meals made with fresh local produce.

sights.name: Arurun Farm
sights.description: Shop in Joetsu offering local vegetables, fruit, rice, miso, pickles, and prepared foods, with monthly farmer events.

sights.name: Nihongi Switchback Station and Cafe Nakagosato Marumu
sights.name_en: Nihongi Switchback Station and Cafe Nakagosato Marumu
sights.name_ja: スイッチバックの駅 えちごトキめき鉄道（株） 二本木駅 喫茶 なかごうさとまるーむ
sights.description: The prefecture’s only switchback station, with a 1910 building and a cafe open daily from 10:00 to 16:00.

sights.name: Yoshikawa Toji no Sato (Tenkeiraku)
sights.description: Sake brewery in Yoshikawa, Joetsu, opened in 1999, using staff-grown rice and offering free brewery tours without reservation.

sights.name: Yukinohako Snow Storage Facility
sights.name_ja: 雪中貯蔵施設ユキノハコ
sights.description: A snow cellar held at 0°C that keeps rice fresh, sweetens vegetables, ages meat, and mellows sake and coffee, with exhibits and a viewing bridge.

sights.name: Ogata Seaside Adventure Course (Ogata Outdoor Activity Facility)
sights.name_en: Ogata Seaside Adventure Course (Ogata Outdoor Activity Facility)
sights.name_ja: 大潟シーサイドアスレチック(大潟野外活動施設)
sights.description: Seaside adventure course beside a campsite where children and adults can play, in a park among Niigata's 100 forest-bathing forests.

sights.name: Sugawara Shrine
sights.description: Shrine founded in 675 enshrining Ame-no-hohi and Sugawara no Michizane, with a keyhole-shaped tumulus and Jomon hearth remains.

sights.name: Rice Terraces (Maki District)
sights.description: Rice terraces in Joetsu’s Maki District, made by reclaiming steep slopes to create more paddies.

sights.name: Joetsu Maizo Bunkazai Center
sights.description: Buried cultural properties center in Joetsu, Niigata.

sights.name: Sakaguchi Memorial Hall
sights.description: Memorial hall in Joetsu for Kinichiro Sakaguchi, known as the sake doctor, displaying his work, brewing songs, and sake-making tools.

sights.name: Region Plaza Joetsu
sights.name_ja: リージョンプラザ上越
sights.description: Multi-use complex in Joetsu with an indoor stadium, skating rink, pool, concert hall, and meeting rooms, beside Joetsu Science Museum.

sights.name: Otate Park (Otate Ruins)
sights.description: Kanto Kanrei residence built by Kenshin for Uesugi Norimasa at the foot of Kasugayama Castle, and later the site of the Otate Rebellion.

sights.name: Ogawa Mimei Literary Museum
sights.description: Literary museum in Joetsu presenting the life and works of novelist and children's author Ogawa Mimei, plus modern literature materials and storytelling events.

sights.name: Japan Ski Origin Memorial Hall
sights.name_ja: 日本スキー発祥記念館
sights.description: Memorial hall in Joetsu marking Japan's first formal ski instruction, given by Major Theodor von Lerch in 1911.

sights.name: SAKURA Plaza
sights.description: Tourist information and local food-and-goods shop facing the Shinkansen ticket gates at Joetsu-Myoko Station.

sights.name: Musee Yukikomachi
sights.description: Cultural exchange facility on the fifth floor of Astopia Takada, a four-minute walk from Takada Station, with galleries and rooms for exhibitions and meetings.

sights.name: Former Imai Dye House
sights.description: This late-Edo dye-shop townhouse, a Joetsu cultural property since 2019, is used to pass on and share local culture.

sights.name: Matsugamine (Cherry Blossoms)
sights.description: About 1,500 cherry trees surround Matsugamine, selected among Niigata’s 100 scenic views, with partial illumination during bloom.

sights.name: Itayama Fudoson
sights.description: A Joetsu City-designated cultural property where Fudo is enshrined in a crescent-shaped water cave with over a hundred stone Buddhas.

sights.name: Kogenji Temple
sights.description: Temple said to have been founded in 1211 by Saishin, a disciple of Shinran; the main hall enshrines a portrait he reportedly drew when pardoned.

sights.name: Ichigo no Hanakotoba (Strawberry Picking)
sights.description: Strawberry-picking place in Joetsu’s Ogata district where visitors harvest Echigo-hime strawberries standing up from February to June.

sights.name: Niigata Prefectural Ogata Water and Forest Park
sights.name_en: Niigata Prefectural Ogata Water and Forest Park
sights.name_ja: 新潟県立大潟水と森公園
sights.description: A park colored by cherry blossoms, hydrangeas and autumn maples, with wildflowers, birds and a fountain lawn popular with children.

sights.name: Mikaburi Castle Ruins
sights.description: Ruins of a 237 m medieval mountain castle, a Kasugayama branch fort, with surviving earthworks and views of the Takada Plain and Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Ichi no Hi Ichi Market
sights.description: Street market in Kakizaki, Joetsu, selling fresh fish, dried goods, vegetables, and fruit along about 70 metres of road closed from the beach entrance.

sights.name: Takada Machikado Exchange Hall (Former Daishi Bank Takada Branch)
sights.name_en: Takada Machikado Exchange Hall (Former Daishi Bank Takada Branch)
sights.name_ja: 高田まちかど交流館（旧第四銀行高田支店）
sights.description: A 1931 reinforced-concrete former bank, designated a Joetsu City cultural property in 2019, with a rentable hall and an exhibition on Takada.

sights.name: Eshin no Sato Memorial Hall
sights.description: A memorial hall in Joetsu's Itakura district about Eshinni, Shinran's wife, with exhibits, local products and views of the Myoko mountains.

sights.name: Building with a Lion Statue (Former Naoetsu Bank)
sights.name_en: Building with a Lion Statue (Former Naoetsu Bank)
sights.name_ja: ライオン像のある館（旧直江津銀行）
sights.description: Former Naoetsu Bank is a pseudo-Western building moved here in 1920, with a lion statue and brick walls recalling Naoetsu’s fires.

sights.name: Echigo Joetsu: Uesugi Kenshin and Kasugayama Castle Exhibition
sights.name_en: Echigo Joetsu: Uesugi Kenshin and Kasugayama Castle Exhibition
sights.name_ja: 越後上越 謙信公と春日山城展
sights.description: A special exhibition on warlord Uesugi Kenshin and Kasugayama Castle, featuring a castle diorama, a life timeline, and touch-panel displays.

sights.name: Mount Ogami Trailhead
sights.name_ja: 尾神岳・尾神岳登山口
sights.description: Beginner trail to 757 m Mount Ogami, once a sacred peak and now known for sky sports, with beech-forest walking and a panorama house.

sights.name: Hasuno Rice Terraces
sights.description: Hasuno Rice Terraces in Oshima, named in 1999 among Japan’s 100 terraced rice fields, with preserved thatched-roof houses.

sights.name: Mushigawa Great Cedar
sights.description: A sacred cedar at Hakusan Shrine, said to be over 1,200 years old, about 30 m tall and 10.6 m in girth, and designated a national natural monument.

sights.name: Mount Ogami Sky Sports Area
sights.name_ja: 尾神岳スカイスポーツエリア
sights.description: Sky sports area on Mount Ogami, long a site of mountain worship, with trails, an observation deck, and paraglider and hang-glider flights.

sights.name: Nigami Firefly Park
sights.description: A firefly park in Nigami, Joetsu, where Genji and Heike fireflies can be seen in early summer among rice fields along the Hokura River.

sights.name: Hayashi Tominaga Residence
sights.description: Thatched residence built in 1883 and still lived in, with a moss dry garden, farmer- and samurai-style rooms, and a preserved hearth; a Joetsu cultural property.

sights.name: Shin-etsu Trail (Oshima District)
sights.description: A 110 km ridge trail in the Sekita Mountains on the Niigata–Nagano border, with trekking from Nonoumi Pass in Oshima.

sights.name: Juge Art Museum
sights.description: A private art museum in Joetsu showing ceramic artist Saburo Saito and painter Takashi Kuraishi, with a garden overlooking rice fields and seasonal flowers.

sights.name: Kamabuta Ruins Guidance Center
sights.description: A guidance center in front of Joetsu-Myoko Station’s west exit, with displays and hands-on learning about the Kamabuta Ruins, a late Yayoi to early Kofun settlement.

sights.name: Nigami Firefly Viewing Platform
sights.description: Volunteer-built viewing spot in Joetsu where firefly larvae glow in a waterway and seasonal instructors explain Genji firefly ecology.

sights.name: Former Kanazu Kentaro Cooperage
sights.description: Late-Edo townhouse in Joetsu preserving a cooper's workshop, hearth and household tools; closed to visitors after the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake.

sights.name: Mount Kirigatake
sights.description: A 507 m mountain in Uragawara, Joetsu, with two trailheads and summit views of the Kubiki Three Mountains and the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Katakai Jomon Museum
sights.description: A museum in Nakago overlooking Mt. Myoko, where visitors can learn about Jomon life near many Jomon sites, including the prefecture-designated Kagomine Site.

sights.name: Nagamine Pond
sights.description: A spring-fed pond from an ancient dune layer, chosen among Niigata's 100 scenic views, with aquatic plants, insects, and a seasonal walking course.

sights.name: Kobayashi Kokei Memorial Art Museum
sights.description: Art museum in Joetsu opened in 2020 for Kobayashi Kokei's works, with his former home, a nationally registered cultural property.

sights.name: Anju and Zushiō Memorial Tower
sights.name_ja: 安寿と厨子王の供養塔
sights.description: Memorial tower for Anju and Zushiōmaru of the Sanshō Dayū legend, relocated in March 1987 during Sekikawa river works.

sights.name: Skytopia Yuuland
sights.name_ja: スカイトピア遊ランド
sights.description: A lodging facility at the foot of Mount Ogamidake with baths, meals, and activity programs, plus paragliding from 650 meters by reservation.

sights.name: Birthplace of Ogawa Mimei
sights.description: Monument marking where Ogawa Mimei, called the father of modern Japanese fairy tales, was born in April 1882.

sights.name: Peace Memorial Park and Exhibition Hall
sights.name_en: Peace Memorial Park and Exhibition Hall
sights.name_ja: 平和記念公園・展示館
sights.description: Park and exhibition hall in Joetsu remembering the Naoetsu POW camp, where 60 of 300 Australian prisoners died.

sights.name: Hitobashira Memorial Hall (Sokushinbutsu)
sights.description: Memorial hall for a monk who became a human pillar to stop landslides; seated remains found in 1937 confirmed the legend.

sights.name: Hosaka Residence
sights.description: Wealthy farmer's residence in Joetsu, including the detached Igan-tei, with delicate interior decoration.

sights.name: Mikuni Kaido
sights.description: Historic road used by Uesugi Kenshin to reach Kanto via Shimizu and Mikuni passes; stone paving seen today is thought to date from the Meiji era.

sights.name: Takahashi Magozaemon Candy Shop
sights.description: Candy shop founded in 1624 along the Hokkoku Kaido, still making awa-ame, okina-ame, and sasa-ame.

sights.name: Campsite
sights.description: Cabin glamping and lawn camping at Cupid Valley, with baths, toilets and climate control in cabins, from 5,500 yen for up to five people.

sights.name: Iwadonosan Myojo-in Temple
sights.description: A Joetsu temple with a cave traditionally linked to Takeminakata’s birth; its Dainichi Nyorai is a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Gozen Shimizu Spring
sights.name_ja: 御前清水（ごぜんしみず）
sights.description: A soft-water spring near the main approach to Kasugayama Castle, former home of Uesugi Kenshin, with a steady flow.

sights.name: Yoya Spring
sights.name_ja: 養爺清水（ようやしみず）
sights.description: A spring Shinran is said to have used daily; a little water still flows, and local residents rebuilt a pavilion.

sights.name: Bogaike Lakeside Park
sights.description: Lakeside park at Bogaike, a pond about 500 meters up, known for a dragon-god legend and a maximum depth of 33 meters.

sights.name: Shin-etsu Trail (Yasuzuka)
sights.description: A 110 km trail along the beech-forested Sekita Mountains ridge on the Niigata–Nagano border, with trekking from Fushino Pass.

sights.name: Echigo Joetsu Uesugi Hospitality Samurai Troupe
sights.name_en: Echigo Joetsu Uesugi Hospitality Samurai Troupe
sights.name_ja: 越後上越上杉おもてなし武将隊
sights.description: A samurai troupe in Joetsu welcomes guests with greetings, martial demonstrations, speeches, and photos, and may visit tour venues on request.

sights.name: Shin-etsu Trail (Itakura)
sights.description: Itakura section of a 110 km ridge trail on the Niigata-Nagano border, with trekking from Sekita Pass at about 1,100 m.

sights.name: Ōma Castle Ruins
sights.description: Mountain-castle ruins built on interlocking ridges and valleys, a Sengoku-period branch of Kasugayama Castle and a Joetsu City historic site.

sights.name: Maejima Memorial Hall
sights.description: Memorial hall in Joetsu honoring Maejima Hisoka, father of Japan's postal service, with about 200 related exhibits.

sights.name: Izumi Jomon Park
sights.description: Izumi Jomon Park in Joetsu is designed after the concentric layouts of Jomon sites and has picnic and barbecue areas.

sights.name: Jōzen-ji Temple
sights.description: Indian pagoda-style temple enshrining the pillow stone Shinran is said to have lain on and the treasure Kawagoe Jūji Myōgō.

sights.name: Iwayado Kannon Hall
sights.description: Kannon hall known as Iwayado.

sights.name: Joetsu City BMX Course
sights.description: BMX course in Joetsu with jumps and berms, able to host All-Japan class competitions.

sights.name: Yokoo Yoshitomo Memorial Hall
sights.description: Memorial hall in an old tax warehouse on Yokoo Yoshitomo’s birthplace, displaying the family tree, paintings, and related items of the former Oguro village head.

sights.name: Kids Ski Tour at Cupid Valley
sights.name_en: Kids Ski Tour at Cupid Valley
sights.description: A day-trip ski tour for beginner elementary pupils in grades 1–4, with transport, meals, and lessons at Cupid Valley.

sights.name: Mushigawa Castle Ruins Park
sights.description: Park at a mountain-castle site whose late Sengoku layout includes a 35-metre main bailey and terraced enclosures.

sights.name: Jōkō-ji Temple
sights.description: Ancient temple founded by Shinran, with a mausoleum housing his skull bone, a National Important Cultural Property main hall, and a paid treasure hall.

sights.name: Shugien Takimoto Residence
sights.description: Wealthy farmer’s residence in Joetsu enclosed by black walls, with a surviving front entrance and a stroll garden of pond, waterfall, arbor, and teahouse.

sights.name: Kokufu Betsuin Temple
sights.description: Kokufu Betsuin is said to be the site of Takegahana Hermitage, where Shinran lived with Eshinni, with an 1805 main hall behind a large ginkgo.

sights.name: Shozenji Dam
sights.description: Shozenji Dam is a multipurpose gravity concrete dam for flood control and water supply in central Joetsu, with about 5,000 hydrangeas along the approach.

sights.name: Kuwadori Citizens' Forest
sights.description: Forest park in Joetsu offering nature observation, forest bathing, and forestry experiences among beech woods, wetlands, and a traditional charcoal kiln.

sights.name: Kobo Shimizu Nature Park
sights.description: A nature park with spring water said to have welled up when Kobo Daishi visited, selected among Niigata Prefecture's 100 famous waters.

sights.name: Kubiki Beef
sights.description: Kubiki beef is raised in Joetsu on local low-pesticide Koshihikari rice straw and won the grand prize at a 2011 competition in Tokyo.

sights.name: Hoshitoge Rice Terrace Walk (Entry Course)
sights.name_ja: 里山を満喫！星峠の棚田ウォーク・エントリーコース
sights.description: A local guide explains regional history while walking some 200 terraced paddies from Hoshitoge to Matsudai Station, about 14 km with 230 m of elevation difference.

sights.name: Shin-etsu Trail (Maki Area)
sights.description: A 110 km ridgeline trail on the Sekita Mountains along the Niigata–Nagano border, with trekking from Maki Pass (970 m) in Joetsu.

sights.name: Naomine Castle Ruins
sights.description: Medieval mountain-castle ruins at 344 m, with dry moats, baileys, a 2 km stone-paved old Mikuni road, and a zelkova said to be 800 years old.

sights.name: Parent-Child Silver Accessory Workshop
sights.name_ja: お子様の絵がアクセサリーに！シルバーアクセサリー親子制作プラン
sights.description: A parent-child workshop in Joetsu that turns a child's flower or animal drawing into a silver pendant or ring to take home the same day.

sights.name: Yamamoto Grape Orchard
sights.description: About 20 farms cultivate and sell grapes across roughly seven hectares on Yamamotoyama hill, with tasting and direct sales overlooking the Takada Plain.

sights.name: Karigane Castle Ruins
sights.description: Mountain-castle ruins at 156 m on the western edge of the Higashi-Kubiki hills, with baileys, dry moats, cut cliffs, and a beacon site said to have signaled Kasugayama.

sights.name: Megisu (Sea Fish)
sights.description: A soft, mild-tasting sea fish, formally nigizu, caught on sandy-mud bottoms 70–200 m off Niigata and eaten locally as fry or tempura in autumn.

sights.name: Maki Furusato Village Nature and Recreation Forest
sights.name_en: Maki Furusato Village Nature and Recreation Forest
sights.name_ja: 牧ふるさと村 自然と憩の森
sights.description: Facility in Maki, Joetsu, with about 100 cherry trees, a relocated thatched headman's house with a waterwheel, and soba-making by reservation.

sights.name: Hijiri no Iwaya (Sacred Cave)
sights.description: A natural rock cave midway on Mount Joroku's north slope, said to be a Shugendo training site of Shinrenbo, overlooking the Kubiki Plain and the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Custom Volume Ring Making
sights.name_ja: お好きなデザインでリング幅のあるボリュームリング制作
sights.description: Make a thick, wide volume ring to your design in Joetsu and take it home the same day.

sights.name: Oshima Village Headman's House
sights.description: A nature-surrounded village headman's house offering rural-life, folk-craft, and snow-country experiences, with overnight lodging.

sights.name: Nigami Fireflies
sights.description: In Nigami, Oshima, a firefly viewing stand and park were built by local volunteers, with an annual festival from early June to early July.

sights.name: Mizushina Burial Mound Group
sights.description: An early 7th-century burial-mound group with corridor-style stone chambers, including small “mini kofun” about 1–1.2 m long and 30 cm wide.

sights.name: Chausuyama Castle Ruins Park
sights.description: Ruins park of Chausuyama Castle, a 42-metre hill in Joetsu that was a subsidiary of Kasugayama Castle and retains a second bailey and an old well.

sights.name: Same-Day Takeaway Silver 925 Pendant Making
sights.name_ja: 当日持帰り可！シルバー925使用のペンダント制作
sights.description: A small-group workshop in Joetsu where beginners make silver 925 pendants with engraved or assembled designs.

sights.name: Global Environment School
sights.description: Experience-based learning facility in western Joetsu where visitors learn about satoyama nature amid terraced fields and charcoal kilns.

sights.name: Sugita Miso Shop
sights.description: Miso shop in Joetsu making carefully prepared miso from Niigata-grown soybeans, with many varieties to choose from.

sights.name: Iwanohara Vineyard Guide Tour
sights.name_ja: 岩の原葡萄園ガイドツアー
sights.description: Guided tour of Iwanohara Vineyard in Joetsu, visiting historic stone wine cellars, a snow room cool in summer, and a Japanese wine tasting shop.

sights.name: Simple Silver 925 Ring Making
sights.name_ja: 当日持ち帰り可！シルバー925使用のシンプルリング制作
sights.description: Make a simple silver 925 ring in Joetsu and take the finished piece home the same day.

sights.name: Kyogatake Castle Ruins
sights.description: Ruins of a medieval mountain castle at 520 meters beside Boga Pond, with nearly intact earthworks, once a branch of Kasugayama Castle.

sights.name: Tokoroten Water
sights.name_ja: トコロテンの水（ところてんのみず）
sights.description: Clear soft spring water from rocky mountains near the Hokura River, used by a tokoroten shop and drawn by visitors for drinking.

sights.name: Kenshin-maru Boat Fishing (Ebisu-ya)

sights.description: Daytime boat fishing on the Kenshin-maru from Naoetsu Port, with a father-and-son crew helping beginners target red sea bream.

sights.name: Nostalgic School and Country Cooking
sights.name_ja: なつかしの学校、なつかしの田舎料理
sights.description: At Tsukikage no Sato, a converted former elementary school, you view old tools and classrooms, then enjoy country cooking from an earlier era.

sights.name: Maki Fureai Experience and Exchange Facility
sights.name_en: Maki Fureai Experience and Exchange Facility
sights.name_ja: 牧ふれあい体験交流施設

sights.name: Yoko Shimizu Spring
sights.description: A maintained spring with a small shrine, said to have supplied drinking water to Utsuo Fort soldiers in the Sengoku period.

sights.name: Maki History and Folklore Museum
sights.description: Folk museum in Maki, Joetsu, themed on the Miyaguchi burial mounds and village life, showing excavated items plus materials on glass and petroleum.

sights.name: Tandem Paragliding Scenic Flight
sights.name_ja: パラグライダー二人乗り遊覧飛行
sights.description: A tandem paragliding flight with an instructor over Ogami-dake needs no special strength and lets you look down on a wide panorama.

sights.name: Welcome to Nadachi: Stay and Fresh Fish Selection Kaiseki Plan

sights.name: Kasugayama Castle Guided Tour

sights.description: Volunteer guides lead a walking tour of Kasugayama Castle ruins, Uesugi Kenshin’s former home, covering fortifications and retainers’ living areas.

sights.name: Kamabuta Ruins Guidance Facility

sights.name_ja: 加茂川を泳ぐ鯉のぼり
sights.description: From mid-April to early May, about 500 koinobori fly above the Kamo River in an annual display begun in 1989.

sights.name: Ōmi Shrine
sights.description: Guardian shrine of Kamo on Mount Kamo, about 1,300 years old, known for its nightingale corridor and a May 21 festival procession.

sights.name: Awagadake Prefectural Recreation Area
sights.description: Recreation area with a 27-site campground, hiking and climbing trails, a visitor center, nature observation forest, and charcoal-making beside a reservoir.

sights.name: Kamo City Folk Museum
sights.description: Folk museum in Kamo City.

sights.name: Gejogawa Dam
sights.description: Dam green space in Kamo for nature study and recreation, with gardens, camping, fishing, and cherry blossoms in late April and early May.

sights.name: Fuyutorigoe Ski Garden
sights.name_ja: 冬鳥越スキーガーデン
sights.description: Family ski area in Kamo with gentle slopes, a sled-only course, three T-bar lifts, and wooden railcar Moha 1 on site.

sights.name: Awagadake Central Climbing Trail
sights.description: Central trail on 1,293 m Awagadake, one of Japan’s 300 famous mountains, with clear-day views of Sado Island and Noto.

sights.name: Gejogawa Dam Green Space
sights.description: A dam green space busy with crucian carp anglers, where 700 cherry trees bloom along a 3.8 km circuit road in mid-April.

sights.name: Gejogawa Dam
sights.description: Dam recreation area with a 10-site campground, nature learning center, dragonfly and wetland gardens, a suspension bridge, and crucian carp fishing.

sights.name: Seiuntei Yamashige
sights.description: Machiya-style restaurant in Kamo where guests dine in a quiet space of traditional Japanese atmosphere.

sights.name_ja: いいオフィス加茂 by 小柳建設
sights.description: Coworking space at Oyanagi Construction in Kamo, also operating as Microsoft Base Niigata-Kamo, with local cafe and bakery pop-ups.

sights.name: Masukagami
sights.description: Sake brewery in Kamo, founded in 1892, using Awagadake water and polishing rice to 60% or less even for regular sake.

sights.name: Gejogawa Dam
sights.description: A dam lake area for nature education and recreation, with a fishing deck, campsite, wetland garden, and nature learning center.

sights.name: Kamo Folding Screen Workshop
sights.name_ja: 加茂の伝統工芸 屏風の製作現場を見学
sights.description: Visitors can watch folding screens made from wood and washi in Kamo and assemble a kumiko coaster to take home.

sights.name: Kamo Kiri Tansu

sights.name: Nagase Shrine
sights.description: Shrine overlooking the Kamo River in Hachiman, Kamo, where a rare hexagonal mikoshi is paraded on June 15.

sights.name_ja: 冬鳥越スキーガーデン（多目的広場）
sights.description: Year-round plaza that is a grass field from spring to autumn and a family ski slope in winter, displaying historic railcars and a flower clock.

sights.name: Awagadake Prefectural Recreation Area
sights.description: Prefectural recreation area at the foot of Mount Awagadake, with a campground, visitor center, and a water source reflecting the mountain in every season.

sights.name: Kamo-jima (Striped Cotton Fabric)
sights.description: Cotton cloth woven in Kamo since the late Edo period, valued for indigo insect resistance and durability as farmers' workwear.

sights.name: Joraku-ji Temple
