sights.name: Shoun Sanso Japanese Garden
sights.description: A Japanese garden built in 1926 as a private villa in Kashiwazaki, with pines, azaleas, about 300 maples, a pond, and a drum bridge.

sights.name: Niigata Prefectural Kashiwazaki Aqua Park
sights.name_ja: 新潟県立柏崎アクアパーク
sights.description: Leisure facility in Kashiwazaki with a year-round pool, an indoor 50-meter pool in summer, and an ice rink in winter.

sights.name: Kamomegahana Observation Deck (Lovers' Cape)
sights.description: An observation deck in Kashiwazaki with views of Mt. Yoneyama, Yoneyama Bridge, Sado, and Mt. Yahiko, also known as Lovers' Cape.

sights.name: Kujiranami Beach
sights.description: A sandy beach in Kashiwazaki, about 440 meters long, selected as one of Japan's 100 Best Beaches.

sights.name: Mount Yoneyama
sights.description: A 992-meter mountain on the Kashiwazaki–Joetsu border offering 360-degree views, with the Sea of Japan to the northwest.

sights.name: Ishiji Beach
sights.description: A roughly 1 km shallow beach in Kashiwazaki with clear water, changing rooms and showers, and views of Sado Island.

sights.name: Sea Use Raion
sights.description: A workation stay in Kashiwazaki facing the Sea of Japan, with Mount Yoneyama behind and the open sea in front.

sights.name: Sauna Horizon
sights.name_ja: サウナ宝来洲（ホライズン）
sights.description: An outdoor sauna in Kashiwazaki with a sea-view wood-stove room, a groundwater cold pool, and a rooftop air bath.

sights.name: Niigata Prefectural Children's Nature Kingdom
sights.name_ja: 新潟県立こども自然王国
sights.description: A large prefectural children's center combining play, learning, and lodging, with outdoor playgrounds, a library, indoor halls, and a natural hot spring.

sights.name: Oumigawa Beach
sights.description: A pebble-and-sand beach just below JR Oumigawa Station, known as the station closest to the sea, with a small river mouth nearby.

sights.name: Banjin and Nishi-Banjin Beach
sights.name_ja: 番神・西番神海水浴場
sights.description: A wide sandy beach with rocky shallows in Kashiwazaki, marked by a red torii, where Nichiren landed after pardon from exile on Sado.

sights.name: Yumi (Kashiwazaki Port Tourism Exchange Center)
sights.name_ja: 柏崎港観光交流センター「夕海」
sights.description: A sea station at Kashiwazaki Port selling local sweets, processed seafood and original desserts, with a cafe serving coffee and Chinese dishes.

sights.name: Oizumi Tera
sights.description: Temple in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

sights.name: Yonahime Shrine
sights.description: A Kashiwazaki shrine known for prayers for safe childbirth, traditionally linked to the birth of Minamoto no Yoshitsune’s son.

sights.name: Kashiwazaki Central Beach
sights.description: The swimming beach closest to central Kashiwazaki, near a domed seaside park and Kashiwazaki Aqua Park.

sights.name: Ban Kami Do
sights.description: Sightseeing spot in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

sights.name: Enma Hall
sights.description: A Kashiwazaki hall associated with the Enma Market (June 14–16); the present storehouse-style building was built in 1896.

sights.name: Swans at Nagamine Oike
sights.description: Nagamine Oike in Kashiwazaki hosts over 400 wintering whooper and tundra swans, with paths for close viewing and feeding using food visitors bring.

sights.name: Kamiwa Beach
sights.description: Beach in Kamiwa, Kashiwazaki, with nearby parking and views of the Kamiwa and Yonahime arch bridges on National Route 8.

sights.name: Shiawase Monaka (Niigata Anko Sweets)
sights.name_ja: 新潟素材のあんこを楽しむ「しあわせ最中」
sights.description: At a Kashiwazaki sweet shop, guests combine four Niigata anko types, ice cream, and freshly boiled shiratama on heart-shaped monaka.

sights.name: Takahama Beach
sights.description: A long, shallow sandy beach in Kashiwazaki spanning Ominato, Miyagawa, and Shiya, where surfing is allowed.

sights.name: Akasakayama Park
sights.description: A 13.7-hectare red-pine hill park in Kashiwazaki with streams, play areas, lawns, and views of the city and the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Tata Shrine Main Hall
sights.description: Main hall of Tata Shrine, built in 1519 and sheltered by a covering hall, retaining mid-Muromachi shrine architecture.

sights.name: Kasashima Beach
sights.description: A small fishing-town beach with low waves, near the Chubu-Hokuriku Nature Trail and the rare Ushigakubi Formation fold.

sights.name: Higashinowa Beach
sights.description: A wide sandy beach beside Kashiwazaki Marina and a seaside park, with beach houses and parking.

sights.name: Mount Hachikoku
sights.description: A 518-meter mountain group on the Kashiwazaki–Nagaoka border, with spring wildflowers and waterfalls including Fudo, Byobu, and Jusanga Falls.

sights.name: Osaki Yukawariso Village
sights.description: About 30,000 hepatica bloom in early March on a hill overlooking the Sea of Japan, while Echigo’s mountains remain under deep snow.

sights.name: Joganen Garden
sights.description: A moss garden in Takayanagi, Kashiwazaki, designated a national Place of Scenic Beauty in 1937, with a tea house and bridges over its pond.

sights.name: Iizuka Residence (Shukoen Garden and Imperial Lodging)
sights.name_en: Iizuka Residence (Shukoen Garden and Imperial Lodging)
sights.name_ja: 飯塚邸（秋幸苑と行在所）
sights.description: Former residence of the Iizuka landowning family in Kashiwazaki, where Emperor Showa stayed in 1947 and named the garden Shukoen.

sights.name: Echigo Yukiwariso Road Smartphone Stamp Rally 2026
sights.name_en: Echigo Yukiwariso Road Smartphone Stamp Rally 2026
sights.name_ja: えちご雪割草街道スマホでスタンプラリー2026
sights.description: A smartphone stamp rally linking four hepatica flower sites in Kashiwazaki and Nagaoka with nearby hot springs and dining facilities.

sights.name: Fukura Hakkei
sights.description: Sightseeing spot in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

sights.name: Nishi-Kujiranami Beach
sights.description: A small inlet beach behind Kujiranami fishing port, down a slope from the inn district, with few visitors.

sights.name: Ushigakubi Intraformational Fold
sights.description: A rare intraformational fold in Kashiwazaki’s Nishiyama Formation, with irregularly bent central layers formed by a submarine landslide about five million years ago.

sights.name: In Utero (Whole-House Rental Inn with Sauna)
sights.name_en: In Utero (Whole-House Rental Inn with Sauna)
sights.name_ja: サウナ付き一棟貸し旅籠 In Utero
sights.description: A whole-house farmhouse inn quietly set in the mountains, with an earthbag sauna where guests can pour their own löyly.

sights.name: Tanine Dam
sights.description: Water source pond in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

sights.name: Kashiwazaki Yume-no-Mori Park
sights.description: A nature park with wide meadows, forest and a large pond, offering picnics, crayfish fishing, sledding and a waterside of more than 30,000 irises.

sights.name: Teishin-ni
sights.description: Historic site and cultural property in Kashiwazaki.

sights.name: Yakushido Beach
sights.description: A beach just after the JR Shinetsu Main Line overpass from Route 8, with a rocky center and sandy shores on both sides.

sights.name: Ōsaki Beach
sights.description: A shallow family swimming beach in Kashiwazaki with clear water, one beach hut, toilets, and a nearby day-trip hot spring.

sights.name: Ukawa Shrine no Oga Yaki
sights.description: Sightseeing spot in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

sights.name: Oginoshima Thatched-Roof Village
sights.description: A rare circular settlement where houses encircle rice fields, drawing sketchers and photographers through the seasons, with sweet crops grown using mountain spring water.

sights.name: Kashiwazaki City Museum
sights.description: Museum in Akasayama Park explaining Kashiwazaki’s history, culture, and nature, with a planetarium for stargazing.

sights.name: Anko Jam
sights.name_ja: 気軽に楽しめる良質な味わい「あんこジャム」
sights.description: A smooth sweet-bean-paste spread made without artificial colors or flavors, for bread, ice cream, or yogurt.

sights.name: Chigo-no-Ie (Folk Toy Museum)
sights.description: Museum in Kashiwazaki displaying about 50,000 folk toys and folk crafts from across Japan.

sights.name: Anju-ji Temple
sights.description: A Soto Zen temple in Kashiwazaki that enshrines Mokujiki Shonin's Thirty-three Kannon statues, including the Hibomo Kannon.

sights.name: Kariwa Kurohime Mountain
sights.description: An 891-meter mountain with beech forest and Ukawa Shrine at the summit, suited to beginner hikes from Kashiwazaki between May and November.

sights.name: Zenkon Fudo Falls
sights.description: A three-tier waterfall over 72 meters high in Kashiwazaki, long worshipped as a Fudo Myoo falls, with a stone statue in a cave by the basin.

sights.name: Sabaishigawa Dam
sights.description: A dam operating since 1974 for flood control and irrigation, with a lakeside campground, sports ground, and 200 cherry trees.

sights.name: Irohaya Seianjo (Dango and Anko Dessert)
sights.name_ja: 柔らかいお団子にあんこを絡めて召し上がる和のデザート
sights.description: Canned Japanese dessert from Kashiwazaki anko shop Irohaya Seianjo, with soft dango and Hokkaido azuki paste cooked in a copper pot.

sights.name: Juo Hall
sights.description: Hall in Kashiwazaki with Mokujiki Buddha statues of Enma and the Ten Kings, and a Binzuru figure rubbed shiny by residents.

sights.name: Takayanagi District, Kashiwazaki
sights.description: A mountain-surrounded, nature-rich area where many fireflies can be viewed over rice fields and streams in early summer, along with thatched-roof circular settlements.

sights.name: Nagahama Beach
sights.description: A shallow sandy beach with clean water in Kashiwazaki, near an area for marine sports such as windsurfing.

sights.name: Osaki Yukiwariso Marche
sights.description: Market at Osaki Yukawariso no Sato selling local sweets, sea-bream bento, and Arahama baked sweet potatoes beside Niigata’s designated hepatica.

sights.name: Doitsuan Indigo Folk Craft Museum
sights.description: Kashiwazaki museum of indigo-dyed goods and everyday utensils from late Edo to Meiji, collected by Matsuda Masahide.

sights.name: Yoneyama Beach
sights.description: A beach directly below Hijirigahana, one of the Yoneyama Fukuura Eight Views, near the former Tawaraya inn where Basho stayed.

sights.name: Kimura Tea Ceremony Museum (Tea Ceremony Experience)
sights.name_en: Kimura Tea Ceremony Museum (Tea Ceremony Experience)
sights.name_ja: 木村茶道美術館 お茶席体験
sights.description: Tea-ceremony museum inside the Shoun Sanso garden in Kashiwazaki, where visitors can experience a tea gathering.

sights.name: Kashiwazaki Civic Activity Center Machikara
sights.name_ja: かしわざき市民活動センターまちから
sights.description: Civic activity center in Kashiwazaki where groups use the building freely and exchange ideas, with some rooms available for paid exclusive use.

sights.name: Dogtooth Violets on Mount Takauchi
sights.description: Dogtooth violets bloom along walking paths on Mount Takauchi, a former castle-site mountain in Kashiwazaki.

sights.name: Hanasaka Rice Terraces
sights.description: Terraced paddies leveled on a slope, with forest left on the ridgelines and canals carrying water from reservoirs.

sights.name: Kashiwazaki Central Beach
sights.name_ja: かしわざきセントラルビーチ
sights.description: Camping and barbecue area in Minatomachi Seaside Park on Kashiwazaki’s coast, with swimming, marine sports, nearby shops, and a day-bath facility.

sights.name: Kadode Thatched-Roof Village
sights.description: Thatched-roof folk-house lodging in Takayanagi with two buildings, where guests share handmade country meals around a sunken hearth.

sights.name: Marine Sports Exchange Center
sights.name_ja: マリンスポーツ交流センター
sights.description: A hub facility that shares information on manners and rules for enjoying marine sports safely, and is open in summer only.

sights.name: 404 Not Found
sights.description: Listing not found.

sights.name: Tainoko-jirushi Fish-Roe Shiokara
sights.name_ja: 鯛の子印 魚卵塩辛
sights.description: Cod roe is salted and fermented into shiokara, then aged for over a year by traditional methods in Kashiwazaki.

sights.name: Ukawa District, Kashiwazaki
sights.description: Fireflies can be seen over rice paddies in early summer in Ukawa, a clear-stream satoyama area and home of the Ayako-mai dance.

sights.name: Nashinokida Rice Terraces
sights.description: Rice terraces at the source of the Kurohime River, covering 9 hectares near wild plants, a campsite, and beech forest.

sights.name: An-an (Cream Shiratama Anmitsu)
sights.name_ja: 手作りにこだわった優しい味「クリーム白玉あんみつ」
sights.description: An-an, a Kashiwazaki sweet shop run by Irohaya Seiansho, serves made-to-order cream shiratama anmitsu with homemade bean paste, agar, and black sugar syrup.

sights.name: Kashiwazaki Marina
sights.description: Marina in Kashiwazaki with 57 berths and storage for 210 small boats, set between Kujiranami and Tonowa beaches.

sights.name: Ayako-mai Hall
sights.description: Hall in Onadani, Kashiwazaki, introducing Ayako-mai, a folk art passed down for about 500 years and designated a national Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 1976.

sights.name: Obiraki Rice Terraces
sights.description: Rice terraces in Kashiwazaki with diamond-shaped plots covering 12 hectares, where fireflies can be seen in the irrigation canals in season.

sights.name: Kurofune Museum
sights.description: Museum in Kashiwazaki showing late-Edo and Meiji Restoration crafts, broadsheets from around Perry's arrival, glassware, pottery, and prints and oils by Sumio Kawakami.

sights.name: Donald Keene Center Kashiwazaki
sights.name_ja: ドナルド・キーン・センター柏崎 「私は日本文学の素晴らしさを伝えたい」
sights.description: Center in Kashiwazaki on scholar Donald Keene’s life, research, and writer friendships, with a restored New York study where you can sit on his sofa.

sights.name: Kashiwazaki Sightseeing Volunteer Guides
sights.name_ja: かしわざき観光ボランティアガイドが、まちの魅力をご紹介します！
sights.description: Volunteer guides lead visits to Kashiwazaki historic sites, alleys, terrain, and calming gardens.

sights.name: Kasashima Town Walk Plan
sights.name_ja: まち歩き後のコーヒー付き！笠島まち歩きプラン
sights.description: A town walk in Kasashima between the sea and mountains, passing 120-year-old railway remains and the Hokkoku Kaido, then local ego and coffee.

sights.name: Niigata Sake Tasting Experience with Guinomi
sights.name_en: Niigata Sake Tasting Experience with Guinomi
sights.name_ja: 本場の新潟で利き酒師から学ぶ、日本酒試飲体験！ぐいのみ付き
sights.description: Taste Niigata-only and rare seasonal sake while the proprietress explains each one, and take home the snake-eye cup used.

sights.name: Kadoide Washi Koshi no Kigami Workshop
sights.name_en: Kadoide Washi Koshi no Kigami Workshop
sights.name_ja: 門出和紙 高志の生紙工房
sights.description: A Kadoide washi workshop where snow-bleached handmade paper is made, offering reserved experiences in traditional papermaking and coaster making.

sights.name: Sake Taster's Talk Plan with Scenic Views
sights.name_en: Sake Taster's Talk Plan with Scenic Views
sights.name_ja: 利き酒師の酒談義（＋絶景付）で日本酒通になろうプラン
sights.description: A sake-taster talk with conversation tips and brewery-hanten photos, then sake selection and tasting overlooking the Sea of Japan and Omigawa Station.

sights.name: Banjin Beach Fun Diving
sights.name_ja: のんびり朝8時集合！柏崎・番神ビーチでファンダイビング
sights.description: A relaxed 8 a.m. fun-diving tour from Banjin Beach in Kashiwazaki, with two beach-entry dives among sand, rocks, seaweed, nudibranchs, and seahorses.

sights.name: Living Kuro Yokan
sights.name_ja: 空気に触れ熟成していく生きている「くろ羊かん」
sights.description: Kuro yokan made since 1894 with Okinawan black sugar, Hokkaido azuki beans and thread agar, cut and packaged to age in the air.

sights.name: Ajiroyaki Rice Crackers
sights.name_ja: 工業米菓の礎を築いた明治生まれのおせんべい、名物「網代焼（あじろやき）」
sights.description: Senbei devised in 1907 by Shintaro Niino, made with rice and fragrant shrimp powder and finished with soy sauce.

sights.name: Autumn Echigo Garden Tour (Relaxed Foliage and Local Cuisine Course)
sights.name_en: Autumn Echigo Garden Tour (Relaxed Foliage and Local Cuisine Course)
sights.name_ja: 錦秋の越後庭園めぐり 紅葉と海山の幸ゆったり満喫コース
sights.description: A one-night, two-day model course visiting gardens in Kashiwazaki, Nagaoka and Yahiko, combining a relaxed itinerary, sea-and-mountain cuisine and a sake-brewery visit.

sights.name: Kofuku Arare (Cocoon-Shaped Rice Crackers)
sights.name_ja: ふっくら甘いまゆ玉、幸せ色の「幸福あられ」
sights.description: Cocoon-shaped rice crackers devised in the late Meiji period, made from Niigata glutinous rice and seasoned with mild white soy sauce.

stays.name: Umibe no Yado Naniwa-ya Yunagi-tei
stays.name_ja: 海辺の宿 浪花屋 夕凪亭
stays.description: Inn in Geiha, Kashiwazaki with scenic views and local seafood dinners.

stays.name: Hotel Alpha-One Kashiwazaki
stays.name_ja: ホテル・アルファ－ワン柏崎
stays.description: Hotel in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

stays.name: Hotel New Green Kashiwazaki
stays.name_ja: ホテル ニューグリーン柏崎
stays.description: Hotel in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

stays.name: Shore View Inn Sea Youth Raion
stays.name_en: Shore View Inn Sea Youth Raion
stays.name_ja: 渚の見える宿 シーユース雷音
stays.description: Inn in Nishiko, Kashiwazaki with a large communal bath.

stays.name: Hotel Route Inn Koto Kashiwazaki
stays.name_ja: ホテルルートインコート柏崎
stays.description: Hotel in Hiyoshi, Kashiwazaki with Wi-Fi.

stays.name: Tabist Business Hotel Chitose Kashiwazaki
stays.name_ja: Tabist ビジネスホテルちとせ 柏崎
stays.description: Hotel in Hiyoshi, Kashiwazaki with parking and business travelers.

stays.name: Hotel Eriawan Ban Kami Misaki
stays.name_ja: ホテルエリアワン番神岬
stays.description: Hotel in Kashiwazaki with scenic views and a large communal bath.

stays.name: Ryokan Daiya
stays.name_ja: 旅館 大家
stays.description: Ryokan in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

stays.name: Tabist Kotake-ya Ryokan Kashiwazaki
stays.name_ja: Tabist 小竹屋旅館 柏崎
stays.description: Ryokan inn in Geiha, Kashiwazaki with a sauna.

stays.name: Oku no Yu Yumotokan
stays.name_ja: 奥の湯 湯元館
stays.description: Lodging in Kashiwazaki, Niigata.

stays.name: Jonnobi Onsen Takayanagi Jonnobi Mura
stays.name_ja: じょんのび温泉 高柳じょんのび村
stays.description: Inn at Jonnobi Onsen in Takayanagi, Kashiwazaki with kaiseki dinners.

stays.name: Nigataken Ritsu Kodomo Shizen Okoku
stays.name_ja: 新潟県立こども自然王国
stays.description: Inn in Takayanagi, Kashiwazaki with family-friendly stays.

day_to_day.name: Minamiuonuma Roadside Station (Yukiakari)
day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅 南魚沼「雪あかり」（国道17号）
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Minamiuonuma selling local Koshihikari and vegetables, with a light-meal counter, a park, and an art hall displaying Munakata Shikō works.

day_to_day.name: Minamiuonuma Roadside Station Yukiakari
day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅南魚沼「雪あかり」と周辺観光
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Minamiuonuma with a morning farm-direct vegetable shop, a local-ingredient restaurant, art displays, and a seasonal play park.

activities.name: Mount Makihata Foothills Campground
activities.name_ja: 巻機山麓キャンプ場
activities.description: Campground at the foot of Mount Makihata, known for wild birds and alpine plants, with 40 tent sites and hiking.

activities.name: Uenohara Campground
activities.name_ja: 上の原キャンプ場
activities.description: Lawn campsite in Uenohara Park on Muikamachi’s Uonuma hills, near iris gardens, with fishing and a footbath at Omatsu Pond.

activities.name: Grape Harvest and Wine Festival
activities.name_ja: ぶどう収穫祭とワインまつり
activities.description: Grape-harvest festival at Agri-Core Echigo Winery in Yairo no Mori Park, with limited wines, food stalls, and outdoor concerts.

activities.name: Muikamachi Hot Springs
activities.name_ja: 六日町温泉
activities.description: A hot-spring area in Muikamachi found when springs gushed during natural-gas test drilling in 1957, designated a national recreational hot-spring area in 1964.

activities.name: Hatsukaishi Onsen Ishiuchi Jung Palnas
activities.name_ja: ハツカ石温泉 石打ユングパルナス
activities.description: Day-trip hot spring next to Ishiuchi Maruyama Ski Resort, with a large bath, open-air bath, salt sauna and medicinal-herb bath.

activities.name: Hakkaisan Ropeway (Sea of Clouds Viewing) / Muikamachi Hakkaisan Ski Resort
activities.name_en: Hakkaisan Ropeway (Sea of Clouds Viewing) / Muikamachi Hakkaisan Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 雲海鑑賞ロープウェー
activities.description: An 81-passenger ropeway with open aerial views, hiking access to Mt. Hakkai, and early runs for sea-of-clouds viewing.

activities.name: Osaki Dam Park Campground
activities.name_ja: 大崎ダム公園キャンプ場
activities.description: Campground in a community park at the foot of Mt. Hakkai, beside Osaki Hakkaizan Son Shrine, with seasonal walks around the dam lake.

activities.name: Uonuma Chrysanthemum Exhibition (Urasa Chrysanthemum Festival)
activities.name_ja: 魚沼菊花展 浦佐菊まつり
activities.description: About 1,000 pots of chrysanthemums, tended for a year by growers from across the region, are exhibited and judged at Fukōji Temple in Urasa.

activities.name: Urasa Hot Springs
activities.name_ja: 浦佐温泉
activities.description: A simple hot-spring area west of Urasa Station, surrounded by Echigo Sanzan and the Uonuma Hills, and known as a climbing base.

activities.name: Ishiuchi Maruyama Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 石打丸山スキー場
activities.description: Ski resort opened in 1949 and linked to GALA Yuzawa and Yuzawa Kogen, with natural snow, varied terrain, and snow glamping.

activities.name: Ikazawa Campground
activities.name_ja: 五十沢キャンプ場
activities.description: Campsite in Minamiuonuma with tent and auto sites, cottages, a fishing pond, and a forestry experience hall.

activities.name: Maiko Onsen Iishi-no-Yu
activities.name_ja: 舞子温泉 飯士の湯
activities.description: Day-trip hot spring about two minutes from Shiozawa-Ishiuchi IC, with an onsite simple spring, Uonuma cuisine, disc golf, camping and glamping.

activities.name: Maiko Snow Resort
activities.name_ja: 舞子スノーリゾート
activities.description: Ski resort one minute from the Shiozawa-Ishiuchi interchange, with 26 runs, a six-person gondola, a snow park, and an on-site hotel.

activities.name: Cold Ascetic Training and Setsubun Festival
activities.name_en: Cold Ascetic Training and Setsubun Festival
activities.name_ja: 寒修行・節分祭
activities.description: Setsubun bean-throwing event in Osaki, Minamiuonuma, linked to seven-day cold ascetic training at Fudo Falls that the public may join by application.

activities.name: Itsukamachi Amaike Educational Green Campground
activities.name_ja: 五日町天池教育グリーンキャンプ場
activities.description: Summer campground at Itsukamachi Ski Area with tent sites, birdwatching, and views of Mount Hakkai and Mount Makihata.

activities.name: Chateau Shiozawa Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: シャトー塩沢スキー場
activities.description: Ski resort in Minamiuonuma with Ipponsugi and Yoshisato slopes and seven runs, 70 percent of them for beginners.

activities.name: Joetsu Kokusai Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 上越国際スキー場
activities.description: Ski resort in Minamiuonuma with four zones and 22 runs for all levels, plus a kids' snow play area and Saturday fireworks.

activities.name: Kabanosawa Hot Spring
activities.name_ja: 樺野沢温泉（かばんさわおんせん）
activities.description: A sodium-calcium chloride hot spring in Minamiuonuma, at 47°C, with day-trip bathing at Joetsu Kokusai Ski Resort's Annex.

activities.name: Osawayama Hot Spring
activities.name_ja: 大沢山温泉
activities.description: A quiet hot spring surrounded by mountains in Minamiuonuma, said to have opened in 1630, with clear, smooth water good for the skin.

activities.name: Muikamachi Hakkaisan Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 六日町八海山スキー場
activities.description: Ski area in Minamiuonuma reached by a 2.2 km ropeway, with 11 courses and three pair lifts.

activities.name: Hakkaisanroku Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 八海山麓スキー場
activities.description: Ski resort with 10 varied runs, a family sled slope, snowboarding on all courses, and elevation from 210 to 420 meters.

activities.name: Muika Snow Resort
activities.name_ja: ムイカスノーリゾート
activities.description: Ski resort in Minamiuonuma with 20 courses, four lifts, a kids' park, and direct access to Muika Onsen Hotel.

activities.name: Yamato City Ski Area Junior Ski Class
activities.name_en: Yamato City Ski Area Junior Ski Class
activities.name_ja: 大和市スキー場 ジュニア・スキー教室
activities.description: Junior ski lessons for elementary and junior-high students at Hakkaisanroku Ski Area in Minamiuonuma, for residents near Yamato City.

activities.name: Itsukamachi Ski Resort
activities.name_ja: 五日町スキー場
activities.description: Ski resort in Minamiuonuma with 10 runs, night skiing, four lifts, and slopes from 160 to 510 meters.

activities.name: Uonuma Rice Planting Experience
activities.name_ja: 自分の手でお米を作る！日本有数の米処、新潟県魚沼で田植え体験
activities.description: Hands-on rice planting with Koshihikari seedlings in Uonuma, open from elementary-school age, with Uonuma Koshihikari rice as a souvenir.

activities.name: Kimono Experience: Bokushi-dori Stroll in Shiozawa-juku
activities.name_en: Kimono Experience: Bokushi-dori Stroll in Shiozawa-juku
activities.name_ja: 着物体験 ～三国街道塩沢宿「牧之通り」散策～
activities.description: In Minamiuonuma, wear Honshiozawa or Shiozawa tsumugi kimono and walk historic Bokushi Street in Shiozawa-juku.

activities.name: Vegetable Harvest and Specialty Farmer Rice Purchase Experience
activities.name_en: Vegetable Harvest and Specialty Farmer Rice Purchase Experience
activities.name_ja: 野菜収穫体験とこだわり農家お米買付体験
activities.description: Visitors harvest seasonal vegetables at Kawanaga Farm in Minamiuonuma and can buy Koshihikari rice while talking with the growers; winter offers include mochi pounding and amazake.

activities.name: Snowmobile Experience at Maiko Snow Resort
activities.name_en: Snowmobile Experience at Maiko Snow Resort
activities.name_ja: スノーモービル体験
activities.description: Snowmobile courses at Maiko Snow Resort let visitors drive 120cc to 200cc machines across the snow after a briefing, with no special driving permit required.

activities.name: Traditional Mochi-Pounding Experience in Uonuma
activities.name_ja: 「お米のまち」魚沼ならでは！昔懐かし餅つき体験
activities.description: Pound freshly cooked glutinous rice in a large mortar, then eat one serving—the size of three cut pieces—in one of three flavors around a hearth.

activities.name: Snow Banana Boat at Maiko Snow Resort
activities.name_en: Snow Banana Boat at Maiko Snow Resort
activities.name_ja: 雪上バナナボート
activities.description: A snowmobile-towed banana boat runs a dedicated course at Maiko Snow Resort, separate from the ski and snowboard slopes.

activities.name: Uenohara Highland Hot Spring
activities.name_ja: 上の原高原温泉
activities.description: Highland hot-spring area in Minamiuonuma, opened in 1992 and used year-round for training camps and hot-spring cures.

activities.name: Maiko Snow Resort Course
activities.name_ja: 白銀のゲレンデをお散歩！舞子スノーリゾートコース
activities.description: Snowshoe walk on snow-covered ski slopes, including making snow sliders and exploring a treehouse in the forest.

activities.name: Gojitsujo Drum
activities.name_ja: 御実城太鼓
activities.description: Said to be the battle drum of Sakado Castle's Ueda group, which directed the Uesugi army and was granted the vanguard.

activities.name: Minamiuonuma Hot Spring Village
activities.name_ja: 南魚沼温泉郷
activities.description: Hot-spring area in Minamiuonuma with scenic baths, inn meals, autumn foliage, winter sports, and snow-viewing baths in winter.

sights.name: Minamiuonuma Maji-don (Rice Bowl Campaign)
sights.description: A food campaign in which local restaurants and sushi shops serve 54 large rice bowls made with Minamiuonuma Koshihikari.

sights.name: Hakkaisan Ropeway and Observation Deck
sights.name_ja: 八海山ロープウェー・八海山展望台
sights.description: Ropeway on Mt. Hakkai, one of the Echigo Sanzan, leading to an observation deck with clear-day views of mountains, the Sea of Japan, and Sado Island.

sights.name: Shiozawa-juku Bokushi-dori (Mikuni Kaido)
sights.name_ja: 三国街道 塩沢宿 牧之通り
sights.description: Historic street in Minamiuonuma recreating the Edo-period Shiozawa post town and its snow-country covered walkways, named after writer Suzuki Bokushi.

sights.name: Uonuma no Sato
sights.description: A rural complex in Nagamori, Minamiuonuma, with a cafe, shops, a snow storehouse, and a soba restaurant, facing Mount Hakkai.

sights.name: Hakkai Shrine
sights.description: Shrine encircled by cedars planted in 1836, where paired trunks symbolize marital harmony and visitors pray for safe childbirth.

sights.name: Mount Hakkai
sights.description: A 1,778 m sacred mountain and symbol of Muikamachi, with three climbing routes and summit scenes used in the 2009 drama Tenchijin.

sights.name: Mount Makihata (Shimizu Trailhead)
sights.description: Shimizu trailhead for 1,967 m Mount Makihata, with two routes; the recommended Ido Ridge takes about five hours to a summit hut.

sights.name: Ishigami Shrine
sights.description: A shrine founded as the guardian deity of Sōtō temple Hōrin-ji, whose coffered ceiling displays 69 works donated by Yokoyama Taikan, Yamamoto Isoroku and others.

sights.name: Tsumugi-dori Light Truck Market
sights.description: A pedestrian market on Tsumugi-dori in front of Shiozawa Station, where light-truck vendors sell local produce, food, clothing, antiques, and crafts.

sights.name: Raiden-sama's Water
sights.name_ja: 雷電様の水（らいでんさまのみず）
sights.description: Water that wells up in several cascades from a huge rock at the foot of Mount Katsura, at 400 tons a day, and is used for tap water and sake.

sights.name: Uono no Sato (Local Food Complex)
sights.description: Uono no Sato has four areas for fresh fish, souvenirs, Echigo sake, and Uonuma cuisine, plus sweets such as sasa-dango soft serve and Uonuma yaki manju.

sights.name: The Veranda Ishiuchi Maruyama
sights.name_ja: ザ・ヴェランダ石打丸山
sights.description: Viewpoint opened in 2022 at Ishiuchi Maruyama Ski Resort, with a terrace overlooking Minamiuonuma rice fields and Mt. Makihata.

sights.name: Ryūkoku-ji Temple
sights.description: White-walled temple housing a Hawaii-donated Kannon and eleven-faced Kannon, with openwork transoms by Ishikawa Unchō and a neighboring hall of 120 Buddha statues.

sights.name: Hakkaisan Son Shrine
sights.description: Hakkaisan Son Shrine's village shrine, built in 1979, enshrines Mount Hakkai and has an 8.5-metre granite torii.

sights.name: Kankō-ji Temple
sights.description: Rinzai Zen temple in Minamiuonuma known for miso said to bring blessings after Uesugi-donated sutras were buried in it and survived a fire.

sights.name: Agricore Echigo Winery
sights.name_ja: アグリコア越後ワイナリー
sights.description: Winery offering snow-cellar tours, paid wine tasting, and a restaurant overlooking the vineyards.

sights.name: Untō-an Temple
sights.description: Sōtō Zen temple in Minamiuonuma, over 1,200 years old, whose 1707 main hall is a prefectural cultural property and whose treasure hall shows Uesugi and Takeda letters.

sights.name: Uramakihata Gorge
sights.description: A 6 km gorge on the north face of Mount Makihata, formed by the Isazawa River, with cliff walls, waterfalls, and a trail in a prefectural conservation area.

sights.name: Uonuma Skyline
sights.name_ja: 魚沼スカイライン（南魚沼市）
sights.description: An about 20 km ridge drive on the Minamiuonuma–Tokamachi border, with five lookouts over Uonuma’s mountains and basin and Tsumari’s river terraces; closed in winter.

sights.name: Imaizumi Memorial Hall Art Station
sights.name_ja: 今泉記念館アートステーション
sights.description: Art gallery in Minamiuonuma overlooking Mount Makihata, with about 40 of 144 Munakata Shiko works on permanent display.

sights.name: Noborikawa River Park
sights.description: River park with a 6.8-kilometre walking path for barbecues and outdoor activities.

sights.name: Mount Sakado
sights.description: Mountain in Minamiuonuma, Niigata.

sights.name: Bishamondo (Kisshozan Fukoji Temple)
sights.name_ja: 毘沙門堂（吉祥山普光寺）
sights.description: Hall enshrining Bishamonten, built about 1,200 years ago by Sakanoue no Tamuramaro and venue of the Hadaka Oshiai festival.

sights.name: Sakado Castle Ruins
sights.description: Castle ruins that were the Ueda Nagao clan's base in the Nanboku-chō period and later a Uesugi garrison guarding the Kantō approach.

sights.name: Yasuo Toyama Nonohana Gallery
sights.name_ja: 外山康雄 野の花館
sights.description: A gallery in a renovated old folk house that displays paintings of often-overlooked flowers.

sights.name: Minamiuonuma Rafting
sights.description: Rafters descend about 11 km of a river that stays high even in midsummer, over roughly two and a half hours, with a 6 m rock jump and cave exploration.

sights.name: Mikuni Kaido Shiozawa-juku Warrior Doll Displays
sights.name_en: Mikuni Kaido Shiozawa-juku Warrior Doll Displays
sights.name_ja: 三国街道塩沢宿武者人形かざり
sights.description: About 20 shops on Bokushi-dori in Shiozawa-juku show Meiji-to-Heisei warrior dolls and kimekomi dolls of local Shiozawa cloth.

sights.name: Osaki Takiya Spring
sights.name_ja: 大崎滝谷の水（おおさきたきやのみず）
sights.description: Spring water from the Uonuma range, drawn from a basin at Omae Shrine on Route 291 and used to grow Osaki greens in winter.

sights.name: Mikuni Kaido Shiozawa-juku Hina Snow-Viewing Decorations
sights.name_en: Mikuni Kaido Shiozawa-juku Hina Snow-Viewing Decorations
sights.name_ja: 三国街道塩沢宿ひな雪見かざり
sights.description: Since 2006, shops and homes around Shiozawa-juku's Bokushi Street display rare hina dolls from the Edo through Heisei periods, including Echigo-jofu kimekomi dolls.

sights.name: Mount Hakkai Observation Deck
sights.description: Observation deck on Mount Hakkai.

sights.name: Tomioka White Art Museum
sights.name_ja: 南魚沼市トミオカホワイト美術館
sights.description: Japan's only museum exhibiting and housing about 500 works by Soichiro Tomioka, internationally known for painting snow country.

sights.name: Mount Sakado (Sakado Trailhead)
sights.description: Sakado trailhead for 634 m Mount Sakado, a beginner hike of about one hour to the summit, with three routes and no hut.

sights.name: Yairo Forest Park
sights.description: Park on green Yairohara overlooking the Echigo Sanzan, with lawns, play equipment, and walking paths near the Uono and Mizunashi rivers.

sights.name: Mount Tango
sights.description: A 1,809-meter mountain in Minamiuonuma, about six hours on foot from the Jujikyo trailhead.

sights.name: Zenibuchi Park
sights.description: A Japanese-style garden park at the foot of Mount Sakado, with seasonal flowers, cherry trees, skunk cabbage, and walking paths.

sights.name: Uonuma Skyline Hakka Overlook
sights.name_ja: 魚沼スカイライン八箇見晴台
sights.description: Viewing platform on the Uonuma Skyline, a roughly 20 km mountain drive from Hakka Pass to Juni Pass, with views of Mount Hakkai on clear days.

sights.name: Shiki Ajiwai-kan (Produce and Souvenir Shop)
sights.description: Shop in Minamiuonuma selling fresh farm-direct vegetables, Uonuma ingredients, souvenirs, and crafts.

sights.name: Hōon-ji Temple
sights.description: Ancient Shingon Chisan-school temple said to have been founded in 735 by Fujiwara no Maro, whose Amida image and treasures are unveiled once every 30 years.

sights.name: Ikeda Memorial Art Museum
sights.description: Art museum displaying about 3,500 items from the late Tsuneo Ikeda’s collection, including sports materials, Lafcadio Hearn documents, and Japanese and overseas art.

sights.name: Mount Makihata
sights.description: A 1,967 m peak in Uonuma Renpo Prefectural Natural Park, with alpine plants and clear-day views of Mount Fuji, the Hakuba range, and the Sea of Japan.

sights.name: Zenibuchi Park Cherry Blossom Viewing
sights.description: Zenibuchi Park, at the foot of Mt. Sakado, holds a spring cherry-blossom viewing with planned nighttime illuminations.

sights.name: Sea of Clouds in Minamiuonuma
sights.name_ja: 南魚沼で雲海を楽しもう
sights.description: Viewpoints around Minamiuonuma where a sea of clouds over the Uonuma Basin can be seen from low mountains by car or on foot.

sights.name: Suzuki Bokushi Memorial Museum
sights.description: Museum displaying manuscripts, relics, and books of Suzuki Bokushi, author of Hokuetsu Seppu, along with Shiozawa textiles.

sights.name: Omatsu Pond
sights.description: A pond in Oguriyama, Minamiuonuma, linked to the local legend of Omatsu, with Benten and Togakushi islands each holding a shrine.

sights.name: Kabasawa Castle Ruins
sights.description: Battlefield castle ruins from the Otate Rebellion, with a 304-meter main bailey overlooking the former Ueda district.

sights.name: Anachi Jūni Daimyōjin Shrine
sights.description: This shrine has a dragon and lion on the eaves, bamboo and tiger plus pine, hawk and sparrow on the brackets, and an unfinished Ōeyama demon-slaying transom.

sights.name: Urasa Castle Ruins
sights.description: Castle ruins on a 300-meter ridge in front of Bishamon Hall in Urasa, built in the Sengoku period to overlook the Mikuni Highway and Uono River traffic.

sights.name: Uonuma Skyline Gokoku Kannon Viewpoint
sights.name_ja: 魚沼スカイライン護国観音展望台
sights.description: Viewpoint on the roughly 20 km Uonuma Skyline, looking down on golden rice fields in early to mid-September.

sights.name: Osaki Dam Lake
sights.description: A nature park around a dam lake in Minamiuonuma, with cherry blossoms and Yairo azaleas, and carp streamers over the water in spring.

sights.name: Kaminohara Park and Omatsu Pond
sights.name_ja: 上の原公園・お松の池
sights.description: Omatsu Pond in Kaminohara Park, at the foot of Mount Masugata, is ringed by about 70 cherry trees and linked to a weaving-woman legend.

sights.name: Osaki Dam Park
sights.description: A park where about 200 cherry trees bloom around the dam lake, with handmade carp streamers above the water.

sights.name: Echigo Jofu
sights.description: Echigo Jofu is a textile nurtured by snow and sustained by 1,700 years of tradition.

sights.name: Joetsu International Playland
sights.name_ja: 上越国際プレイランド
sights.description: Water and amusement park with 150 m and 100 m water bobsleds, a 180 m river ride, go-karts, and miniature golf.

sights.name: Mount Iizuna
sights.description: A dogtooth-violet colony in Minamiuonuma, walkable from the station, where spring flowers cover ancient burial mounds among oak and beech.

sights.name: Tenshoji Temple
sights.description: Soto Zen temple, the setting of an avalanche tale in Hokuetsu Seppu, with three Kamakura-period Buddha images designated prefectural cultural properties.

sights.name: Ohara Sports Park
sights.description: Sports park with a night-lit baseball field, 20 night-lit tennis courts, and a multipurpose ground for soccer and athletics.

sights.name: Iizunayama Kofun Group
sights.description: A kofun group on Iizunayama southwest of Yokawa, once over 100 mounds; about 30 round mounds, mostly around 15 meters across, remain.

sights.name: Rokumanki Castle Ruins
sights.description: Steep mountain castle with large fortifications, said to have been Fukushima Ōinosuke Masatame's residence in the Tenbun era, abandoned when Uesugi Kagekatsu moved to Aizu.

sights.name: Ushiroyama Beech Forest Park
sights.description: Forest-bathing spot in a beech forest at 500 meters elevation, recommended in summer and autumn.

sights.name: Uenohara Iris Garden
sights.description: An iris garden that began with 200 plants from Meiji Shrine and now has 100 varieties and 8,000 plants, with an on-site hot-spring foot bath.

sights.name: Kanreizuka Historic Site Park
sights.description: A park of about 800 square meters around the grave of Kanto kanrei Uesugi Akisada, who died in battle at Nagamorihara.

sights.name: Shiozawa Tsumugi Memorial Hall
sights.description: Hall presenting traditional Shiozawa weaving, with a free ground-floor craft shop and a paid weaving workshop upstairs.

sights.name: The Veranda Ishiuchi Maruyama Night Terrace
sights.name_en: The Veranda Ishiuchi Maruyama Night Terrace
sights.description: A viewing terrace at The Veranda Ishiuchi Maruyama with a night gondola, sunset and city-light views, and evening fireworks over Minamiuonuma.

sights.name: Ueno Mineral Spring
sights.description: Quiet cold mineral spring in Minamiuonuma, a toji resort since the Meiji era, with sulfur water at 14–16°C.

sights.name: Nakajima House
sights.description: A house on Makino-dori in Shiozawa, a former Mikuni Kaido post town, holding Mokujiki's only Myoken Bodhisattva, carved in 1805.

sights.name: Ikazawa Gorge
sights.description: This gorge runs upstream from Jumonji Gorge above Mikunigawa Dam, where the Shimotsu River and Kuromatazawa join; a ten-minute walk reaches Rainbow Falls.

sights.name: Mount Nakanodake
sights.description: One of the Echigo Sanzan, this 2,085-meter peak on the Minamiuonuma–Uonuma border is about six hours from the Jujikyo trailhead.

sights.name: Maiko Resort Green Season
sights.description: Maiko Resort in Minamiuonuma offers summer camping, ground golf, disc golf, and reserved firefly and stargazing tours.

sights.name: Kongo Reisen (Sacred Spring)
sights.name_ja: 金剛霊泉（こんごうれいせん）
sights.description: Spring water from bedrock midway up Mount Hakkai, one of the Three Mountains of Echigo, with year-round constant flow and temperature.

sights.name: Kimikaeri Kannon
sights.description: An unpainted wooden Kannon, 1.49 m tall and carved from a single pillar, unveiled once every 12 years.

sights.name: Ueda no Sato (Countryside Experience Village)
sights.description: Countryside experience village in Uonuma offering rice planting, harvesting, and handmade soba making.

sights.name: Minamiuonuma Kirizai Rice Bowl
sights.description: Local dish of Minamiuonuma Koshihikari rice topped with finely cut vegetables, pickles, and natto, served at flagged restaurants and Muikamachi onsen facilities.

sights.name: Mount Iiji
sights.description: A 1,111 m mountain with views of the Uonuma range; hikes take about 2.5 hours from the Maiko or Igarashi trailheads.

sights.name: Oguriyama Sun Sports Land
sights.name_ja: 小栗山サンスポーツランド
sights.description: Multi-sport facility with three night-lit tennis courts, four gateball courts, and a 2,100-square-metre skate park.

sights.name: Ueda no Sato Countryside Experience Village
sights.name_en: Ueda no Sato Countryside Experience Village
sights.name_ja: いなか体験村 上田の郷
sights.description: A year-round rural experience village in Minamiuonuma with rice planting, soba making, mochi pounding, and meals at its countryside cafeteria.

sights.name: Shakunage Lake (Mikunigawa Dam)
sights.name_ja: 三国川ダムしゃくなげ湖
sights.description: Mikunigawa Dam on the Mikuni River supplies water and electricity and reduces flooding; a circuit around Shakunage Lake is an autumn-foliage spot, with camping and fishing nearby.

sights.name: Mikuni Kaido Shiozawa-juku (Bokushi Street) Walk
sights.name_ja: 三国街道塩沢宿（牧之通り）の散策
sights.description: A guided walk on Bokushi Street, a snow-country post town of covered arcades where author Suzuki Bokushi lived.

sights.name: Snow Country A-Grade Gourmet
sights.description: Japan's first project disclosing ingredient information, serving local snow-country dishes without chemical seasonings, rated one to three stars in the Snow Country Tourism Zone.

sights.name: Exploring Uncho's Works in Minamiuonuma
sights.name_ja: 南魚沼の雲蝶作品を探求
sights.description: Ryukoku-ji Kannon Hall and Anachi Junidaimyojin preserve Uncho's openwork carvings of lions, peonies, dragons, and an unfinished Shuten-doji scene.

stays.name: Satoyama Jujo
stays.name_ja: 里山十帖
stays.description: Inn in Osawa, Minamiuonuma with scenic views and a quiet countryside setting.

stays.name: ryugon

stays.name: YUZAWA Onsen Lodge House
stays.description: Private lodge house in Ishiuchi, Minamiuonuma, one minute from the Ishiuchi Maruyama ski lift.

day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Mitsuke with an open lawn facing Mount Sumon and Mount Awaga, a local produce market, Suwa Dairy soft serve, and yakiniku restaurant Kiraku.

sights.name: Mitsuke English Garden Autumn Fair & Garden Halloween
sights.name_en: Mitsuke English Garden Autumn Fair & Garden Halloween
sights.name_ja: みつけイングリッシュガーデン「オータムフェア＆ガーデンハロウィン」
sights.description: Autumn fair at Mitsuke English Garden, with dahlias, anemones and salvia in bloom, Halloween photo spots, quiz rallies and craft activities.

sights.name: Mitsuke English Garden
sights.name_ja: みつけイングリッシュガーデン
sights.description: Free English-style garden in Mitsuke supervised by horticulturist Kei Yamada, with seasonal roses, peonies and dahlias plus an on-site cafe.

sights.name: Navel Mitsuke
sights.description: Civic exchange center in Mitsuke and a hub for community activities, with a local-products market, café, multipurpose plaza, and town information.

sights.name: Shinden Park
sights.description: A 1.7-hectare park near central Mitsuke, with a gourd-shaped pond, seasonal garden flowers, and a rest area.

sights.name: Ohira Forest Park
sights.description: Forest park in Mitsuke centered on Ohira Pond, with Japanese red pine woods, walking trails, and a 100-site campground.

sights.name: Suidoyama-Kannonyama Park
sights.description: Hilltop park in southeastern Mitsuke with views of Mount Sumon, Awagatake, and the city, plus spring cherries and about 10,000 hydrangeas.

sights.name: Mitsuke Heritage Hall
sights.description: Museum on life in Mitsuke, showing everyday tools of past residents, Jomon pottery from the nationally designated Mimitori Site, and local history and folk materials.

sights.name: Mitsuke Sogo Gym
sights.description: Gym in Mitsuke, Niigata.

sights.name: Tentoku-ji Inari Hall
sights.description: Inari hall within Tentoku-ji, founded in 1481 by enshrining Inari from Kyoto as the temple guardian, with a 1988 monument of Aizu Yaichi's school precepts.

sights.name: Mitsuke Civic Baseball Stadium
sights.description: Municipal baseball stadium in Mitsuke with two fields, both equipped for night games.

sights.name: Citizens' Forest
sights.description: A citizens’ forest in Mitsuke with about 400 donated memorial cherry trees of seven varieties on roughly 2 hectares of a 12-hectare site.

sights.name: Oguriyama Fudo-in Temple
sights.description: The 17th temple of the Echigo 33 Kannon pilgrimage, said to have been founded by Priest Joren in 806.

sights.name: Hydrangeas at Suido-yama and Kannon-yama Park
sights.name_en: Hydrangeas at Suido-yama and Kannon-yama Park
sights.name_ja: 水道山・観音山公園のあじさい
sights.description: About 10,000 blue and purple hydrangeas bloom on Kannon-yama's slope from mid-June to early July, with paths for walking among the flowers.

sights.name: Mitsuke Sugisawa Forest
sights.description: A 20-hectare prefectural forest in Mitsuke for nature experiences, with a viewing gazebo overlooking the Echigo Sanzan and about 1,000 wild mountain lilies in mid-to-late July.

sights.name: Tsubakizawa-ji Temple
sights.description: Shingon temple known as the 16th of the Echigo 33 Kannon sites, said to be Uesugi Kenshin's prayer temple and to keep a military screen he donated.

sights.name: Mitsuke Sports Park
sights.description: Sports park in Mitsuke with a lit certified 400-meter track, five lit tennis courts, a baseball field, and an administration building.

sights.name: Yamagata Aritomo Poem Monument
sights.description: A poem monument to Yamagata Aritomo, who visited Mitsuke as an imperial commander in the Boshin War, stands beside Oguriyama Fudo-in's Kannon hall.

sights.name: Mitsuke City Community Bus
sights.name_ja: 見附市コミュニティバス
sights.description: A community bus in Mitsuke with a 100-yen flat fare and day pass, useful for sights such as Mitsuke English Garden and Patio Niigata.

sights.name: Mitsuke Ryotei Lunch (Daytime Kaiseki)
sights.name_ja: 料亭のまち見附の老舗「料亭ランチ・お昼懐石」
sights.description: Five long-established ryotei in textile town Mitsuke serve affordable daytime kaiseki lunches, each 3–10 minutes from Nakanoshima-Mitsuke IC.

sights.name: Kannon-yama Park Beech and Japanese Hornbeam Forest
sights.name_en: Kannon-yama Park Beech and Japanese Hornbeam Forest
sights.name_ja: 観音山公園のブナ、アカシデ自然林
sights.description: A 1.1-hectare natural forest of beech and Japanese hornbeam over 400 years old, one of Niigata’s 100 selected beech forests.

sights.name: Mitsuke City Giant Kite Heritage Hall
sights.name_en: Mitsuke City Giant Kite Heritage Hall
sights.description: Workshop and gallery in central Imachi where visitors can view hexagonal giant kites made for the Imachi–Nakanoshima kite battle.

sights.name: Factory Outlet Shopping
sights.name_ja: ファクトリーアウトレットショッピング
sights.description: Primeira, a shop beside a knit factory in Mitsuke, sells brand outlet and original goods at factory prices, with no reservation required.

sights.name: Mitsuke MADE Hospitality: A Little Luxury Reward Tour
sights.name_en: Mitsuke MADE Hospitality: A Little Luxury Reward Tour
sights.name_ja: 見附MADEのおもてなし～ちょっと贅沢な欲張りご褒美ツアー～
sights.description: Half-day Mitsuke tour visiting an English garden, a knit outlet, a traditional restaurant, and Patio Niigata roadside station.

sights.name: Imacho Historical Walk (Guide Group Nabirazu)
sights.name_ja: 今町歴史散歩 ガイドグループなびらーず～史跡巡り～
sights.description: A guided walk through Imacho, a former boat-transport town and Hokuetsu Boshin War battleground, visiting shrines, temples, haiku monuments, and battle sites.

stays.name_ja: ホテルルートイン見附 -中之島見附インター-

stays.description: Ryokan inn in Gakko, Mitsuke; 5-minute drive from Mitsuke Station.

stays.name_ja: 草薙旅館
stays.description: Ryokan inn in Hon, Mitsuke with Wi-Fi.

stays.description: Hotel in Mitsuke, Niigata.

stays.description: Hotel at Danjobetsujinko Onsen in Joshinta, Mitsuke with a large communal bath.

day_to_day.name: Sasagawa Nagare Roadside Station (Yuhi Kaikan)
day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅「笹川流れ」 夕日会館
day_to_day.description: Niigata's northernmost roadside station on the Sea of Japan, beside JR Kuwagawa Station, with a bridge to the beach.

day_to_day.name: Iwafune Port Direct Sales Shop
day_to_day.name_ja: 岩船港直売所
day_to_day.description: Fishery-cooperative market beside Iwafune Port's landing and auction site, selling just-landed local fish and produce, with a fishermen's cafeteria.

day_to_day.name: Roadside Station Asahi (Asahi Midori no Sato)
day_to_day.name_en: Roadside Station Asahi (Asahi Midori no Sato)
day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅 「朝日（朝日みどりの里）」（国道7号）
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in Murakami's Asahi district with a product shop, restaurant serving Asahi pork, 60°C Mahoroba hot spring, pool, cottages, and a toy history museum.

day_to_day.name: Kamihayashi Roadside Station (Honami no Sato)
day_to_day.name_ja: 道の駅 「神林（穂波の里）」
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in the Iwafune Koshihikari rice district, selling fresh vegetables, local rice, mochi, rice-flour bread, and sasa dango.

day_to_day.name: Asahi Midori-no-Sato Farm Produce Shop
day_to_day.name_ja: 朝日みどりの里農産物直売施設
day_to_day.description: Direct-sales shop selling Murakami seasonal vegetables, fruit and processed farm goods, with a wide selection of wild vegetables in season.

day_to_day.name: Yume Farm Arakawa Strawberry Garden
day_to_day.name_ja: 夢ファームあらかわいちご園
day_to_day.description: A 2,000-square-metre greenhouse growing Echigo-hime, Niigata’s original strawberry, for tasting when fully ripe.

activities.name: Murakami Evening Bamboo Lantern Festival
activities.name_ja: むらかみ 宵の竹灯籠まつり
activities.description: About 20,000 bamboo lanterns light Komachi and Anzen-koji streets in Murakami's castle town, with free music at nearby temples and townhouses.

activities.name: Senami Onsen
activities.name_ja: 瀬波温泉
activities.description: Coastal hot-spring area in Murakami that began in 1904 when hot water erupted during oil drilling; the source is 95°C.

activities.name: Senami Onsen Beach
activities.name_ja: 瀬波温泉海水浴場
activities.description: A roughly 1 km swimming beach just behind Senami Onsen, listed among the Environment Ministry's 100 selected bathing beaches, with calm water and sunsets between Sado and Awashima.

activities.name: Miyai Sake Brewery (Shimeharitsuru)
activities.name_ja: 宮尾酒造（株）
activities.description: Founded in 1819, this Murakami brewery draws Asahi-range groundwater and polishes local Gohyakumangoku rice for flavorful Shimeharitsuru sake.

activities.name: Yumoto Ryusen (Senami Onsen)
activities.name_ja: 瀬波温泉 湯元龍泉
activities.description: Day-use hot spring in Senami Onsen drawing about 94°C sodium chloride water from 180 meters underground, with a sulfur scent near the Sea of Japan.

activities.name: Imagawa Campground
activities.name_ja: 今川キャンプ場
activities.description: White-sand beach campsite with rocky stretches in Murakami, where swimming, fishing, and walks are possible and camping is also allowed in the parking area.

activities.name: Asahi Mahoroba Onsen
activities.name_ja: 朝日まほろば温泉（朝日まほろばふれあいセンター）
activities.description: Day-use hot spring in Murakami with soft water from about 1,300 meters underground and open-air baths overlooking seasonal scenery beside Roadside Station Asahi.

activities.name: Sasagawa Campground
activities.name_ja: 笹川キャンプ場
activities.description: Sandy campsite and swimming beach on the Sasagawa Nagare coast in Murakami, with pine-covered rocks and a path to Itagai Beach.

activities.name: Taiyo Shuzo Nagomigura Exhibition Hall
activities.name_ja: 大洋酒造（株）
activities.description: Sake brewery in Murakami with a Nagomigura exhibition of brewing tools and sake history, and brewery tours by reservation.

activities.name: Futagojima Forest Park Auto Campground
activities.name_ja: 二子島森林公園オートキャンプ場
activities.description: Auto campground on one of two islands in Miomote Dam Lake, linked by a floating pier, with tent sites, fishing, and rental boats.

activities.name: Samukawa Campground
activities.name_ja: 寒川キャンプ場
activities.description: Seaside campsite on a white-sand beach with emerald water in Murakami's Sanpoku district, where visitors can swim, fish, and walk.

activities.name: Itagai Campground
activities.name_ja: 板貝キャンプ場
activities.description: Campsite on a wide, gently shelving inlet beach in Murakami, where visitors can swim, fish from the rocks, and walk a path toward Sasagawa Beach.

activities.name: Yurihana Onsen Hachiman Exchange Hall
activities.name_ja: ゆり花温泉 交流の館 八幡
activities.description: This public inn in Murakami Sanpoku, offering local cuisine and sodium-calcium sulfate baths at Yurihana Onsen, closed at the end of March 2026.

activities.name: Goishi Campground
activities.name_ja: 碁石キャンプ場
activities.description: Coastal campsite in Katsugi, Murakami, where black-and-white pebbles resemble Go stones and are said to have named the place.

activities.name: Senami Onsen Funyu Park
activities.name_ja: 瀬波温泉 噴湯公園
activities.description: Hilltop park overlooking the Senami hot-spring town and the Sea of Japan, with a steaming source well where visitors can boil onsen eggs.

activities.name: Kuwagawa Campground
activities.name_ja: 桑川キャンプ場
activities.description: Campground on a fine sandy beach in Kuwagawa, offering swimming, fishing, and sunset views toward Awashima.

activities.name: New Tea Picking Experience
activities.name_ja: 新茶のお茶摘み体験
activities.description: May tea-picking in a Murakami tea field, with instruction from a tea-shop owner and leaves you may take home.

activities.name: Northernmost Tea Dyeing Experience
activities.name_ja: 北限の茶染め体験
activities.description: A Murakami-tea dyeing experience where you can make an original handkerchief and a stencil-dyed frame.

activities.name: Senami Onsen One-of-a-Kind Vessel Making (Toi Pottery Studio)
activities.name_en: Senami Onsen One-of-a-Kind Vessel Making (Toi Pottery Studio)
activities.name_ja: 瀬波温泉の思い出に！1点物のお好きな器作り体験（1個）
activities.description: Make one ceramic vessel, such as a tea bowl or mug, at Toi Pottery Studio; a 28-year instructor assists and firing takes about three months.

activities.name: Sea Kayaking at Sasagawa Nagare
activities.name_ja: 笹川流れでシーカヤック体験
activities.description: Sea kayaking along Sasagawa Nagare, a national Place of Scenic Beauty and Natural Monument, passing unusual rocks and entering sea caves, with rentals for beginners.
