food.description: Chinese restaurant in Sun Mall Town offering over 15 original ramen and seasonally limited original noodles.

food.name: Chuka Ryori Kinkaro
food.description: Chinese restaurant with a red sign along a national road, serving Sichuan mapo tofu, gyoza, fried rice, sweet-and-sour pork, noodles and set meals, plus weekday lunch.

food.name: de Vinco Henjinmokko
food.name_ja: de Vinco へんじんもっこ
food.description: Restaurant directly operated by Henjinmokko, known for sausages, serving Italian-centered European-style dishes including pizza from a high-temperature oven and pasta, along with Henjinmokko products, in an open kitchen.

food.name: Le Ash
food.description: Restaurant with counter seating serving lunch and an evening special menu, including hamburg steak, combo plates, and pork cutlet.

food.name: SEISUKE next door
food.description: French and Italian restaurant, the second shop of Restaurant Seisuke, in a complex at Sawada beach; breakfast with bread and coffee is also served.

food.name: Cucina
food.description: Located near the Kanai Station intersection along the Nakatsu River; serves pizza, pasta, paella, risotto and carpaccio using Sado ingredients, with lunch, set courses and banquets.

food.name: Un Grand Pas
food.description: French restaurant below the slope to Sado High School, serving seasonal fish roast and other Sado-ingredient dishes through dessert, plus evening courses and set menus with a main, salad and drink.

food.name: Motsu Yaki Den Sado Kanai
food.name_ja: もつ焼き でん 佐渡金井店

food.name: Izakaya Kosugiya
food.description: An izakaya near Ogi Port Sado Kisen Terminal serving sashimi and other dishes made with Sado seafood and local vegetables.

food.name: Izakaya Nogata
food.description: Izakaya with a black plank exterior serving Sado beef, local seafood and grilled skewers, with personal roasters for yakiniku and, on some days, seasonal sashimi and grilled fish.

food.name: Izakaya Orufe
food.description: Izakaya in Aikawa, reopened in 2007 from a long-established snack bar, serving skewers, fried food, grilled fish, steak, noodles and fried rice, with counter and raised-floor seating.

food.name: Jizake to Shunsai Ryanto
food.name_ja: 地酒と旬彩 りゃんと
food.description: Japanese izakaya in Ryotsu's entertainment district on Sado, serving local sake and seasonal seafood from kaiseki courses to sake snacks, with counter seats.

food.name: Izakaya Hotaru
food.description: Couple-run homestyle izakaya serving fried natto, squid dumplings, pork skewers grilled to order with sweet miso sauce, and light-tasting cold ramen.

food.name: Ikoi no Ba Saneki
food.description: Daytime set-meal restaurant and evening izakaya serving a seasonal set meal, katsudon, salt-based vegetable ramen, and eight-piece nigiri sushi by reservation.

food.name: Izakaya Okesa Yokocho
food.name_ja: 居酒屋 おけさ横丁
food.description: Izakaya inside a hotel serving Sado countryside cuisine and local sake.

food.name: Naito Supotto J1
food.description: Night spot serving drinks and occasional seafood from fishermen the owners know, with karaoke on a 100-inch screen.

food.name: Sunakku Appuru
food.name_ja: スナック あっぷる
food.description: Snack bar in Aikawa with a gray-and-black interior, a 100-inch screen and karaoke; serves drinks and light-flavored ramen, and sometimes holds mini live shows.

food.name: OKESA BAR BUNZO
food.description: Bar serving drinks from local sake to Scotch; about 90% of customers are local drinkers, in a space particular to Aikawa.

food.name: Sakenomi-dokoro Hetappi
food.description: Counter-seat drinking place where solo guests are welcome.

food.name: Izakaya Kyoan
food.description: Izakaya where guests can chat casually.

food.name: Izakaya Arinko
food.description: Izakaya with counter and raised seating serving kushiyaki, grilled fish, handmade gyoza and tamagoyaki made with local ingredients; banquets arranged to budget.

food.name: Kushiyaki Kinpuku
food.description: Charcoal-grilled yakitori (meat, gizzard, tsukune and daily specials) in a bar-like interior, with Sado cold sake, wine and a simmered dish.

food.name: Yakiniku no Ie
food.description: Yakiniku restaurant serving lean Sado beef thigh meat with a house yakiniku sauce, alongside kimchi from Kimchi no Ie.

food.name: Yakitori Kushishige
food.description: Yakitori shop on a coastal street grilling over binchotan charcoal with house-made sauce; Kanto-style eel is available in summer.

food.name: Yakitori Yajima
food.description: Charcoal-grilled yakitori using Date-dori chicken and Sado beef skewers; parties of 1 to 15.

food.name: Yakiniku Aka Chochin
food.name_ja: 焼肉 赤ちょうちん
food.description: Seaside restaurant serving yakiniku as well as ramen, set meals, and rice bowls, with a large parking lot in front.

food.name: Sumibi Kushiyaki Enman
food.description: Charcoal-skewer restaurant in Hamochi grilling hand-skewered Koshi no Tori chicken from Niigata over high-heat charcoal, also serving chicken-bone soup ramen and other dishes; takeout available.

food.name: Noriba Shokudo Shiosai Ryotsu
food.name_ja: のりば食堂 しおさい 両津店
food.description: Standing soba counter in Sado, Niigata.

food.name: Daimaru Ramen
food.description: Ramen restaurant serving additive-free, pesticide-free local ingredients, including Sado white-miso ramen and daily handmade chashu; takeout gyoza is also available.

food.name: Soba Dokoro Yozaemon
food.description: Serves handmade soba from home-grown, home-milled flour, plus soba croquettes and soba shiruko, in a renovated former mine-chief residence on Aikawa Kyomachi-dori; open Saturdays, Sundays and holidays only.

food.name: Noodle Restaurant Isonoya
food.description: Serves udon and soba made each morning, plus curry nanban and other noodles, set meals, and donburi; the Isonoya set includes assorted tempura, salad, half rice, and mini udon or mini soba.

food.name: Teuchi Udon Okesa
food.name_ja: 手打うどん おけさ
food.description: Sanuki udon shop whose Kagawa-born owner serves 100% domestic-wheat hand-made noodles in a grilled-mackerel and bonito broth simmered one hour each morning, plus rice sets, three Sado sakes, snacks, and pizza.

food.name: Ikebukuro Taishoken Sado
food.name_ja: 池袋大勝軒 佐渡店
food.description: Tsukemen restaurant branched from Ikebukuro Taishoken; serves pork, chicken and seafood soup with homemade noodles.

food.name: Soba Chobokuri
food.description: Soba shop opened in 2007 serving year-round 100% stone-milled soba, including ago-dashi bukkake soba.

food.name: Kato Restaurant
food.description: Restaurant in central Kanai founded over 60 years ago, serving ramen, rice bowls, curry, set meals and Western dishes, including pork teki rice and homemade nuka sanma with Sado Koshihikari rice.

food.name: Family Restaurant Taigaa
food.name_ja: ファミリーレストラン たいがあ
food.description: Family restaurant on the Minamisen bus street serving hamburg steak, katsudon, fried rice, ramen, a pork stamina rice bowl with garlic and garlic chives, and omelette rice; a stage with a drum set can host live music.

food.name: Kitchen Kotoya
food.name_ja: キッチン ことうや
food.description: Meals are served in a dining room made by renovating about half of an old house; dogs have separate seating, phone reservations are accepted, and a Japanese-style room for up to 10 can be reserved.

food.name: Sosaku Ryori no Mise Taro
food.name_ja: 創作料理の店 タロー
food.description: Creative cuisine restaurant serving tofu pizza, beer-battered karaage chicken, German-style potatoes, and mapo tofu, with shochu available.

food.name: Unsuke
food.description: Serves Sadogohan, 10 seasonal dishes centered on Sado island ingredients, in a former folk house; a private plan for one group a day includes a meal and a building and storehouse tour, and vegetarian or vegan requests can be met.

food.name: Kominka Kukan Kyomachitei
food.name_ja: 古民家空間 京町亭
food.description: A renovated old house in Aikawa serving dishes made with Sado ingredients; terrace seating is available on warm, clear days.

food.name: Oshokuji Dokoro Mitsuruka
food.description: Restaurant on Ryotsu Ebisu Honmachi-dori shopping street serving handmade meals made with seasonal ingredients and local sake.

food.name: Mereparekaiko
food.description: A couple who moved to Mushizaki, formerly a settlement of 17 people, serve menus using the island's seasonal ingredients and medicinal-cuisine knowledge.

food.name: Shikisai Kappo Den
food.description: A Japanese restaurant that uses local ingredients, serves Sado sake, and is also open for lunch on weekdays.

food.name: Aburiya Charakuragee
food.name_ja: 炙り屋 ちゃらくらげぇ
food.description: Grilled-food restaurant named from a Sado dialect word meaning iikagen; seasonal Sado sashimi and local sake are also served.

food.name: Sumibiyaki Toki
food.description: Restaurant serving charcoal-grilled seasonal local fish and steak, Sado regional dishes, original dishes, set meals, rice bowls and noodles, with local sake.

food.name: Shokusai Sobo Tan
food.description: Creative-cuisine restaurant using seasonal ingredients; lunch includes omurice and pasta, evening service includes meat and fish dishes, and there are over 100 cocktails.

food.name: Yajima Higashi-odori
food.description: Casual restaurant serving Sado-grown Koshihikari rice dishes such as kamameshi and oyakodon, noodles and fried foods, with charcoal-grilled Tsugaru jidori yakitori from the evening.

food.name: Yo Kitaya
food.description: Old house from the gold-mining era serving a menu of seasonal wild plants and local ingredients; also sells Sado souvenirs and goods.

food.name: Sado Kaiten Sushi Benkei Sado Main Store
food.name_en: Sado Kaiten Sushi Benkei Sado Main Store
food.name_ja: 佐渡 廻転寿司 弁慶 佐渡本店

food.name: Gin Sushi
food.description: Sushi restaurant on Haneda shopping street with a single-board counter, serving an eight-piece Sado sushi set of that day's local catch plus dishes such as overnight-dried squid and mozuku.

food.name: Matsuhama
food.description: Restaurant in Ogi serving fresh seafood, meat, and drinks; specialty is the reservation-required Ogi Irifune Gozen, a two-tiered box of sashimi, grilled fish, fried food, turban shell, and igoneri.

food.name: Onogame Lodge
food.description: Serves set meals, curry, and noodles using local ingredients, plus a seafood rice bowl of fish the owner catches; choose a seat and order at the counter, with terrace seats overlooking Onogame.

food.name: Tabiso Shokujidokoro Minato
food.name_ja: 旅荘 食事処 みなと
food.description: Serves seafood from Takachi fishing port, including squid somen with homemade sauce, at an attached dining hall.

food.name: Kappo Ishiyama
food.description: Kappo restaurant serving seasonal seafood dishes, including a daily set meal with sashimi, for lunch, meals, and banquets; it has a courtyard.

food.name: Sushi Chozaburo
food.description: Sushi restaurant using fish from Ryotsu Market and local fishermen, including Oma tuna and Aomori sea urchin, plus set meals, rice bowls, and clear-soup ramen.

food.name: Itamae no Mise Takeya
food.description: Restaurant in Aikawa's Tenryo-dori shopping street serving sashimi, simmered fish, and ika no goro-yaki (squid and vegetables steam-grilled in miso with squid liver), plus Sado-grown Koshihikari rice.

food.name: Uoya Ryori no Mise Uoharu
food.name_ja: 魚屋料理の店 魚晴
food.description: Ground-floor fish shop sells local catch from the morning auction; upstairs tatami seating serves set menus and seafood picked at the counter cooked to order, including abalone simmered rice bowls and abalone steak.

food.name: Kuidokoro Hikino
food.description: Serves sashimi, grilled fish, nigiri sushi, thick rolls and boxed sushi made with seafood from off Sado, plus sushi-and-ramen sets and yakiniku grilled on a far-infrared roaster.

food.name: Sakae Sushi
food.description: Sushi restaurant facing Ogi port; uses locally landed seafood bought directly from fishermen when possible.

food.name: Kominka Shokudo Mochidake
food.name_ja: 古民家食堂 持田家
food.description: Run by the adjacent Mochida fish shop; serves seasonal seafood, including a rice bowl with about 10 fresh toppings at lunch, plus local sake and cocktails at night in a 60-year-old house.

food.name: Kappo Nakasho
food.description: Japanese restaurant serving sashimi, grilled fish, seafood donburi with eight or more kinds of seafood, and tempura donburi with shrimp, squid and vegetables; Aikawa miso soup and Sado sake are also served, with tatami seating.

food.name: Kappo Inayoshi
food.description: Kappo restaurant in Ogi serving grilled eel available year-round, plus kamameshi, sauce katsudon, set meals and noodles, with three private rooms.

food.name: Kappo Goshima
food.description: Kappo restaurant run by an owner who trained in Tokyo, serving local fish, bara sushi, and an omakase course of fish purchased that day.

food.name: Kisaragi Honten
food.description: A dining place for tourists serving Sado ingredients, with a fatty silver salmon set meal, turban shell curry, and handmade Sadokko pudding using Sado milk.

food.name: Nihon Ryori Urashima
food.description: Japanese restaurant serving seasonal sashimi, grilled dishes and simmered dishes made with fresh Sado seafood.

food.name: Kappo Ikkyu
food.description: Kappo restaurant serving fish; the omakase course includes sashimi, tempura and grilled fish using Sado ingredients, with all-you-can-drink available.

food.name: Oshokuji Dokoro Yuzuru
food.description: Restaurant in the Sado Historical Legend Museum over a pond, with views of carp and a Japanese garden; serves seafood including a seasonal seafood donburi and Sado Koshihikari rice, with no admission fee for dining only.

food.name: Higuchi Shokudo
food.description: Shokudo on a national road serving sushi with seasonal toppings, plus a la carte dishes, ramen, set meals and donburi, with local sake, shochu, beer, wine and cocktails; three private rooms.

food.name: Taishu Kappo Katsusai
food.name_ja: 大衆割烹 かつさい
food.description: Family-run restaurant about five minutes from the Ogi Port Sado Kisen Terminal, serving seafood rice bowls and sashimi set meals made with fish caught in Ogi.

food.name: Karuta Japanese Restaurant
food.description: Japanese restaurant in the Sawada district serving tempura and seafood as its main dishes, plus set meals, rice bowls, noodles, and courses with sashimi, tempura, salad and dessert.

food.name: Ogi Sushi
food.description: Shopping-street sushi restaurant for lunch and evening meals, serving seasonal seafood sushi, miso soup, summer eel, winter hot pots and a lunch tempura rice bowl, with three raised rooms.

food.name: Tengu
food.description: Serves mainly sashimi and grilled fish, sometimes the owner's catch, plus charcoal-grilled yakiniku and yakitori; lunch includes set meals and ramen.

food.name: Toki Nomura Food
food.description: Gelato and ice-cream shop in Sado, Niigata.

food.name: Yamashita Tea House
food.description: Tea house in a renovated barn with Ogi tarai-bune tub-boat tables, serving zenzai and warabi-mochi.

food.name: Puchidoru
food.description: Shop offering natural-yeast bread and sweets made with Sado rice flour, dairy and fruit, including Shima Cheesecake and Okesa Potato, with an attached cafe corner.

food.name: Matterato
food.description: Gelato specialty shop using Sado Island strawberries, figs, milk, and honey.

sights.name: Manjoshiki Rock Shelf
sights.description: A broad rock shelf on Sawazaki Coast in Sado, uplifted by an earthquake, where tide pools reflect the sky on calm days.

sights.name: Kitazawa Flotation Plant
sights.description: A former gold and silver ore flotation plant in Aikawa, Sado, where the method was first put to practical use in Japan in 1940.

sights.name: Ameya Pier
sights.description: A roughly 30-meter pier at Sawada Beach on Sado, popular for photos, with Futami Peninsula to the right and Ogi Peninsula to the left.

sights.name: Sado Gold Mine
sights.description: Historic site of 400 years of Sado gold and silver mining, where tunnels show past mining work and Meiji-era industrial remains.

sights.name: Toki Forest Park
sights.description: A Sado park with crested ibis exhibits on conservation and reintroduction, close-up viewing of captive toki, and a monument to Kin, the last Japanese-born ibis.

sights.name: Sado History and Legend Museum
sights.description: Museum where life-sized robot dolls reenact Sado history and legends, with an attached memorial hall for Living National Treasure Sasaki Shodo.

sights.name: Sado Nishimikawa Gold Park
sights.name_ja: 佐渡西三川ゴールドパーク
sights.description: Hands-on museum at the Nishimikawa placer gold mine site, where visitors can pan for gold and see history exhibits.

sights.name: Onogame Rock and Tobishima Daylily Colony
sights.name_en: Onogame Rock and Tobishima Daylily Colony
sights.description: A 167-meter-high monolithic rock jutting into the sea, listed with two Michelin Green Guide stars, among Tobishima daylilies that bloom from late May to early June.

sights.name: Yajima and Kyojima Islands
sights.description: Two islands float in a calm inlet and are linked by a red drum bridge, where you can ride tarai boats.

sights.name: Shukunegi
sights.description: Historic Sado port village of over 100 plank-walled houses by a small inlet, designated a national Important Preservation District, with three houses open for a fee.

sights.name: Myosenji Temple
sights.description: Temple founded in 1278 on a former Takeda Honma castle site, with Niigata's only five-story pagoda and Hino Suketomo's grave.

sights.name: Osado Skyline
sights.description: A scenic road about 30 km long linking Kanai and Aikawa, rising above 900 meters with views over Sado Island.

sights.name: Senkaku Bay Ageshima Park
sights.description: The park at Ageshima Bay, Senkaku Bay's fifth scenic spot, has an observatory, a paid underwater viewing boat and an aquarium.

sights.name: Futatsugame Beach
sights.description: A swimming beach beside Futatsugame on Sado, listed among Japan’s 100 best bathing beaches and given two stars in the Michelin Green Guide Japon.

sights.name: Futatsugame Island
sights.description: Island resembling two crouching turtles whose view changes with the tide, with a beach in Japan's 100 bathing-beach selection and two Michelin Green Guide stars.

sights.name: Nanban Ebi (Sweet Shrimp)
sights.description: Sweet shrimp formally called Hokkoku akaebi, known in Niigata as nanban ebi because their color and shape resemble red chili peppers.

sights.name: Sado Daylily Week
sights.description: In June, about 500,000 Tobishima daylily plants bloom around Onogame on Sado's Sotokaifu coast, with local drum and folk-song performances.

sights.name: Watsu Shrine
sights.description: Shrine enshrining Itakeru-no-Mikoto as a guardian of travel, and one of nine Sado shrines listed in the 927 Engishiki, called the island’s ichinomiya.

sights.name: Koyozan (Autumn Foliage Mountain)
sights.description: Mountain area in central Kosado whose southern slopes are known for autumn foliage, with walking paths, lookouts, and a late-October festival.

sights.name: Nanaura Coast
sights.description: A 10 km uplifted coastline spanning seven villages, with scattered coral, sunset viewpoints, Married Couple Rocks, and a Jomon cave dwelling.

sights.name: Shukunegi Raised Wave-Cut Platform
sights.description: A raised wave-cut platform formed when the land rose about 2 meters in the 1802 Ogi earthquake, with reddish earth and rugged rocks beyond a tunnel.

sights.name: Ryuodo Cave
sights.description: A lava cave in Kotoura, Sado, called Sado's Blue Grotto, where sunlight turns the sea blue and access is by kayak or boat tour.

sights.name: Choja Bridge
sights.description: Choja Bridge, completed in 2002 in Fukura on Sado, is Niigata’s first extradosed bridge and spans a deep inlet.

sights.name: Sawada Beach
sights.description: Calm, shallow swimming beach on Mano Bay, a two-minute walk from Kawarada shopping street, with the Ameya Pier photo spot.

sights.name: World Heritage Liner Bus
sights.name_ja: 世界遺産ライナーバス
sights.description: Reservation-required liner bus between Ryotsu Port and Kirarium Sado; a ticket gives 50 yen off the Kirarium exhibition fee.

sights.name: Sai-no-Kawara
sights.description: A seaside path from Negai village linking Ono-game and Futatsu-game, where caves hold rows of stone Jizo statues.

sights.name: Benkei no Hasami-iwa (Wedged Rock)
sights.description: Coastal rock formation in Shimo-Aikawa, Sado, where a wedge-shaped boulder is wedged between giant rocks, linked to a Sado Benkei legend.

sights.name: Oma Port
sights.description: A Sado port completed in 1892 by the pre-concrete tataki method for mine ore and coal shipments; stone revetments, a truss bridge, loader piers, and crane bases remain.

sights.name: Matsugasaki History Park
sights.name_ja: 松ヶ崎ヒストリーパーク
sights.description: Coastal leisure spot on Sado with Konose Lighthouse, a free campsite, and a reconstructed Edo-period Sado magistrate’s office at a historic landing point.

sights.name: Daizen Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in rural Sado with a thatched Noh stage rebuilt in 1846, a prefectural tangible folk cultural property.

sights.name: Former Aikawa Detention Branch
sights.description: Former detention branch in Aikawa.

sights.name: Sado Magistrate's Office Site
sights.description: The government section of Aikawa’s 1603 shogunate magistrate’s office, with courts and an on-site gold and silver refinery, was restored in 2000.

sights.name: Kiyomizu-dera Temple
sights.description: Temple on Sado founded in 808 and modeled on Kyoto's Kiyomizu-dera, enshrining Senju Kannon and included in the Seven Lucky Gods pilgrimage.

sights.name: Senjojiki Rock Reef
sights.description: A flat, wide rock reef on the Shimo-Aikawa coast, long known as a scenic spot, with a bridge for viewing Sea of Japan waves.

sights.name: Ushio Shrine
sights.description: Ancient shrine enshrining deities from Izumo Taisha since 792, with fine hall carvings, a 1,000-year-old sacred cedar, and a designated Noh stage.

sights.name: Uga Shrine
sights.description: A shrine on a conical hill above the Ryobi coast in Sado, dedicated to Ukanomitama, a deity of food.

sights.name: Senkaku Bay
sights.description: Collective name for five small Sado bays over about 3 km, with cliffs around 30 meters, likened to Norway’s Hardangerfjord.

sights.name: Sea Town Shopping Street
sights.description: A shopping street connected to Sado Kisen Ryotsu Terminal, offering local sake, seafood, sweets, crafts, and limited buri curry.

sights.name: Tassha Beach
sights.description: A swimming beach in a quiet inlet of Senkaku Bay, about ten minutes by car from Aikawa, and relatively calm even on rough days.

sights.name: Nyu Saki Beach
sights.description: Beach in Sado, Niigata.

sights.name: Donden Mountain
sights.description: Formally Tadara Peak, this gentle plateau of three 900-meter peaks in the Osado Mountains is known for alpine plants and spring trekking.

sights.name: Jinmen-iwa (Human Face Rock)
sights.description: A greenish andesite rock about 10 meters high on Koshi-no-Nagahama resembles a human profile and is a popular photo spot with Mano Bay behind it.

sights.name: Hiyoshi Shrine
sights.description: Shrine locally known as Sanno-san, founded in 1226 for exiled Emperor Juntoku and noted for its monkey statues and three-day April festival.

sights.name: Shiizaki Suwa Shrine
sights.description: A branch of Suwa Taisha founded in 1376 on a hill overlooking Lake Kamo, with a 1902 Noh stage for firelight Noh and visitor practice.

sights.name: Yajima Experience Exchange Center
sights.description: Exchange center at the back of an inlet overlooking Yajima and Kyojima, where visitors can board tub boats.

sights.name: Akagame and Kazeshima Seaside Park
sights.name_ja: 赤亀・風島なぎさ公園
sights.description: A seaside park and campsite between Akagame Rock and Kazeshima Benten on the Maehama coast in Sado, with a swimming beach and year-round toilets.

sights.name: Meoto Iwa
sights.description: Two rocks on Nanaura Coast, 22.6 m and 23.1 m high, linked to the Kojiki land-creation myth and said to be a husband and wife.

sights.name: Rikiya Tarai-bune Sightseeing Boats
sights.name_ja: たらい舟力屋観光汽船
sights.description: Women skippers steer traditional tarai-bune tub boats; motorboat rides and a Sado-style Blue Cave cruise are also offered.

sights.name: Mano Park
sights.description: Park centered on the area where exiled Emperor Juntoku spent 22 years, with about 2,000 cherry trees in mid-April.

sights.name: Kodo Summer Performance
sights.name_ja: 目の前で鼓童演奏が見られる！鼓童夏の公演鑑賞
sights.description: A 45-minute Kodo taiko performance at Aiport Sado, a five-minute walk from Ryotsu Port, with talks and a hands-on segment.

sights.name: Toki Terrace
sights.description: Facility on Sado for observing wild crested ibises, with indoor exhibits, telescopes, and rooftop views of Mount Kinpoku and the Kuninaka Plain.

sights.name: Hajikizaki Lighthouse
sights.description: An octagonal lighthouse at Hajikizaki, Sado’s northern tip, built in 1919 and known as a setting of the film Times of Joy and Sorrow.

sights.name: Sado Dairy
sights.description: A Sado dairy processing milk collected each morning; visitors can watch milk packing and pudding and yogurt production for about 30 minutes.

sights.name: Sado Kokubunji Temple
sights.description: Temple on Sado whose present buildings stand to the east and date from the early Edo period, housing a wooden Yakushi Nyorai Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Suhama Beach
sights.description: A 4 km sandy beach on Sado with clear, shallow water, away from town, beside a free campsite and bungalow village.

sights.name: Nagate Cape
sights.description: A flat-rock cape at the center of Nanaura Coast in Sado-Yahiko-Yoneyama Quasi-National Park, popular for swimming, snorkeling, fishing, and sunsets.

sights.name: Jogahama Beach
sights.description: A 150-meter-wide artificial beach in Akadomari with clear swimming water and white sand, beside Sunrise Jogahama, a lodging with a day-use hot spring.

sights.name: Akagame and Kazeshima Nagisa Park Beach
sights.name_en: Akagame and Kazeshima Nagisa Park Beach
sights.name_ja: 赤亀・風島なぎさ公園海水浴場
sights.description: A swimming beach in a scenic park on Sado’s Maehama coast, with Kazeshima Benten and Akagame Rock, clear water, a gravel shore, and lawn campsites.

sights.name: Dairenji Temple
sights.description: Sōtō Zen temple founded in 1421 as the Honma clan’s family temple, with a gate moved from fallen Hamochi Castle.

sights.name: Auto Park Sawata
sights.description: Campsite about ten minutes by car from Sawata, in forest with views of Mount Kinpoku and the Kuninaka Plain, with powered sites and parking.

sights.name: Hasedera Temple
sights.description: Sado temple modeled on Yamato's Hasedera, founded in 807 by Kobo Daishi, holding three Important Cultural Property Eleven-faced Kannon statues.

sights.name: Hakuundai Exchange Center
sights.name_ja: 交流センター 白雲台
sights.description: A mountain-lodge-style building at about 850 m with a deck overlooking Ryotsu Bay, the Kuninaka Plain and Ogi Peninsula; closed in winter.

sights.name: Ogawa Sunflower Field
sights.description: Sunflower field in Ogawa, Sado, beside the road toward Senkaku Bay, with blooms set against the sea in early to mid-August.

sights.name: Aikawa Skills Heritage Exhibition Hall
sights.description: Hands-on facility in Aikawa teaching Mumyoi-yaki pottery using gold-mine clay and sakiori weaving, with displays of local crafts and Bun'ya dolls.

sights.name: Shohoji Temple
sights.description: Temple founded in 1324 as the Honma family temple, known as Zeami's place of exile, with the prefecture's oldest mask and June candlelight Noh.

sights.name: Chikobo Temple
sights.description: Shingon Buddhist temple founded in 808, noted for its carvings and a stop on the Sado Seven Lucky Gods pilgrimage.

sights.name: Hagi Great Mulberry Tree
sights.description: A mountain mulberry on Sado, about 1,300 years old and nine meters tall, counted as one of Japan’s three noted mulberry trees.

sights.name: Mano Imperial Mausoleum
sights.description: Cremation mound of Emperor Juntoku, who died in exile on Sado in 1242; managed by the Imperial Household Agency.

sights.name: Ogi Gosho Cherry Trees
sights.description: Two satozakura trees at Kaichō-ji Temple in Ogi, said to have been planted by Retired Emperor Juntoku, bear white blossoms with irregularly split petal tips.

sights.name: Himesaki Lighthouse
sights.description: Iron lighthouse on Sado, first lit in 1895 and selected for the World's 100 Historic Lighthouses.

sights.name: Sashu Oyari Hall (Aikawa Tourism Exchange Center)
sights.name_en: Sashu Oyari Hall (Aikawa Tourism Exchange Center)
sights.name_ja: 佐州おーやり館（相川観光交流センター）
sights.description: Walking-tour hub in Aikawa renovated from traditional Sashu-kan inn, with a rest room, exhibition space, and simple lodging for students.

sights.name: Sado Great Bronze Statue of Nichiren Shonin
sights.name_en: Sado Great Bronze Statue of Nichiren Shonin
sights.description: A bronze statue of Nichiren, about 13 m tall (26 m with pedestal), built by over 3,000 priests and believers for the 750th anniversary of the Nichiren sect, facing India.

sights.name: Sado Print Village Art Museum
sights.description: The museum, in the former Aikawa Summary Court, displays about 300 works by Shinichi Takahashi and local amateur artists and offers printmaking classes.

sights.name: Jissoji Temple
sights.description: Temple where Nichiren is said to have chanted each morning, with a bronze statue and a cedar over 1,000 years old.

sights.name: Shiroyama Park
sights.description: Hilltop park in Ogi overlooking the sea, with walking paths, a lookout, an Ozaki Kōyō haiku monument, and about 3,000 camellias.

sights.name: Kyomachi Street
sights.description: Main street in Aikawa connecting the gold and silver mines with the magistrate's office, retaining narrow lanes from the former mining town.

sights.name: Tassha Coast
sights.description: Calm coastal inlet on Sado near Senkaku Bay, a swimming beach linked to the Sansho Dayu reunion and Meyarai Jizo.

sights.name: Fusube Village
sights.description: Lodging building of the Fusube Village experience facility in Kotomari, with a kitchen, dining area and beds for five, plus pottery, weaving and bamboo crafts.

sights.name: Kodomari Hakusan Shrine Noh Stage and Millstone Mound
sights.name_en: Kodomari Hakusan Shrine Noh Stage and Millstone Mound
sights.name_ja: 小泊白山神社能舞台と石臼塚
sights.description: Pre-Meiji Noh stage at Kodomari Hakusan Shrine in Hamochi, Sado, beside a mound of millstones collected and dedicated in 1977.

sights.name: 404 Not Found
sights.description: No listing details are available for this page.

sights.name: Takei Kumano Shrine
sights.description: A village shrine in a cedar forest whose 1869 Noh stage, a prefectural tangible folk cultural property, has a tiled roof, hashigakari bridge, and carved beam brackets.

sights.name: Keikyuji Temple
sights.description: Shingon temple founded in 807 and a Sado Seven Lucky Gods stop; its Eight Patriarchs Hall is a prefectural tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Aikawa Local History Museum
sights.description: Museum in the former Imperial Property Bureau Sado branch, a national historic site with gold-mine and folk exhibits.

sights.name: Hydrangeas at Rengeho-ji Temple
sights.description: Ancient Shingon temple on Sado, said to have been founded by Kobo Daishi, where 7,000 hydrangeas bloom from late June to early July.

sights.name: SADO PORT LOUNGE
sights.description: A coworking space on Sado using reclaimed local timber, with plans from 30 minutes, business supplies, and sea and mountain views.

sights.name: Freeway Diving Shop & School (Sado)
sights.name_ja: ダイビングショップ＆スクール フリーウェイ 佐渡店
sights.description: A diving shop in Sawata, central Sado, offering PADI courses in three to four days and guided dives for beginners through experienced divers.

sights.name: Sado Museum
sights.description: Art museum on Sado showing sketches by Tsuchida Bakusen, gold and silver mine displays, and a garden with rocks and old folk houses.

sights.name: Mount Kinpoku (Kurigasawa Trailhead)
sights.name_ja: 金北山・栗ヶ沢登山口
sights.description: A 1,172 m peak on Sado renamed in 1601 after the gold mine’s discovery, with a summit shrine and seasonal wildflowers.

sights.name: Sawazaki-hana Lighthouse
sights.description: Lighthouse at the tip of Ogi Peninsula on Sado, first lit in 1928; the present tower, built in 1987, exceeds 24.2 metres.

sights.name: Tsurushi Silver Mine
sights.description: Silver mine ruins in the Sawane mountains of Sado, discovered in 1542, with more than 600 mining traces.

sights.name: Kita Ikki's Grave
sights.description: Grave of Kita Ikki, a thinker and social activist of the Meiji to early Showa eras, at Shoko-ji Aoyama Cemetery overlooking rice fields.

sights.name: Tsugami Shrine
sights.description: Tsugami Shrine in Okawa enshrines the Sumiyoshi sea gods for Kitamaebune voyage safety and business prosperity.

sights.name: Ogi Diving Center Clubhouse
sights.name_ja: 小木ダイビングセンター・クラブハウス
sights.description: A divers' clubhouse on the clear Kotoura inlet, a one-minute walk from departure boats, with nearby cave walks and the Ogi no Yu hot spring.

sights.name: Lake Kamo
sights.description: Niigata’s largest lake, about 17 km around, now brackish, with shoreline paths and oyster farming since 1932.

sights.name: Futatsugame Adonis Flowers
sights.description: Near Futatsugame in Sado's Negai district, clusters of wild adonis can be seen along the road without climbing the mountain.

sights.name: Mourazaki Park
sights.description: A park on northern Sado Island overlooking the Sea of Japan, with orange rock lilies from late May to early June and a shrine for sea safety.

sights.name: Lake Kamo Night Kayak
sights.name_ja: 幻想的な星影ナイトクルーズへ・・・加茂湖ナイトカヤック
sights.description: Night kayaking on Sado's Lake Kamo departs Kamoko Boathouse near Ryotsu Port, with Osado mountain views and stars on clear nights.

sights.name: Sawazaki Coast
sights.description: Sawazaki Coast on Sado has pillow lava from a submarine eruption, a lighthouse above the rocks, and tarai-boat fishing.

sights.name: Oumedo Sacred Trees (Wisteria and Plum)
sights.name_ja: 御梅堂の霊木 藤・梅
sights.description: Sacred wisteria and plum trees at Oumedo in Ogura, Sado; the wisteria trunk measures 230 cm, and the plum is traditionally linked to Nichiren.

sights.name: Nichiren Shonin Wave Daimoku Monument
sights.description: A monument at Maura no Tsu, where Nichiren set sail after his pardon, marking the legend that Namu Myoho Renge Kyo rose from the waves.

sights.name: Ryotsu Catholic Church
sights.description: Catholic church in Ryotsu, founded in 1879 by a French missionary and rebuilt in 1887 after a fire to a design by Father Papino.

sights.name: F.WAVE Diving Service
sights.name_ja: ダイビングサービス F.WAVE
sights.description: A diving service guiding visitors to points suited to daily sea conditions, plus Osado mountain trekking, lessons, eco-tours, and gear rental.

sights.name: Sankyo Pond
sights.description: A densely wooded pond near Komyobutsu-ji Temple on Sado, 500 meters around, that can be circled on a walking path.

sights.name: Murasame Pine
sights.description: A 19-metre pine, a Niigata Prefecture natural monument, stands on the Sado Coast Guard grounds and was once a landmark for ships at sea.

sights.name: Konponji Temple
sights.description: Nichiren sacred site where Nichiren is said to have written the Kaimoku-shō at Sanmaidō; 29 halls stand across its grounds.

sights.name: Dai Sado Nature Hodo
sights.description: Nature site in Sado, Niigata.

sights.name: Iwayayama Stone Cave
sights.description: Cave site in Shukunegi, Sado, where early Jomon pottery was found and later cliff-carved Buddhas and stone statues are enshrined.

sights.name: Lake Kamo Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: Cherry blossoms at Lake Kamo in Ryotsu, Sado, a brackish lake joined to the sea in 1903 and known for oysters.

sights.name: Donden Mountain (Tsubaki Trailhead)
sights.name_ja: ドンデン山・椿登山口
sights.description: Rounded peak in Sado’s Osado range, with a beginner trail from Tsubaki to highland turf meadows, rhododendrons, and a mountain hut.

sights.name: Soja Shrine Noh Stage
sights.description: Noh stage at Soja Shrine in Yoshioka, thought to date from the mid-Meiji period, with a Sado-style layout and city cultural-property designation.

sights.name: Daianji Temple
sights.description: Temple in Aikawa founded in 1606 by Sado's first magistrate Okubo Nagayasu, with national historic-site towers and a city-designated tabu forest.

sights.name: Mearai Jizo
sights.description: Jizo enshrined beside a spring at Tassha on Sado, said to have restored a mother's eyesight in the Sansho Dayu legend.

sights.name: Hachiman Wakamiya Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Ryotsu Minato, locally called Wakamiya-san, that holds the Minato Festival each May 5 with fishing flags and a mikoshi procession.

sights.name: Shimogokufu Ruins
sights.description: Square national historic site near Takeda Bridge, with a double moat and remains of two pillar buildings, backed by the Osado mountains.

sights.name: Dainichido Hall
sights.description: Worship hall of Ōhirume Shrine, said to have been rebuilt in 1718, housing a seated Dainichi Nyorai and revered as a guardian of cattle.

sights.name: Kasuga Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Aikawa founded in 1605 by Okubo Nagayasu, with a Noh stage hosting takigi Noh several times a year.

sights.name: Mumyoi-yaki Gyokudo Kiln
sights.name_ja: 無名異焼 玉堂窯元
sights.description: Gallery and shop of Gyokudo Kiln on Route 350, with paid Mumyoi-yaki pottery experiences on the wheel or by hand-carving.

sights.name: Mano Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Sado enshrining Emperor Juntoku and keeping a short sword, inkstone, fan and vase said to be his belongings.

sights.name: Tōkō-ji Temple
sights.description: Sōtō Zen temple on Sado founded in 1382, the eighth stop of the Sado Shikoku pilgrimage, with Six Jizō board paintings by Kanō Banyū.

sights.name: Kofuku Jizo
sights.description: A white Jizo statue 17.5 m tall including its base, completed in 1983, is visible from afar against Mount Togami's green foothills.

sights.name: Niibo Dam Lake
sights.description: An agricultural dam on the upper Kokufu River, with about 20 varieties and 1,500 cherry trees plus early-summer azaleas along the shore.

sights.name: Kirarium Sado (Sado Gold and Silver Mine Guidance Facility)
sights.name_en: Kirarium Sado (Sado Gold and Silver Mine Guidance Facility)
sights.name_ja: 佐渡金銀山ガイダンス施設「きらりうむ佐渡」
sights.description: Information hub and gateway for the Sado Gold and Silver Mine, introducing it through videos and historical scrolls and providing walking guides.

sights.name: Shukunegi Hangiri (Tub Boat Cruise)
sights.description: A slow eco cruise in handmade cedar-and-bamboo tub boats past Shukunegi's Edo-like streets and rocky coast.

sights.name: Mano Tourist Center
sights.description: A Sado specialty shop beside Mano Imperial Mausoleum that displays akadama stone and has a cafe overlooking Osado and Mano Bay.

sights.name: Hojo-bo Edohigan
sights.description: Giant Edohigan cherry, said to be 250–260 years old, beside a thatched building at the former Hojo-bo site in Sado.

sights.name: Nami no Hana (Wave Flowers)
sights.description: White sea foam that forms when plankton-rich waves strike rocks, often seen along Sado’s Sotokaifu coast and Mano Bay.

sights.name: Torigoe Library
sights.description: Library in Sado’s Saruhachi district with about 20,000 books donated by classical performing-arts scholar Torigoe Bunzo, open for free browsing.

sights.name: Sadokoku Ogi Folk Museum and Sengokubune Exhibition Hall
sights.name_en: Sadokoku Ogi Folk Museum and Sengokubune Exhibition Hall
sights.name_ja: 佐渡国小木民俗博物館・千石船展示館
sights.description: Museum in the former Shukunegi school building displaying about 30,000 folk items and the restored 1858 ship Hakusan Maru, beside the preserved village.

sights.name: Mount Kinpoku (Sawaguchi Trailhead)
sights.description: Intermediate trailhead for Mount Kinpoku (1,172 m) on Sado; the summit shrine is about 2.5 hours up, with seasonal wildflowers along the path.

sights.name: Honkoji Temple (Miyakawa)
sights.description: Nichiren temple in Miyakawa opened by Nichigyo Shonin, with the Pardon Stone where Nichiren sat and the pine where he hung his robe.

sights.name: Myoshoji Temple
sights.description: Nichiren Buddhist temple on Sado where the saint lived about two and a half years until his pardon in 1274.

sights.name: Ishina Seisui-ji Temple
sights.description: Ancient temple in Ishina, Sado, said to have been founded in 807, with sacred spring water and a city-designated ginkgo.

sights.name: Chobokuri (Soba Restaurant)
sights.description: Year-round soba restaurant in Osaki, Hamochi, opened in 2007 by the Osaki Soba Association, serving 100% stone-milled soba and ago-dashi bukkake soba.

sights.name: Hojo Family Residence
sights.description: Edo-period residence of the Hojo family of Chinese-medicine doctors, with a thatched main house designated an Important Cultural Property and thought to date from the late 18th century.

sights.name: Choanji Temple
sights.description: Kuchikawachi temple said to date from 831, keeping a late-Heian wooden Amida and Niigata’s only Korean bell, both National Important Cultural Properties.

sights.name: Sado Kokubunji Temple Ruins
sights.description: Ruins of a provincial temple completed in 764 under Emperor Shomu’s edict, with foundation stones of the main hall, corridors, gates, and pagoda still visible.

sights.name: Kamo Shrine Noh Stage
sights.description: Independent Noh stage behind Kamo Shrine on Sado, one of four historic Kuninaka Noh sites, with night performances in August.

sights.name: Kotoura Cave (Ryuo Cave) High-Speed Motorboat Tour
sights.name_en: Kotoura Cave (Ryuo Cave) High-Speed Motorboat Tour
sights.name_ja: 青の洞窟を高速モーターボートで行く！琴浦洞窟 (竜王洞) めぐり
sights.description: High-speed motorboat tour of geopark-designated Ogi Peninsula scenery, including Sahachimonji and Kotoura Cave, also called the Blue Cave.

sights.name: Kuaterume Sado
sights.description: Hot-spring facility on Sado partly using a German spa system, with bubble, jet and reclining baths and free-flowing natural spring water amid greenery.

sights.name: Nana Kiteya Mano
sights.description: A shop in Mano, Sado selling freshly picked produce, apple juice, cakes, and local sweets.

sights.name: Retired Emperor Juntoku Stone Monuments
sights.description: Four monuments stand at Koigoura, the reputed landing place of Retired Emperor Juntoku, with Mano Bay and the Osado range behind them.

sights.name: Kuroki Gosho Site
sights.description: Site of the temporary palace of Retired Emperor Juntoku, exiled to Sado after the 1221 Jokyu War, with pines and poetry monuments.

sights.name: Hori Kinen Kanai Nogakudo
sights.description: Sightseeing place in Sado, Niigata.

sights.name: Honkoji Temple (Izumi)
sights.description: Temple founded in 1310 near the Kuroki Imperial Palace site, housing a wooden standing Sho Kannon statue designated a national important cultural property.

sights.name: Sugi Pond
sights.description: A spring-fed pond near a 440-metre pass on Sado, ringed by large cedars and paired with Hyotan Pond.

sights.name: Donden Plateau
sights.description: Former cattle-grazing grassland on Mt. Donden where alpine plants grow at about 900 meters, with star-filled skies at night.

sights.name: Aikawa Fureai Historical Walking Tour
sights.name_ja: 相川ふれあいガイドと歩く！相川ふれあい歴史散策
sights.description: A guided walking tour of historic Aikawa, from the Sado Magistrate's Office through old streets to the Kitazawa flotation plant ruins, without entering facilities.

sights.name: Straw Pot Mat Making and Kobiri Plan
sights.name_en: Straw Pot Mat Making and Kobiri Plan
sights.name_ja: 昔ながらの手しごとといっぷく。カフェで過ごす藁鍋敷き作りとゆったり『こびり』プラン
sights.description: At Oni Café near Ryotsu Port on Sado, make a straw pot mat, then relax over a kobiri snack with onikin waffles.

sights.name: Tenryohai Sake Brewery
sights.description: A sake brewery about seven minutes by car from Ryotsu Port, brewing with Mount Kinpoku underground water and Sado rice, with free tours by reservation from April to December.

sights.name: Niibo History and Folklore Museum
sights.description: Museum in Niibo displaying Sado history, folk tools, crested ibis materials, archaeological finds, and works by artists linked to the area.

sights.name: Akadomari Local History Museum
sights.description: Local history museum in Akadomari General Cultural Hall, with Sado festival displays including Onidaiko, Akadomari folk materials, and a corner on writer Hasegawa Kaitaro.

sights.name: Saruhachi Rice Terraces
sights.description: Rice terraces in remote Saruhachi, Sado, among remaining thatched-roof houses, irrigated by stream water from 636-meter Kyozukayama.

sights.name: Kitakatahe Rice Terraces
sights.description: Rice terraces line a sea-breeze coastal terrace in Kitakatahe, Sado, home of the Crane Wife tale that roots The Grateful Crane.

sights.name: Ninomiya Shrine
sights.description: Shrine enshrining Retired Emperor Juntoku's daughter, with a thatched Noh stage and the Iris Hall on a former temporary-palace site.

sights.name: Shokoji Temple
sights.description: Old Ji-sect temple in Shukunegi, founded in 1349 as Sado's first, whose 1717 gate is the village's oldest building.

sights.name: Otowa Pond
sights.description: Natural pond and prefectural natural monument in beech and mizunara forest near the Osado Skyline, with a high-moor floating island of over 20 plant species.

sights.name: Ogi Coast
sights.description: A roughly 16 km volcanic coastline on Sado, a national natural monument and Place of Scenic Beauty, also known for tub-boat seaweed fishing.

sights.name: Three Cedars of Hase
sights.description: Three giant cedars, each over 500 years old and about 50 meters tall, stand beside the Kannon Hall at Hasedera Temple.

sights.name: Primeval Forest and Giant Cedar Trekking Senjusugi Route
sights.name_en: Primeval Forest and Giant Cedar Trekking Senjusugi Route
sights.name_ja: 神秘の大自然！原生林と杉巨木群トレッキング～千手杉ルート～
sights.description: Trek through Sado’s mossy old-growth forest and giant cedars on the Senjusugi route, suited to beginners, children, and older visitors.

sights.name: Primeval Forest Trekking Uchikaifu Route
sights.name_ja: 原生林トレッキング～内海府ルート～
sights.description: Guided trek on Sado’s Uchikaifu route through giant-cedar old-growth forest, limited to 15 people a day aged junior high and above.

sights.name: Japanese Crested Ibis
sights.description: Japanese crested ibises are usually seen foraging in rice paddies on Sado’s Kuninaka Plain, especially in groups after the October harvest.

sights.name: Ogi Specialty Products Development Center
sights.name_ja: 小木特産品開発センター
sights.description: A year-round shop in Ogi, Sado, selling local produce, seafood and sweets made from pesticide-free sweet potatoes, with nationwide shipping.

sights.name: Sado Daikannon Showa Hall
sights.name_ja: 佐渡大観音 昭和殿
sights.description: Group of more than 220 Buddhist statues in Sado, centered on a 1970 eleven-faced Kannon over 7 meters tall, carved from one 2,200-year-old cypress.

sights.name: Yokoyama Trailhead (Mount Kinpoku)
sights.description: Yokoyama trailhead for 1,172 m Mount Kinpoku on Sado, about 3 hours 15 minutes to the summit for intermediate hikers.

sights.name: Yorankasha (Fresh Produce Market)
sights.name_ja: 新鮮空間 よらんか舎
sights.description: Direct-sales shop in central Sado offering daily local vegetables, Sado processed foods, and an eat-in corner.

sights.name: Millstone Mound
sights.description: In 1977, household millstones were gathered and dedicated at Hakusan Shrine in Hamochi, a district once known for stonemasons.

sights.name: British Aircraft Landing Memorial Tower
sights.description: A stone monument in front of Takachi Elementary and Junior High School commemorates the 1946 emergency landing of a British Dakota and a runway built with local villagers.

sights.name: Odate Vertical Shaft
sights.description: A vertical mine shaft with an underground elevator, completed in 1877 by German engineers, reaching 352 metres and used until mining ended in 1989.

sights.name: Niibo Silver Mine
sights.description: Silver mine in Niibo, Sado, also called Takizawa Silver Mine, where Edo-period records survive and old mine tunnels remain.

sights.name: Bronze Bell (Jinguji Temple)
sights.description: An 83 cm, 187 kg Japanese temple bell at Jinguji, cast in 1295 and later moved from Shokoji after that temple closed.

sights.name: Japan Amateur Masterpiece Art Museum
sights.name_ja: 日本アマチュア秀作美術館
sights.description: Art museum attached to Ogi Library that shows only amateur artists' works, including paintings by Winston Churchill, Toshiki Kaifu, and Natsume Soseki.

sights.name: Toki-no-Sato Golf Club
sights.name_ja: ときの郷ゴルフクラブ
sights.description: Sado’s only 18-hole golf course, in the Kosado hills, with Mano Bay views from the outbound holes.

sights.name: Beach Riding (Seaside Horseback Experience)
sights.name_ja: Beach Riding 海で乗馬体験！
sights.description: Staff lead horseback walks along the Sado shore for beginners, with summer sunset rides recommended from about 5 p.m.

sights.name: Kakiya Miura Oyster Cuisine Plan
sights.name_ja: 両津港から徒歩圏内！ぷりっぷりの加茂湖の牡蠣を炭火焼きで存分に味わう かき家みうらさんの牡蠣料理プラン
sights.description: Oyster dining plan at Kakiya Miura, a 15-minute walk from Ryotsu Port, with charcoal-grilled Lake Kamo oysters and other oyster dishes.

sights.name: Stylish Lake Kamo Oyster Cafe
sights.name_ja: 加茂湖を一望できるオシャレなカフェで牡蠣料理のフルコースを召し上がれ♪
sights.description: caMoco Café Koasobi, five minutes by car from Ryotsu Port, serves a full course of Lake Kamo oysters that mature in one year.

sights.name: Crab Set Meal and Observation Bath Set
sights.name_en: Crab Set Meal and Observation Bath Set
sights.name_ja: ”ととのう”極上体験！カニ御膳 × 展望風呂の贅沢セット
sights.description: A meal-and-bath plan on Sado with a red snow crab set lunch, limited to 12 a day, plus a Japan Sea view bath and sauna.

sights.name: Osado Ishina Natural Cedars
sights.description: Natural cedars, some over 300 years old and shaped by wind and fog, line a 650 m trail near 900 m elevation.

sights.name: Former Tanabe Residence
sights.description: Former residence of Tanabe Kurohei in Akadomari, who funded the rebuilding of Akadomari Port after making a fortune in Hokkaido.

sights.name: Anju Mound (Shikanoura)
sights.description: Anju's mound at Shikanoura in Sotokaifu, Sado, is said to mark where she died after reuniting with her mother, in a rice field by the sea.

sights.name: Akagame Rock
sights.description: A red iron-quartz rock with a hollow center, seen from Akagame-Kazeshima Nagisa Park beach and said to look like nestling turtles.

sights.name: Kuratani Giant Straw Sandals
sights.description: Giant straw sandals, about one metre wide and 1.8 metres long, are hung each March along Route 350 in Okuratani as roadside deities against misfortune.

sights.name: Jishoro Time Bell Tower
sights.description: A time-bell tower in Aikawa whose bell, cast from Sado copper in 1712, once told the hour and is rung again morning and evening.

sights.name: Anyoji Haguro Shrine
sights.description: A shrine said to have been transferred from Dewa’s Haguro Shrine in 772, set among giant cedars and holding Sado’s smallest Noh stage.

sights.name: Hirane Saki no Hashoku Oketsu Gun
sights.description: Sightseeing spot in Sado, Niigata.

sights.name: Kokeume Plum Tree at Shinpo-in Temple
sights.name_en: Kokeume Plum Tree at Shinpo-in Temple
sights.description: A large plum tree at Shinpo-in Temple on Sado, traditionally planted by Emperor Juntoku, with flowers emerging from moss on the trunk.

sights.name: Shironoyama Park
sights.description: Hilltop park with late-Sengoku castle ruins and a folktale exhibition hall, whose fifth-floor room looks over Akadomari Port and the Echigo mountains.

sights.name: Nabekura Falls at Shinzenji Temple
sights.description: Historic falls at Shinzenji Temple where exiled monk Mongaku practiced austerities, near a stone Fudo Myoo he is said to have carved.

sights.name: Mushizaki Beach Snorkeling (Easy 2-Hour Course)
sights.name_ja: 両津港から車で30分！虫崎ビーチで「スノーケリング」お気軽2時間コース
sights.description: A two-hour guided snorkeling course at clear Mushizaki Beach, 30 minutes by car from Ryotsu Port, with gear rental included.

sights.name: Yahata Tulip Fields
sights.description: Tulip-growing area in the dunes of Yahata, Sado, where 500,000 tulips bloom among pine trees.

sights.name: Nanban Shrimp Meal and Scenic Bath Set
sights.name_en: Nanban Shrimp Meal and Scenic Bath Set
sights.name_ja: ”ととのう”極上体験！南蛮エビ御膳 × 展望風呂の贅沢セット
sights.description: A lunch-and-bath set with a Sado nanban shrimp meal limited to 12 servings a day, plus a Sea of Japan view bath and sauna.

sights.name: Lake Kamo Cycling Course
sights.name_ja: 加茂湖サイクリングコース
sights.description: A 17.7 km cycling course that circles Lake Kamo, starting and ending at Ryotsu Port.

sights.name: Koumaru Exhibition Hall
sights.description: Exhibition hall in Ogi displaying Koumaru, a Japanese cargo ship that carried goods across the Sado Strait until 1961.

sights.name: Mount Donden, Kita-Ikarigoe Trailhead
sights.name_ja: ドンデン山・北五十里登山口
sights.description: Beginner trailhead for Mount Donden on Sado, about three hours to the summit from April to November, with a mountain hut.

sights.name: Konosehana Lighthouse
sights.description: A lighthouse on Konose Cape, Sado’s nearest point to Echigo, standing in Matsugazaki History Park and first lit in 1952.

sights.name: Jogahana Lighthouse
sights.description: A small lighthouse about 11 metres tall on Jogahana Cape in Noura, Sado, first lit in 1966 and reached by a short footpath.

sights.name: Zencho-ji Temple
sights.description: Shingon temple on high ground behind Akadomari Port, said to date from around 827, with a Kannon image shown once every 33 years.

sights.name: Ogura Senmaida
sights.description: Sightseeing spot in Sado, Niigata.

sights.name: Himesaki Lighthouse Hall
sights.description: White iron lighthouse on Himesaki cliff at Ryotsu Port’s entrance, lit since 1895 and still in its original form, with a campground and paths nearby.

sights.name: Ishina Seisui-ji Temple
sights.description: Temple in Sado housing two early Buddha statues carved by Mokujiki Shonin in 1782, including Yakushi Nyorai and Jizo Bosatsu.

sights.name: Kinbura Free Pass with Koban-Making Experience
sights.name_en: Kinbura Free Pass with Koban-Making Experience
sights.name_ja: 世界遺産関連施設をお得にまわる「金ぶらフリーパス」＆小判作り体験付き
sights.description: A two-day pass for Kirarium Sado and the Sado Gold Mine historic site, including a koban-making experience.

sights.name: Kendo Spirit and Shinai Craftsman
sights.name_ja: 剣道の精神世界に触れる 竹刀職人の技を学ぶ
sights.description: Observe part of shinai making by a Sado craftsman, one of about ten left in Japan, and practice basic kendo etiquette.

sights.name: Honma Family Noh Stage
sights.description: Rebuilt in 1885, the Honma family’s tiled Noh stage on Sado has acoustic jars under the floor and hosts an annual performance in late July.

sights.name: Mount Donden, Ishibana Trailhead
sights.name_ja: ドンデン山・石花登山口
sights.description: Intermediate trailhead for 934 m Mount Donden on Sado, about five hours to the summit across turf grassland with rhododendrons and azaleas.

sights.name: Shizume Ichizaemon's Grave
sights.description: Grave built in 1845 for Shizume Ichizaemon, a Sado magistrate who worked to revive the gold and silver mines, beside Benkei's Scissors Rock.

sights.name: Sadokaze Shiogama Salt Workshop
sights.name_ja: 塩工房 佐渡風塩釜
sights.description: Salt-making workshop facing Meoto Iwa on Nanaura Coast, boiling local seawater over firewood by traditional methods; visitors can watch the process.

sights.name: Ryotsu Okawa (Outdoor Print Village)
sights.description: A settlement of about 50 homes stretching 2.5 km, known for local prints of daily life on house walls.

sights.name: Sado Folk Craft Museum
sights.description: Museum in a Meiji merchant house showing Sado crafts, armor, clocks, and antique ceramics carried by kitamaebune ships.

sights.name: Sesonji Temple
sights.description: Ancient temple with a green garden; six halls are nationally registered cultural properties, and it is a Sado Seven Lucky Gods site.

sights.name: Ishidaki no Ume
sights.description: A plum tree said to be over 750 years old clasps a large stone at its base and blooms pale pink around mid-March near Mano Imperial Mausoleum.

sights.name: Hase Koya-maki (Japanese Umbrella Pine)
sights.description: A Japanese umbrella pine over 400 years old and 40 meters tall stands in the garden just inside Hasedera Temple’s gate.

sights.name: Ninomiya Shrine Noh Stage
sights.description: An independent Noh stage at Ninomiya Shrine, already noted in an 1863 record, has hosted takigi Noh since 2003.

sights.name: Cherry Blossoms around Mount Myoken
sights.description: A plaza at 890 m in Sado’s Osado mountains holds the snow-spread Senryu mountain cherry, plus katakuri, orange azaleas, and autumn foliage.

sights.name: Mushizaki Snorkeling and Sea Kayaking (Full-Day Plan)
sights.name_en: Mushizaki Snorkeling and Sea Kayaking (Full-Day Plan)
sights.name_ja: 両津港から車で30分！虫崎で「スノーケリング」＋「シーカヤック」1日満喫プラン
sights.description: A full-day snorkeling and sea kayaking plan at clear Mushizaki Beach, 30 minutes by car from Ryotsu Port, with rental gear and a guide.

sights.name: Katanoo Rice Terraces
sights.description: Rice terraces overlooking the sea in mountainous Katanoo, Sado, where the last wild Japanese crested ibis lived.

sights.name: Himegasawa Trailhead (Mount Kinpoku)
sights.name_ja: 金北山・姫ヶ沢登山口
sights.description: Himegasawa trailhead for 1,172 m Mount Kinpoku on Sado, about 2 hours 35 minutes to the summit shrine for intermediate hikers.

sights.name: Geppōse Rice Terraces
sights.description: Rice terraces in Geppōse, Sado, where scattered small paddies called hidden fields are irrigated by seven streams and springs and tended with help from off-island volunteers.

sights.name: Sado Osaki Lighthouse
sights.description: Lighthouse in the Senkakuwan Ageshima Yuen grounds, first lit in 1964, just before the Your Name filming site Machiko Bridge.

sights.name: Mushukunin Grave Monument
sights.description: A mountain gravestone inscribed with the origins, Buddhist names, names, and ages of 28 unregistered workers who died underground in 1853.

sights.name: Kobuse Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Nishimikawa, said to have been founded in the Muromachi period, where rites are performed toward the sacred Mikeishi stone.

sights.name: Gosho Cherry at Kaichoji Temple
sights.description: Satozakura at Kaichoji Temple, traditionally said to have been planted by Emperor Juntoku, blooming in mixed white flowers from late April to early May.

sights.name: Mumyoi Ware
sights.description: Sado pottery made from gold-mine iron oxide and Sawane clay is very hard, rings clearly when struck, and grows glossier with use.

sights.name: Island Mirage Special Plan (Sado Gold Mine)
sights.name_en: Island Mirage Special Plan (Sado Gold Mine)
sights.name_ja: 最先端技術 × 佐渡金銀山 佐渡金山の坑道を歩くアトラクション体験！お得なアイランドミラージュ特別プラン
sights.description: Walk-through in the Sado Gold Mine’s Doyu Tunnel using MR glasses and projection mapping, plus Sodayu Tunnel entry and gold-leaf soft serve or coffee.

sights.name: Sado Private Sightseeing Taxi (3-Hour / 5-Hour Plans)
sights.name_ja: 佐渡をたっぷり満喫！おまかせ観光タクシー貸切３時間
sights.description: A private sightseeing taxi charter on Sado for three or five hours, led by drivers who know the island and its recommended spots.

sights.name: Site of Japan's Last Crested Ibis Feeding
sights.name_en: Site of Japan's Last Crested Ibis Feeding
sights.name_ja: 日本最後のトキ餌付けの地
sights.description: A stone monument in Nishimikawa commemorates observer Uji Kintaro, who in 1967 fed Kin, Japan's last wild-born crested ibis.

sights.name: Anju Mound (Hatano)
sights.description: Mound in Hatano, Sado, said to stand where Anju’s comb and relics were buried, long revered for harvest, matchmaking and eye-healing prayers.

sights.name: Kohie Shrine Main Hall and Torii
sights.name_en: Kohie Shrine Main Hall and Torii
sights.name_ja: 小比叡神社 本殿・鳥居
sights.description: The 1640 main hall and stone Myojin torii of Kohie Shrine, once the guardian shrine of Rengehoji Temple on Sado.

sights.name: Tsugami Island
sights.description: Island off the Okawa settlement on eastern Sado, overlooked from Mikaeri Pass, with a vermilion Tsugami Bridge and Tsugami Shrine relocated there in 1791.

sights.name: Kasuga Shrine Noh Stage (Aikawa)
sights.description: Noh stage at Kasuga Shrine in Aikawa, Sado, said to be where Noh on the island began; firelight Noh is held several times a year.

sights.name: Mumyoi Ware Pottery Experience
sights.name_ja: 佐渡金山で発見された赤土を使った焼き物「無名異焼（伝統的工芸品）」を作ろう！
sights.description: Make Mumyoi ware, Sado's traditional pottery, from iron-oxide clay found at Sado Gold Mine under a local potter's guidance.

sights.name: Toki Guide Request Form
sights.name_ja: トキガイド手配依頼フォーム
sights.description: Form to arrange certified guides who explain crested ibis watching points, etiquette, and reintroduction efforts during early-morning or daytime drives through Kuninaka.

sights.name: Nagae Atsukushihiko Shrine Noh Stage
sights.name_ja: 長江熱串彦神社能舞台
sights.description: Thatched Noh stage at Atsukushihiko Shrine in Nagae, one of the few pre-modern Noh stages on Sado and a city cultural property.

sights.name: Primeval Forest Trekking - Sotokaifu Route
sights.name_ja: 原生林トレッキング～外海府ルート～
sights.description: A specialist-guided trek to giant cedars centered on Kongo Cedar, introduced at the 2008 Toyako Summit, with entry limited to 16 people a day.

sights.name: Yorokuro Cherry of Kitakoura
sights.description: A giant warm-region mountain cherry on a seaside hill, the northern limit of its type on the Sea of Japan side, standing 25 metres tall.

sights.name: Nashinoki Jizo
sights.description: Jizo hall at Nashinoki Pass on the old Mano–Akadomari road, surrounded by small stone Jizo said to number in the thousands.

sights.name: Jinnobi Cafe & Restaurant
sights.description: Cafe and restaurant in Mano, Sado, where locals and travelers enjoy food, drinks, and open views at a relaxed island pace.

sights.name: Meiji Memorial Hall
sights.description: Memorial hall completed in 1902 to commemorate over 40 Sado-born soldiers killed in the Sino-Japanese War, also enshrining later war dead, with a Russian sailors' grave on site.

sights.name: Kusakari Shrine Noh Stage
sights.description: A thatched Noh stage at Kusakari Shrine where performances have been recorded since 1863 and torchlight Noh is held each June 15.

sights.name: Great Ginkgo of Seisuiji Temple
sights.description: A 26-metre ginkgo with an 8.18-metre trunk girth stands at the gate-front residence of Seisuiji Temple, modeled on Kyoto's Kiyomizu-dera.

stays.name: Kohan no Yado Yoshida-ya
stays.name_ja: 湖畔の宿 吉田家
stays.description: Inn at Sadokamomizumi Onsen in Ryotsuebisu, Sado with lakeside location.

stays.name: Koukian Euphoria
stays.name_ja: 香季庵Euphoria
stays.description: Accommodation in Sado, Niigata.

stays.name: Hotel Mancho
stays.name_ja: 伝統と風格の宿 ホテル万長
stays.description: Hotel in Aikawageko, Sado with open-air baths.

stays.name: Tabino Hotel Sado Annex
stays.name_ja: たびのホテル佐渡Annex
stays.description: Hotel in Sado, Niigata.

stays.name: Hotel Oosado
stays.name_ja: HOTEL OOSADO(ホテル大佐渡)
stays.description: Hotel in Sado, Niigata.

stays.name: HOTEL AZUMA
stays.description: Inn in Aikawaora, Sado with open-air baths and scenic views.

stays.name: Kara Furu
stays.name_ja: カラふる
stays.description: Inn in Matsugasaki, Sado with open-air baths and a renovated traditional house.

stays.name: Tabino Hotel Sado
stays.name_ja: たびのホテル佐渡
stays.description: Hotel in Sado, Niigata.

stays.name: Kanai Seiyo-kan
stays.name_ja: 金井西洋館
stays.description: Inn in Kanaishinbootsu, Sado with a renovated traditional house.

stays.name: Yado-ya Fukuro
stays.name_ja: 宿屋ふくろう
stays.description: Inn in Chukokabuto, Sado with business travelers.

stays.name: Guesthouse Kimama
stays.name_ja: ゲストハウスきまま
stays.description: Guesthouse in Izumikabuto, Sado with pet-friendly rooms.

stays.name: Sado Kominka Stay Sadomari Izumi no Ie
stays.name_en: Sado Kominka Stay Sadomari Izumi no Ie
stays.name_ja: 佐渡古民家ステイ さどまり 泉の家
stays.description: Inn in Izumikabuto, Sado with a renovated traditional house.

stays.name: Guest House UZU Sado
stays.name_ja: ゲストハウスＵＺＵ佐渡
stays.description: Guest house in Kaizuka, Sado.

stays.name: Iseya Shinkan
stays.name_ja: いせや新館
stays.description: Private rental inn in Nakahara, Sado, with pets allowed.

stays.name: Shima no Hotel
stays.name_ja: 島のホテル
stays.description: Small hotel in Nakahara, Sado, opened in April 2023, with a bath and toilet in every room.

stays.name: Goen no Yado Itoya
stays.name_ja: ご縁の宿 伊藤屋
stays.description: Ryokan in Mano Shinmachi, Sado, with Sado beef steak, seasonal seafood, and homemade sweets.

stays.name: Pension Nagakura
stays.name_ja: ペンション 永倉
stays.description: Pension in Mano, Sado, with a Western-style twin room.

stays.name: AKIYATO Active Art Hotel
stays.description: Hotel in Katabata, Sado, with art-viewing rooms and a garden for the four seasons.

stays.name: Fureai Hausu Ushiozu no Sato
stays.name_ja: ふれあいハウス潮津の里
stays.description: House in Seai, Sado, with a maifan-stone artificial hot-spring bath and bay sunset views.

stays.name: Yuhi to Mizuumi no Yado Aokiya
stays.name_en: Yuhi to Mizuumi no Yado Aokiya
stays.name_ja: 夕日と湖の宿 あおきや
stays.description: Inn in Harakuro, Sado.

stays.name: Hotel New Katsura
stays.name_ja: ホテルニュー桂
stays.description: Lakeside hotel in Harakuro, Sado, with a natural hot spring, five minutes by car from Ryotsu Port.

stays.name: Toki Densetsu to Rotenburo no Yado Kiraku
stays.name_en: Toki Densetsu to Rotenburo no Yado Kiraku
stays.name_ja: 朱鷺伝説と露天風呂の宿きらく
stays.description: Hillside inn by Lake Kamo in Haraguro, Sado, with an open-air bath and views of the lake, Osado mountains, and town.

stays.name: Guest House Jinku
stays.name_ja: ゲストハウスじんく

sights.name: Tsubame-Sanjo Factory Festival 2026
sights.name_ja: 燕三条 工場の祭典2026
sights.description: Open-factory event in Tsubame-Sanjo where 108 metalworking factories and companies usually closed to the public offer tours and activities.

sights.name: KYOWA Classic Car & Life Station
sights.name_ja: KYOWA クラシックカー＆ライフステーション
sights.description: Retro facility in Sanjo displaying Showa-era domestic classic cars and motorcycles, with some test rides and a historical corner of period appliances and household goods.

sights.name: Nakaura Himesayuri Forest Park
sights.name_ja: 中浦ヒメサユリ森林公園
sights.description: Forest park campground with 80 lawn auto campsites, five bungalows, a fishing pond, and an athletic course on 28 hectares.

sights.name: Yagigahana Cliff
sights.description: A quartz-trachyte cliff over 200 meters high on the upper Ikarashi River, a prefectural natural monument and peregrine falcon breeding site.

sights.name: Honjoji Temple
sights.name_ja: 法華宗総本山 本成寺
sights.description: Head temple of the Hokke sect, founded in 1297 by priest Nichin, with carvings by late-Edo sculptor Ishikawa Uncho and his grave on site.

sights.name: Sanjo Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Sanjo whose grounds include Kanayama Shrine for the metalwork deity and adjoin Hachiman Park, with festivals through the year.

sights.name: Sanjo Blacksmithing Dojo
sights.description: Sanjo workshop offering courses in traditional blacksmithing, woodworking, and Buddhist altar making, including forging lessons by active blacksmiths.

sights.name: Tsubame-Sanjo Jibasan Summer Fair 2026
sights.name_ja: 燕三条じばさんサマーフェア2026
sights.description: Nine-day summer fair in Tsubame-Sanjo with maker demos, craft workshops, food stalls, and a century-old nail-clipper display.

sights.name: Kita-Iogawa Rice Terraces
sights.description: Terraced rice fields at the foot of Mount Awagatake in Sanjo, selected among Japan's 100 terraced rice fields, with mountain views and late-April dogtooth violets.

sights.name: Shirasagi Forest Park
sights.description: A forest park in Sanjo where Genji and Heike fireflies fly over about 20,000 Japanese irises on early summer nights.

sights.name: Ichinokido Shinmei Shrine
sights.description: Shrine whose grounds are illuminated by 300 lanterns from December 30 to January 3, and where Sanjo Kagura is performed on November 14.

sights.name: Suwada Factory
sights.name_ja: 株式会社 諏訪田製作所
sights.description: Century-old blade smithy where craftsmen hand-make nail clippers and bonsai shears, with factory tours available.

sights.name: Snow Peak Headquarters Campfield
sights.name_ja: スノーピークヘッドクォーターズキャンプフィールド
sights.description: Campground beside Snow Peak headquarters in Sanjo, with free sites on natural terrain, gear rentals, and staff support.

sights.name: Isurugi Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Sanjo, Niigata.

sights.name: Hakucho no Sato Park
sights.description: Tundra swans arrive on the Ikarashi River from early November, with up to about 400 birds visible from an observation building morning and evening.

sights.name: Tsubame-Sanjo Wing
sights.description: Information and sales space in the JR Tsubame-Sanjo Station concourse, presenting local tourism and industry and selling products made in the area.

sights.name: Sanjo City History, Folklore and Industry Museum
sights.name_en: Sanjo City History, Folklore and Industry Museum
sights.name_ja: 三条市歴史民俗産業資料館
sights.description: Museum showing Paleolithic and Jomon finds, old documents, festival tools and Showa-era goods; its building is a registered national tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Maoigaike Pond
sights.name_ja: 雨生ヶ池（まおいがいけ）
sights.description: A 2-hectare pond in remote Yoshigahira, ringed by primeval beech forest and linked to a giant-snake legend marked by an August festival.

sights.name: Snow Peak FIELD SUITE SPA HEADQUARTERS
sights.name_en: Snow Peak FIELD SUITE SPA HEADQUARTERS
sights.description: A nature-oriented bath, dining and lodging resort in Sanjo offering day-use bathing, with a sauna and outdoor cooling area overlooking Mt. Awagatake.

sights.name: Honda CBX400F Classic Bike Rental, 6-Hour Course (Spring–Autumn)
sights.name_en: Honda CBX400F Classic Bike Rental, 6-Hour Course (Spring–Autumn)
sights.name_ja: ホンダCBX400F クラシックバイクレンタル 6時間コース（春～秋）
sights.description: A six-hour Honda CBX400F rental for touring from Tsubame-Sanjo along the Teradomari coast or to Yahiko Onsen.

sights.name: Mount Awagatake
sights.description: A 1,293 m mountain spanning Sanjo and Kamo; the summit takes about four hours and offers views toward Sado and Noto on clear days.

sights.name: Green Sports Center Campground
sights.name_ja: グリーンスポーツセンター
sights.description: Campground on Eimeiji Mountain, also called Osaki Mountain, with over 20 dirt tent sites among greenery for campfires and tent stays.

sights.name: Koshoji Temple
sights.description: Koshoji Temple is a Soto Zen temple about 400 years old, where about 1,400 hydrangeas of 300 varieties bloom from mid-June to early July.

sights.name: Honda S800 Classic Car Rental (6-Hour Course, Spring to Autumn)
sights.name_en: Honda S800 Classic Car Rental (6-Hour Course, Spring to Autumn)
sights.name_ja: ホンダS800 クラシックカーレンタル 6時間コース(春～秋)
sights.description: Six-hour rental of a 1966 Honda S800 open sports car from Tsubame-Sanjo, with drives along the Teradomari coast and a visit to Yahiko Onsen.

sights.name: Green Sports Center and Osakiyama Park
sights.name_en: Green Sports Center and Osakiyama Park
sights.name_ja: グリーンスポーツセンター・大崎山公園
sights.description: Nature park centered on a green sports center, with campsites, tennis courts, and a summit lookout over the city and Mt. Yahiko.

sights.name: Nozaki Manufacturing (Mini Cart Making)
sights.name_ja: 株式会社 野崎製作所
sights.description: A metalworking company founded in 1902 that produces agricultural machinery parts and architectural hardware, where visitors can make a mini cart using a press machine in about one hour.

sights.name: Sanjo Curry Ramen
sights.description: Local curry ramen in Sanjo, served at over 70 shops as curry soup or as ramen topped with curry.

sights.name: Otani Dam
sights.description: A stacked-stone rockfill multipurpose dam near Hayabusa Plaza and a visitor museum, with mountain autumn foliage and an area of 101 hectares.

sights.name: Honai Park
sights.description: Park in Sanjo with a tropical plant greenhouse, a Japanese garden, and a fountain that forms six shapes.

sights.name: Hachijurigoe Experience Bus Tour
sights.name_ja: 秘境八十里越体感バスツアー
sights.description: A bus tour views National Route 289 construction at Hachijurigoe, reconnecting Aizu and Echigo, plus local nature and Kawai Tsugunosuke history.

sights.name: Yoshigahira Nature Experience Village
sights.description: A nature area in Sanjo with a campground, a fishing pond, and a prefecture-designated spring, plus beech-forest trekking in autumn.

sights.name: Watanabe Orchard
sights.description: Orchard in Sanjo, about 100 years old, that grows pears and grapes while playing classical music and offers drive-through sales at harvest.

sights.name: Shirasagi-so (Hot Spring)
sights.description: Hot spring facility in Sanjo's Yata district, with a telescope, a large hall, Japanese rooms, and a cold mineral spring rich in metasilicic acid.

sights.name: Awagadake Kita-Iokawa Trailhead
sights.name_ja: 粟ケ岳・北五百川登山口
sights.description: Kita-Iokawa trailhead for 1,292 m Awagadake, spanning Sanjo and Kamo, with views of Asakusadake and Sumondake; the hut is closed after a roof collapse.

sights.name: Nozaki Factory (Kick Scooter Making)
sights.name_ja: 親子で楽しくおもちゃ作り！キックスケーター（1台）
sights.description: Build a two- or three-wheel kick scooter from parts on factory machines, with craftsman support, and take it home to ride the same day.

sights.name: Kasabori Dam
sights.description: A multipurpose dam for flood control, power generation and irrigation, near a Japanese serow reserve in Okuhayade Kurisumon Prefectural Natural Park (63 hectares, 207 meters).

sights.name: Mount Sumon
sights.description: A peak of about 1,537 metres in Sanjo, reached by a trail of about six hours from Yoshigahira, open from June to November.

sights.name: Factory Tour and Mini Cart Making
sights.name_en: Factory Tour and Mini Cart Making
sights.name_ja: プロに学び、本物の機械に触れる！工場見学＆ミニ台車づくり
sights.description: A small-group workshop in Sanjo where visitors make mini carts on professional press machines with one-on-one craftsman support and take them home the same day.

sights.name: BLASTMAN
sights.description: Warehouse store in Sanjo selling overseas vintage furniture and DULTON goods, with an American-style diner serving T-bone steak and spare ribs.
